items.text: Lead your household in serving the Lord, as Joshua did, and do not neglect this duty because of public office.
items.quote: he and his house would serue the Lord.

items.text: Rule your own house well, for he who cannot rule his own house is not fit to govern the church.
items.quote: a Bishop that cannot rule his own house, is not fit to gouerne the Church.

items.text: Do not be indulgent or negligent toward your children, but exercise proper restraint and governance, lest they become headstrong.
items.quote: through the too-much-indulgencie and negligence of their parents, and partly through their owne headstrong affections, and rebellious will, runne without restraint

items.text: Obey your parents in the Lord and do what they command, for that is your whole calling.
items.quote: their whole calling is to be obedient to their parents... and to doe what they command them in the Lord.

items.text: Obey your master in the Lord and do what he commands, and be faithful in your service, as Joseph was to Potiphar.
items.quote: their whole calling is to be obedient to their parents and masters, and to doe what they command them in the Lord.

items.text: Oversee the care of your house yourself; do not shift it all to wife or servant, nor waste your time in idleness.
items.quote: masters of families who commit all the care of their house either to their wiues, or to some seruant, and mispend their whole time in idlenesse

items.text: Manage the household diligently; do not spend your days in bed, attire, and gossiping.
items.quote: many mistresses, who spend their time in lying a bed, attiring themselues, and goshipping.

items.text: Do not neglect your wife, but perform the duties of a husband.
items.quote: he may not neglect his wife, children, and seruants.

items.text: Do not neglect your children, but perform the duties of a father.
items.quote: he may not neglect his wife, children, and seruants.

items.text: Do not neglect your servants, but perform the duties of a master.
items.quote: he may not neglect his wife, children, and seruants.

items.text: Perform your household duties conscientiously, for the good ordering of church and commonwealth.
items.quote: a conscionable performance of domesticall and houshold duties, tend to the good ordering of Church and commonwealth

items.text: Learn subjection in the family, for if you cannot be subject in a family, you will hardly be subject in church or commonwealth.
items.quote: inferiours that cannot be subiect in a familie; they will hardly be brought to yeeld such subiection as they ought in Church or commonwealth

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 61 · Of well vsing naturall affection. … Of haters of others.

items.text: Love her as your own flesh: nourish and cherish her, and do not hate her.
items.quote: For no man euer yet hated his owne flesh: but nourisheth and cherisheth it.

items.text: Love one another and do not hate; your brother or kinsman is your own flesh.
items.quote: our brother or neighbour is Our flesh.

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 98 · Of aiming at our owne, in seeking the good of others. … Of preferring honestie before commoditie.

items.text: Obey your parents in the Lord, seeking first God's honor and their good, not your own benefit as the chief end.
items.quote: the three former have respect to God, and to that good conscience which children ought to carrie towards him: the first pointeth at Gods image which parents carie (in the Lord:)

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 1 · Of those who may seeke to be maried. … Of ripenesse of yeares in them that are to be maried.

items.text: Do not make matches for your children or cause them to be married before they are of ripe years; such marriages are mock-marriages and nullities.
items.quote: such parents... make matches for them in their child-hood, and cause them to be maried: such mariages are mock-mariages, and meere nullities.

items.text: Take care for the marriage of your children when they pass the flower of their age.
items.quote: parents to take care for the mariage of their children... if they passe the floure of their age

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 57 · Of naturall selfe-loue. … Of the error of Stoicks in condemning all passion.

items.text: Care for your children; let natural affection make you do for them.
items.quote: Admirably much is that which parents doe for their children, which they would neuer doe, if there were not a naturall affection in them to their children.

items.text: Support your parents in their old age, impotence, or any need, giving them succour.
items.quote: From children againe this affection ariseth towards their parents, that when parents grow old, impotent, or any way vnable to helpe themselues, they might haue succour from their children.

items.text: Let the marriage bond raise natural affection between you, so that you care for one another.
items.quote: by vertue of that bond raised a naturall affection not only in husband and wife one to another

items.text: Care for your kindred — brothers, cousins, and all your kin — as for yourself.
items.quote: God hath yet further extended this naturall affection to brethren, cousins, and other kindred.

items.text: Seek the spiritual good of your family as your own, for spiritual love should extend to them.
items.quote: This spirituall affection extendeth it selfe as farre as, naturall affection, namely to wiues, husbands, children, parents, brethren, cosins, friends, &c.

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 86 · Of Christs leauing his Father and mother for his spouse. … Of the equall priuiledge of all the Saints.

items.text: Love Christ above them; do not let affection for parents swallow up your love for him.
items.quote: This then is our dutie, that we suffer not any naturall affection and dotage on our parents to swallow vp that loue we owe to Christ.

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 127 · Of the meaning of the eight verse. … Of the connexion of masters duties with seruants.

items.text: Perform faithful service to your master as a good work, knowing God will reward you.
items.quote: Faithfull seruice performed to men is a good thing

items.text: Provide them competent food, clothing, and lodging, and do not repay their service with frowns, checks, or blows.
items.quote: not affording competent food, clothing, lodging, but frownes, checkes, and blowes

items.text: Do not threaten them, but rule gently, remembering that you have a Master in heaven.
items.quote: forbearing threatning

items.text: Give them what is just and equal, for they labour for you and God sees all.
items.quote: giue vnto your seruants that which is iust and equall

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 126 · Of the meaning of the seuenth verse.

items.text: Serve your master with good will, ready and cheerful, doing it with a good mind.
items.quote: A readinesse and cheerefulnesse in doing a thing; a doing it with a good minde.

items.text: Desire and endeavor that your master may reap profit and benefit by your service.
items.quote: A desire and endeuour that their masters may reape profit and benefit by their seruice.

items.text: Serve your master as to the Lord, not to men only; serve men for the Lord's sake.
items.quote: Looke not so much to men and their reward, as to God and his reward: serue men in and for the Lord, euen as if you serued God.

items.text: In serving your master, cast an eye upon God for his approval and reward.
items.quote: An eie is to be cast vpon God euen in those duties which we performe to men: and that both for approbation and reward from God.

items.text: Recognize that a servant's place is more abject and inferior than that of a wife or child; do not look for their privileges.
items.quote: Though wiues and children be inferiours as well as seruants, yet may not seruants looke for such priuiledges as they haue. Another manner of subiection must be performed by seruants.

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 96 · Of the meaning of the first verse of the sixt Chapter.

items.text: Obey your parents in the Lord, hearkening to their commands, reproofs, directions, and exhortations with humble submission and reverent respect.
items.quote: Children obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.

items.text: Honor your father and mother, and be not ashamed of them whatever their estate—rich or poor, learned or unlearned.
items.quote: if they be parents to children, they must be honoured by children

items.text: Honor and obey your grandparents, as those in the place of parents.
items.quote: there is an honour and a subiection due by all who are in place of children, to all such as are in place of parents

items.text: Honor and obey your parents-in-law, as those in the place of parents.
items.quote: there is an honour and a subiection due by all who are in place of children, to all such as are in place of parents

items.text: Honor and obey your guardian, as one in the place of a parent.
items.quote: there is an honour and a subiection due by all who are in place of children, to all such as are in place of parents

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 115 · Of the connexion of Parents dutie with Childrens. … Of the extent of these words, Fathers, Children.

items.text: Do not provoke them to wrath, but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
items.quote: prouoke not your children to wrath: but bring them vp in the nurture and admonition of the Lord

items.text: Carry yourself worthy of honor and be an example to them in performing your own duty, lest your ill example make them negligent.
items.quote: as ye looke for dutie from your children, performe dutie to them

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 120 · Of parents fixing precepts in their childrens mindes. … Of the subiection which beleeuing seruants owe.

items.text: Keep your children under by good discipline, so that they learn dutiful subjection.
items.quote: by discipline keepe their children vnder

items.text: Teach your children their duty to God, and diligently fix His precepts in their minds.
items.quote: Parents must especially teach their children their dutie to God.

items.text: Be subject to your master as master, whatever his disposition, whether he believes or not.
items.quote: subiection wherein they are bound to their masters, as masters, whatsoeuer their disposition were.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 9 · Of equalitie in yeeres betwixt husband and wife.

items.text: Seek a spouse somewhat answerable in age.
items.quote: there should be some equalitie betwixt the parties that are maried in Age

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 67 · Of contentment in that which is sufficient. … Of Christs forbearing to hate the Church.

items.text: Provide her with food and apparel, and be content with that sufficiency, not seeking extravagant excess.
items.quote: Hauing food and raiment, we must be therewith content.

items.text: Do not hate her, but love, nourish and cherish her, as Christ loves the church.
items.quote: The Lord hateth not his Church. And the Lord nourisheth and cherisheth his Church.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 6 · Of the lawfulnesse of mariage to all sorts of persons.

items.text: Have your own wife only, and not another's, to avoid fornication.
items.quote: to auoid fornication let euery man haue his owne wife, and let euerie woman haue her owne husband.

items.text: Have your own husband only, and not another's, to avoid fornication.
items.quote: to auoid fornication let euery man haue his owne wife, and let euerie woman haue her owne husband.

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 80 · Of preferring husband or wife before parents. … Of Polygamy and Bigamy.

items.text: Prefer your wife before your parents.
items.quote: A wife, or an husband must be preferred before parents.

items.text: Prefer your husband before your parents.
items.quote: A wife, or an husband must be preferred before parents.

items.text: Do not keep your married children so under subjection that they cannot freely perform duty to their spouse.
items.quote: keepe them, euen after they are maried, so strait vnder subiection, as they cannot freely performe such duty as they ought to their husband, or their wife

items.text: Do not keep your married children from their spouse.
items.quote: keepe their children from their husbands, or from their wiues.

items.text: Do not give so to your parents that your wife lacks necessaries, and do not vex her to please them.
items.quote: keepe their wiues very bare, suffering them to want necessaries

items.text: Do not secretly take from your husband to give to your parents.
items.quote: priuily purloine from their husbands to bestow on their parents.

items.text: Live together continually.
items.quote: associate themselues together by continuall cohabitation

items.text: Keep the marriage bond unbroken until death parts you.
items.quote: It must neuer be cut asunder till death cut it.

items.text: Have only one wife; do not commit polygamy.
items.quote: Mariage can be but betwixt two, one man, and one woman.

items.text: Have only one husband; do not have more than one husband.
items.quote: our lawes haue iustly made it felony for a man to haue more wiues then one, or a woman more husbands.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 4 · Of matrimoniall Chastitie. … Of Adulterie.

items.text: Be chaste with her: keep your body from being defiled with strange flesh, and be satisfied at all times in her and ravished with her love.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part 2, Section 4
items.quote: Let euerie man haue his OWNE wife

items.text: Be chaste with him: keep your body from being defiled with strange flesh, and be satisfied at all times in him and ravished with his love.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part 2, Section 4
items.quote: Let euerie woman haue her OWNE husband

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 107 · Of appropriating prosperity and long-life to the obedience which children yeeld to their parents. … Of Gods ordering his fauours so as they may appeare to be true blessings.

items.text: Obey your parents, as this is a sure evidence of your conformity to God's whole law and a means to your own well-being.
items.quote: obedience to parents is one of the surest euidences of our conformity to the whole law

items.text: Ask your parents' blessing, recognizing that their prayers have great power with God.
items.quote: the custome of childrens asking their parents blessing

items.text: Bless your children, for the faithful prayer of a parent is of great force with God for a dutiful child.
items.quote: of parents blessing their children

items.text: Seek provident care for your children's welfare and long life, as Naomi said, 'Shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?'
items.quote: by their prouident care, as Noami said to Ruth, shall I not seeke rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?

items.text: Pray earnestly for your children, for the faithful prayer of parents is of great force with God.
items.quote: by their instant praier: for the faithfull praier of parents is of great force with God for dutifull children

items.text: Do not be overly indulgent toward your children, lest God punish both you and them.
items.quote: when parents are too indulgent ouer their children, God doth punish the sinne both of parent and childe

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 79 · Of the ancient Law of mariage.

items.text: Leave your father and mother, and be joined to your wife; give her priority over your parents in your daily care and affection.
items.quote: For this cause shall a man leaue his father and mother, and shall be ioyned vnto his wife

items.text: As your husband cleaves to you, cleave to him; be as firm to him as to yourself.
items.quote: if a man must inseparably cleaue to his wife, the wife must answerably cleaue to her husband

items.text: Treat your spouse as your own flesh; be as close as parts of the same body.
items.quote: they two shall be one flesh

items.text: Do not utterly forsake your parents when you marry; continue to honor and care for them, though your daily attendance now belongs to your spouse.
items.quote: neither generally to be taken of all duties, as if no dutie were to be performed to parents by children after they are maried

items.text: While you are under your parents' government, perform daily service to them, seeking to please them in all things.
items.quote: of that daily seruice which children vnder their parents gouernment performe vnto them, seeking to please them in all things

items.text: In any unavoidable conflict between your wife and your parents, cleave to your wife.
items.quote: by this Law he must leaue his parent, and cleaue to his wife.

items.text: Dwell together; do not live apart.
items.quote: the husband and wife must dwell each with other

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 117 · Of parents prouoking children. … Of parents nurturing their children.

items.text: Do not provoke them to wrath; avoid too much austerity, sourness, threatening, reviling, hard handling, severe correction, restraint, or small allowance.
items.quote: prouoke not your children to wrath; avoid too much austeritie, sowrenesse, threatning, reuiling, too hard handling, too seuere correction, too much restraint, too small allowance.

items.text: Watch over your own behavior, that you make not your child to sin.
items.quote: Parents must be so watchfull ouer their cariage, as thereby they make not their children to sinne.

items.text: Provide all needful things for them, even such as nourish their bodies and preserve health and life.
items.quote: Parents ought to prouide all needfull things for their children: euen such things as tend to the nourishing of their bodies, and preseruing of their health and life.

items.text: Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord: instruct and correct them as befits a child.
items.quote: Bring them vp in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

items.text: Do not only prevent mischief, but actively seek their good in all things.
items.quote: It is not sufficient for parents to preuent such mischiefes as children may fall into, but they must also seeke their good.

items.text: Be neither too austere nor too remiss, but keep a mean discipline befitting a child.
items.quote: They must not prouoke their children to wrath, yet they must keepe them vnder discipline.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 26 · Of the mysterie of Mariage. … Of celebrating mariage with sorrow.

items.text: Love one another entirely and intimately, as Christ loves his church.
items.quote: man and wife who intirely, as they ought, loue one another

items.text: Do not marry without the consent of your parents or those who have authority over you.
items.quote: mariages without parents, or other gouernours and friends consent

items.text: Do not force your child into marriage; give your consent only when the marriage is lawful and fitting.
items.quote: forced, stolne, vnequall, or any other way vnlawfull mariages

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 18 · Of the distance of time betwixt the contract and mariage. … Of a religious consecrating of mariage.

items.text: After your contract, keep your body only for your espoused; you no longer have power over your own body.
items.citation: Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part I, Section 18
items.quote: after the contract is made, neither the man nor the woman haue the power of their owne body.

items.text: Do not absent yourself long from your espoused after the contract, lest you alienate their heart.
items.citation: Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part I, Section 18
items.quote: to be affianced and made sure to a wife, and then to trauell beyond sea... be absent from their spouse a yeere, or two, or three... This may be a meanes to alienate the heart of his spouse from him for euer.

items.text: If you must delay the wedding, do not put it off too long, and do it only with the mutual and joint consent of both parties.
items.citation: Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part I, Section 18
items.quote: so may others haue occasions to put off their mariages: which may be lawfull, so the mariage be not put off too long, and that there be a mutuall and ioynt consent of both parties.

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 131 · Of masters subiection to a greater master. … Of Gods being in heauen.

items.text: Treat your servant as a fellow servant of Christ, remembering that you both have one Master in heaven, and so do not rule over him with harshness or oppression.
items.quote: Masters and seruants are in the same subiection, and vnder a like command. There is one master, euen Christ: and all men whosoeuer are brethren, fellow-seruants.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 23 · Of the honour of mariage in regard of the first institution thereof. … Of the Priuileges of mariage.

items.text: Be a mutual help to one another in all things needful for soul and body, in prosperity and adversity, in health and sickness.
items.quote: man and wife might be a mutuall helpe one to another

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 14 · Of a contract what it is? … Of the grounds of a contract.

items.text: Take her as your espoused wife and faithfully promise, before sufficient witnesses, to marry her in time meet and convenient.
items.quote: I A. take thee B. to my espoused wife, and doe faithfully promise to marie thee in time meet and conuenient.

items.text: Take him as your espoused husband and faithfully promise, before sufficient witnesses, to yield to be married to him in time meet and convenient.
items.quote: I B. take thee A. to my espoused husband, and doe faithfully promise to yeeld to be maried to thee in time meet and conuenient.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 18 · Of husbands and wiues mutuall prayers. … Of the things for which husbands and wiues are to pray alone.

items.text: Pray for each other and with each other for all needful blessings of soul, body, name, and goods.
items.quote: prayer is a mutuall dutie which one oweth to the other

items.text: Lead her in prayer; be her mouth to God when you pray together.
items.quote: the husband, who is as a Priest vnto his wife, and ought to be her mouth to God

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 16 · Of the reasons which shew how requisite a contract is. … Of abusing, or neglecting a contract.

items.text: Pray for one another once you are contracted, that God would bless you to live together happily.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part 1, Section 16
items.quote: after the contract is made, they may simply and absolutely pray each for other

items.text: Prepare yourselves before marriage to perform the duties God's word requires of husband and wife, and to bear crosses patiently.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part 1, Section 16
items.quote: it is a meanes to make them before hand prepare themselues to perfome such mariage duties as Gods word requireth

items.text: Keep yourselves pure and do not come together sexually until the marriage is solemnized; the betrothed woman remains a virgin.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part 1, Section 16
items.quote: she ought to keepe her selfe a virgin till the mariage be consummate

items.text: If you know a lawful impediment to the marriage, disclose it once a contract is published; do not conceal it.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part 1, Section 16
items.quote: after they haue notice therof, they will not forbeare to disclose what they know.

items.text: Make a legal contract before the wedding so that no one can secretly carry off your daughter or ward before the appointed day.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part 1, Section 16
items.quote: preuent many plots and practises of inueigling, or stealing away maids and widowes
items.needs_role: parents or guardians (to daughter or ward)

items.text: Do not neglect to make a contract before marriage; it is a warrantable and honourable proceeding.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Part 1, Section 16
items.quote: Few there be in comparison of the multitudes that are maried, who make any conscience thereof. They thinke it needlesse, and vtterly neglect it.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 3 · Of impotent persons that ought not to seeke after mariage. … Of that ineuitable danger which hindereth mariage.

items.text: If you are impotent, do not seek to marry, for God by that sign shows he calls you to live single.
items.quote: They ought not to seeke after mariage: for by those signes of impotencie God sheweth that he calleth them to liue single.

items.text: Before entering marriage, disclose any impotence, for concealing it wrongs the person you marry and frustrates procreation.
items.quote: who conceale their impotencie and ioyne themselues in marriage, whereby they frustrate one maine end of mariage, which is procreation of children

items.text: If you have a contagious disease, do not seek to marry, for it endangers your intended spouse.
items.quote: They who are infected with such contagious diseases... ought not to seeke after mariage: for that cannot but turne to the danger of the partie with whom they marie.

items.text: Before entering marriage, disclose any contagious disease, for concealing it causes unanswerable prejudice to the person you marry.
items.quote: Contrarie to the end and vse of mariage doe they sinne, who conceale such diseases, and so ioyne themselues in mariage, to the vnanswerable preiudice of the partie whom they marrie.

items.text: Do not dissolve the marriage because your wife is barren; the bond is inviolable even if you have no children.
items.quote: so inuiolable is the mariage bond, that though it be made for childrens sake, yet for want of children it may not be broken.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 6 · Of pardoning adulterie vpon repentance. … Of the difference of adultery in a man, and in a wife.

items.text: Forgive a repentant adulterous spouse if you choose to continue the marriage; you may do so without sin.
items.quote: they may so doe, if they will, and that without iust exception to the contrarie, they ought so to doe.

items.text: Keep yourself only to your spouse; adultery is equally the sin of the husband and the wife.
items.quote: the sinne of either partie is alike. Gods word maketh no disparity betwixt them.

items.text: Do not withhold conjugal dues except by mutual consent and for a time.
items.quote: Their power also ouer one another in this respect is alike. If on iust occasion they abstaine, it must be with mutuall consent.

items.text: Excel in virtue and govern your wife by example; do not claim a double standard that excuses your adultery.
items.quote: it is meet that adulterous husbands be so much the more seuerely punished, by how much the more it appertaineth to them to excell in vertue, and to gouerne their wiues by example.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 37 · Of the vices contrarie to that mutuallcare, which man and wife should haue of one anothers credit.

items.text: Conceal and cover one another's infirmities and imperfections; do not blaze them abroad to others.
items.quote: they are most bound to conceale and couer each others imperfections.

items.text: Do not open your ears or give credit to every light report that any shall raise against your spouse.
items.quote: By opening their eares, and giuing credit to euery light report that any shall raise.

items.text: Do not pervert or misinterpret your spouse's actions, words, or thoughts, taking everything in the worst part.
items.quote: By peruerting and mis-interpreting one anothers actions, words, yea and thoughts also: taking euery thing in the worst part.

items.text: Disclose to one another the common evil rumors which are raised of them, for bedfellows are most fit and most bound to do it.
items.quote: bedfellowes are most fit to disclose such things one to another: and most bound to doe it.

items.text: Do not envy one another at the good report that is made of the other, nor gainsay it.
items.quote: by enuying one at the good report that is made of the other, and gainsaying the same

items.text: Be affected with reports that go of your spouse, and have a mutual care for one another's fame, not neglecting it as strangers.
items.quote: a carelesse regard, or plaine neglect of one anothers fame: when the husband is no way affected with any report that goeth of his wife, nor the wife with any of the husband

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 7 · Of the things which are absolutely necessarie to make a person fit for mariage.

items.text: Marry only outside the degrees of consanguinity and affinity which God's law forbids.
items.quote: one beyond those degrees of consanguinitie and affinitie which are forbidden by the law of God

items.text: Keep yourself only to the one to whom you are married or betrothed; do not take another.
items.quote: One that is free: nor maried, nor betrothed to another

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 8 · Of the hainousnesse of Adulterie.

items.text: Maintain your affection for your spouse as the most inviolable of all relationships; do not let adultery alienate it.
items.quote: husbands and wiues affection (which of all other ought to be the most inuiolable) is so alienated

items.text: Provide for your household and do not waste your goods on a paramour.
items.quote: the adulterous husband spending that wherewith he should prouide for his family, on his harlot

items.text: Do not steal from your husband.
items.quote: the adulterous wife purloining what she can from her husband

items.text: Never wish for or plot your spouse's death.
items.quote: husbands and wiues are stirred vp to wish, and long after one anothers death

items.text: Avoid adultery, lest you brand your children with infamy and deprive them of privileges.
items.quote: children borne in adulterie (whom they brand with an indelible character of infamie, and depriue of many priuiledges that otherwise they might enioy)

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 14 · Of husbands and wiues dwelling together. … Of the respects for which man and wife may for a time liue asunder.

items.text: Dwell with your wife; do not leave her.
items.quote: Saint Peter expresly chargeth husbands to dwell with their wiues

items.text: Leave your father's house and live with your husband.
items.quote: Iaakobs wiues to leaue their fathers house, and goe with their husband.

items.text: Do not desert one another; live together even if one is an unbeliever.
items.quote: not to leaue one another, but to dwell together, yea though the one be an infidell.

items.text: If one is confined or banished and the other can come, the free one must go if asked.
items.quote: the partie that is free ought to come to the other, if at least that other require it.

items.text: While apart by necessity, keep your love alive through letters, messages, and gifts, and return as soon as possible.
items.quote: take all occasions... to manifest their longing desire one after another by letters, messages, tokens... and to return with all the speed they can.

items.text: Leave your father and mother and cleave to your wife.
items.quote: man is enioyned to leaue father and mother, and to cleaue vnto his wife

items.text: Care for one another's well-being.
items.quote: a mutuall prouident care in husband and wife one for another

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 10 · Of equalitie in estat• and condition betwixt those that are to be maried together.

items.text: Marry one of similar estate and wealth, so that neither demeans the other as servant but lives as a yoke-fellow.
items.quote: Some equalitie in outward estate and wealth is also befitting the parties that are to be maried together

items.text: Seek a partner of similar social condition, not above or below your degree.
items.quote: that Princes, Nobles, and Gentlemen, mary such as are of their owne ranke: and the meaner sort such as are of their degree

items.text: Tell your father and mother of your intention to marry and gain their consent before proceeding.
items.quote: if that partie be vnder the gouernment of parents, the matter must be moued to them, before there be any further proceeding therein

items.text: Declare your liking to the person you wish to marry and confirm mutual affection before marrying.
items.quote: that liking must be moued to the other partie so liked, to know whether there be a reciprocall affection of one towards another

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 26 · Of husbands and wiues redressing sinne in one another. … Of husbands and wiues helping forward the growth of grace in each other.

items.text: If your spouse falls into any sin, reprove and restore him or her by meek instruction, persuasion, and gentle reproof, and do not let sin lie on them.
items.quote: When either husband or wife is fallen into any sinne, a mutuall dutie it is for the other, to vse what redresse may be of that sinne.

items.text: Help forward the growth of grace in your spouse by approving the least measure of grace in them, by holy conference about religion, by mutual example, by prayer and reading together, and by stirring one another to attend public worship.
items.quote: Hereunto must be added an helping forward of the growth thereof: which man and wife must mutually endeuour to effect one in another.

items.text: Put your husband in mind of maintaining holy exercise in the family, and stir him up if he is backward; your persuasion can prevail with him more than any other's.
items.quote: the wife must put her husband in minde thereof, if he forget it; and stirre him vp, if he be backward.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 8 · Of the lawfulnesse of other mariages after one of the maried couple is dead.

items.text: Yield to your spouse the power over your body that marriage gives, and do not withhold it.
items.quote: the bond of mariage giueth them a like power ouer one anothers body

items.text: Remain bound to your spouse as long as he or she lives, for death alone dissolves the bond.
items.quote: The woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband, so long as he liueth

items.text: If your brother died childless, marry his widow to raise up offspring for him.
items.quote: it commanded the next kinsman that was liuing and free to marie her, that he might raise vp seed to his brother deceased
items.conflict: Not binding under the New Testament; a widow is free to marry whom she will, only in the Lord (1 Cor 7:39).

items.text: If he refuses to marry you, loose his shoe and spit in his face before the elders.
items.quote: the widow reiected was to loose his shooe from his foot, and to spit in his face in the presence of the Elders
items.conflict: This penalty is part of the Levitical law, not binding on Christians; do not shame your brother-in-law but leave judgment to God.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 20 · Of husbands and wiues hatefull imprecations and wishes one against another. … Of husbands and wiues mutuall care for one anothers saluation.

items.text: Never curse her or wish her dead, either aloud or in your heart.
items.quote: cursing the day that euer they knew one another, and wishing that one of them had beene vnder the ground before they came together.

items.text: Never curse him or wish him dead, either aloud or in your heart.
items.quote: their hearts will be filled with a thousand wishes of one anothers death.

items.text: Pray for her and seek her salvation, that you may be a means of saving her.
items.quote: What knowest thou, ô man, whether thou shalt SAVE thy wife?

items.text: Pray for him and seek his salvation, that you may be a means of winning him to Christ.
items.quote: S. Peter enioyneth wiues to doe their endeuour to win their husbands.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 11 · Of husbands and wiues mutuall hatred contrary to loue. … Of contentions betwixt man and wife.

items.text: Love your spouse, for this alone is motive enough: they are yours by God's ordinance.
items.quote: such an one is thine husband, or such an one is thy wife, yet this should be motiue enough.

items.text: Maintain outward peace and agreement with your spouse, for they are nearer than brothers and sisters.
items.quote: they are neerer then brothers and sisters.

items.text: Avoid giving offense to your spouse, for offenses cause contentions.
items.quote: Offences cause contentions.

items.text: When an offense is given, do not take it but pass it by, so peace will not be broken.
items.quote: When an offence is giuen by the one partie, it must not be taken by the other; but rather passed by.

items.text: When both are angry, labor quickly to quench the fire; do not let wrath lie with you nor part beds for it; strive first to offer reconciliation and accept it when offered.
items.quote: Wrath must not lie in bed with two such bed-fellowes: neither may they part beds for wrath sake... they must both striue first to offer reconciliation.

items.text: Do not bolster up children, servants, or any in the household against your spouse.
items.quote: Children, seruants, nor any other in the family must be bolstred vp by the one against the other.

items.text: Do not make comparisons with other husbands or wives, or with a former spouse, for they stir up contention.
items.quote: They must forbeare to twit one another in the teeth with the husbands or wiues of other persons: or with their owne former husbands or wiues.

items.text: Take heed of rash and unjust jealousy, for it is the bane of marriage and picks quarrels.
items.quote: Aboue all they must take heed of rash and vniust iealousie, which is the bane of mariage.

items.text: Endeavor to please your spouse in all things consistent with a good conscience, and let your own will be crossed rather than give them discontent.
items.quote: In all things that may stand with a good conscience they must endeuour to please one another.

items.text: Be of one mind; when discord threatens, say, Let there be no strife between us, for we are one flesh.
items.quote: let man and wife be of the same minde one to another as Abraham was to Lot... say, Let there be no strife betwixt thee and me, for we are man and wife: no more two, but one flesh.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 1 · Of the generall heads of this treatise. … Of a wiues subiection in generall.

items.text: Submit to your own husband in everything as to the Lord; let your opinions, affections, speech, and actions all savor subjection.
items.quote: Wiues submit your selues vnto your owne husbands as vnto the Lord.

heading: Treatise 1 · The first Treatise. AN EXPOSITION OF THAT PART OF SCRIPTVRE out of which Domesticall Duties are raised. · Section 129 · Of the meaning of this phrase, Doe the same things. … Of masters forbearing threatning.

items.text: Fear, obey, and do service to your master with singleness of heart as unto Christ.
items.quote: to feare, to obey, to doe seruice, with the like

items.text: Perform the good duties of your place toward your servant with singleness of heart, as unto Christ, not with eye-service.
items.quote: with singlenesse of heart, as vnto Christ, not with eie seruice as men pleasers, but as the seruants of Christ they doe the will of God from the heart.

items.text: Treat your servant justly and equitably.
items.quote: he expresseth there vnder these two words, iust, equall

items.text: Seek your servant's good, not merely your own use of him.
items.quote: they are for their seruants good, as well as seruants for theirs.

items.text: Forbear threatening and moderate your authority over your servant.
items.quote: forbearing threatning

items.text: Do not consider yourself to have absolute power over your servant.
items.quote: Now that Christian masters should not be of the same minde

items.text: When your servant repents and promises amendment, do not execute every threatened vengeance.
items.quote: though the partie that caused the threatning be neuer so sorie for his fault, and humble himselfe, and promise amendment, and giue good hope thereof.

items.text: Be mild, gentle, patient, and long-suffering toward your servant.
items.quote: mildnesse, gentlenesse, patience, long suffering, with the like.

items.text: Do not be bitter toward your wife.
items.quote: the Apostle dehorteth husbands from bitternesse

items.text: Do not provoke your children to wrath.
items.quote: parents from prouoking their children to wrath

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 3 · Of an husbands superioritie ouer a wife, to be acknowledged by a wife. … Of a fond conceit, that husband and wife are equall.

items.text: Acknowledge that he is your superior by God's appointment, and that he has authority over you; do not think yourself every way as good as him.
items.quote: That she acknowledge her husband to be her superiour.

items.text: Respect him as your superior, yielding him the honor and reverence due to his place above you.
items.quote: That she respect him as her superiour.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 39 · Of the vices contrary to the good prouidence of husband and wife, about the goods of the family.

items.text: Provide for your wife what is meet for her place while you live together, and make provision for her maintenance if she outlives you.
items.quote: affordeth vnto his wife so much as is meet for her place while he liueth with her, nor thinketh of prouiding sufficient maintenance for her, if shee ouer-liue him

items.text: Do not secretly hoard, purloin, or commit to others your husband's goods without his knowledge; deal faithfully with his estate.
items.quote: a wife secretly hoordeth vp whatsoeuer she can get, either by her owne industry, or else by purloining from her husband

items.text: Do not spend your goods on your own pleasures abroad while your wife wants at home; she was given to you as a helper and deserves your care.
items.quote: spend their goods abroad in hunting, hauking, carding, dicing, eating, drinking, or the like, and suffer their wiues to want at home

items.text: Do not bring your husband into debt or weaken his estate by excessive spending on apparel, house adornment, dainty fare, or idle gossiping.
items.quote: by gorgeous decking and adorning their houses, by braue and costly apparell, by dainty fare, by gossipping abroad

items.text: Be diligent and careful to preserve and increase your family estate; do not idle away your days or neglect your household's goods.
items.quote: Idlenesse, and a carelesse neglect of their estate

items.text: Remember you were married to do your husband good, not evil; be a helper suited to him.
items.quote: they were maried to doe their husbands good, and not euill all the daies of their life

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 9 · Of remedies against Adulterie, and in particular of due beneuolence, and of defect or excesse therein.

items.text: Delight in your wife and maintain a pure and fervent love, yielding due benevolence as a remedy against adultery; do not deny it when justly required.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Section 9
items.quote: yeelding that due beneuolence one to another which is warranted & sanctified by Gods word

items.text: Delight in your husband and maintain a pure and fervent love, yielding due benevolence as a remedy against adultery; do not deny it when justly required.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Section 9
items.quote: yeelding that due beneuolence one to another which is warranted & sanctified by Gods word

items.text: Do not be insatiable; forbear this duty during fasts, when she is weak or sick, in her time of separation, and while she nurses.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Section 9
items.quote: Excesse is either in the measure, or in the time. In the time, when it is against Pietie, Mercy, or Modestie.

items.text: Do not be insatiable; forbear this duty during fasts and when he is weak or sick.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 2, Section 9
items.quote: Many husbands and wiues are much oppressed by their bedfellowes vnsatiablenesse in this kinde.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 23 · Of husbands and wiues care to win one the other, when one of them is not called. … Of husbands and wiues hindering sinne one in another.

items.text: If your spouse is not a believer, use every means to draw him or her to faith in Christ.
items.quote: If one be a beleeuer the other not, the beleeuer must vse all the meanes that may be, to draw on the other also to beleeue.

items.text: If married to an unbeliever, dwell with them and do not separate.
items.quote: To this end doth S. Paul aduise beleeuing husbands and wiues that are maried to vnbeleeuers, to dwell with them.

items.text: Since both are believers, build one another up in the most holy faith.
items.quote: If both be beleeuers, their mutuall care must be to edifie one another in thier most holy faith.

items.text: Watch over one another to prevent sin before it is committed, and make redress after it is committed.
items.quote: both to preuent sinne before it be committed, and also to make what redresse they can after it is committed.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 10 · Of mutuall loue betwixt man and wife.

items.text: Love your wife with a fervent, constant affection.
items.quote: husbands to loue their wiues

items.text: Love your husband with a fervent, constant affection.
items.quote: wiues, and they are commanded to be louers of their husbands

items.text: Let mutual love be the ground of all other duties, so that all is done in love.
items.quote: Loue is the ground of all the rest

items.text: Love your present spouse as entirely as any former spouse, and do not let love for the deceased diminish it.
items.quote: their loue must be as intire to that other as it was to the former

items.text: Honor the memory of a virtuous deceased spouse.
items.quote: the memorie of a vertuous husband or wife ought to be pretious to the suruiuing partie

items.text: Cleave to your spouse and do not let love for parents swallow up your love for your spouse.
items.quote: leaue father and mother, and cleaue to their yoke-fellow

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 33 · Of the wisdome of husbands and wiues, in redressing one anothers ill name. … Of husbands and wiues like affection towards one anothers credit.

items.text: Give notice to one another of any ill report and labor to bring each other to repentance.
items.quote: husbands and wiues must first giue one another notice of the report that goeth of them, and endeuour to worke in them a sense of those euils

items.text: Notice the good qualities in one another and speak of them when occasion offers.
items.quote: take notice of the good qualities which are in one another, and make those good qualities the subiect of their speech

items.text: Receive with joy sincere reports of your spouse's good qualities, without feeling lessened by their praise.
items.quote: lend a willing and ioyfull eare to such as shall truly and vnfainedly, without flatterie or hypocrisie, speake any thing in commendation of the one or of the other

items.text: Imitate the good things you see or hear in your spouse, so that others may say you learned it from each other.
items.quote: they must imitate those good things which they behold, or heare to be in one another, and so imitate them

items.text: Tell one another of the good report you hear, so that you may both give glory to God and walk worthy of it.
items.quote: wisely and seasonably to giue one another notice of that good fame which is raised of them, thereby to prouoke them both to giue glorie to God

items.text: Feel your spouse's reputation as your own: rejoice in their good report, grieve at their ill report.
items.quote: be so affected with the report that goeth of either of them, as if the report were of their owne selues

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART I. Of Husband and Wife, who are so to be accounted. · Section 20 · Of clandestine mariages. … Of ill or well ordering mariage feasts.

items.text: Marry openly, not in private or secret, but with a lawful minister and sufficient witnesses, for the honor of marriage.
items.quote: clandestine mariages, such as are made in priuate houses, or other secret places, or in Churches without a sufficient number of witnesses, or in the night time, or without a lawfull Minister of the word

items.text: When your daughter marries, gather friends and make a feast, as Laban did for his daughter.
items.quote: Laban gathered together all the men of the place, when his daughter was maried.

items.text: Make a feast for your son's wedding, as the king made for his son in the parable.
items.quote: it is noted that many guests were bidden to the wedding.

items.text: Invite friends and godly guests, such as Jesus and his disciples, to the wedding feast.
items.quote: when a friend of the virgin Marie was maried, Iesus and his Disciples, besides many other, were inuited thereto.

items.text: Make the wedding feast within your means, at a seasonable time, with moderation, and sanctify it with edifying talk, riddles, and psalms.
items.quote: moderation vsed both by him that maketh the feast, and also by them that partake thereof

items.text: When you are a guest at a wedding feast, eat and drink moderately, do not overindulge or spend too much time, and keep from corrupt talk.
items.quote: moderation vsed both by him that maketh the feast, and also by them that partake thereof

items.text: At your wedding feast, remember the poor and needy and send them portions.
items.quote: let the poore that scarce haue sufficiencie be remembred.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 7 · Of a wiues inward feare of her husband. … Of a wiues base esteeme of her husband.

items.text: Reverence him in your heart, esteeming him worthy of all honor for his place and office because he is your husband.
items.quote: Let the wife see that she feare her husband.

items.text: Be careful to please him.
items.quote: such an awfull respect of him as maketh her care how she may please him

items.text: Do not despise him or think lowly of him; rather, overlook his infirmities and honor his office.
items.quote: they ought to turne their eies and thoughts from his person to his place, and from his vicious qualities to his honourable office.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 16 · Of the errour of Papists about man and wifes separation. … Of husbands and wiues vnlawfull absenting themselues one from another.

items.text: Dwell with her; do not send her away to a country house or live apart without necessity.
items.quote: send their wiues vnto some countrey house, and there euen mew them vp, as Hawkes, neuer caring to come at them

items.text: Dwell with him; do not gad out of the house in the day or lie out at night from mere lightness.
items.quote: gad out of their owne houses in the day, lie out of them in the night

items.text: Put her away only for fornication; any other cause of divorce makes her commit adultery.
items.quote: whosoeuer shall put away his wife, causeth her to commit adulterie

items.text: Do not separate from bed and cohabitation to pursue a supposedly higher estate; no estate on earth is more perfect for married persons.
items.quote: No estate in this world can be greater or perfecter then is meet for maried persons.

items.text: Share one household; do not have separate rooms, tables, servants, or beds even in the same house.
items.quote: the man abiding in one end thereof, his wife in another: and so haue their seuerall roomes, seuerall tables, seuerall seruants

items.text: Render due benevolence to one another; do not deprive each other by separate beds.
items.quote: they rob each other of that due beneuolence which they mutually owe one to another

items.text: Do not divorce even if your spouse solicits you to sin; walk warily, avoid society for a time, or complain to the magistrate, but seek reform.
items.quote: it is no sufficient cause finally to dissolue mariage

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 28 · Of the sinnes of husbands and wiues contrary to a mutuall care of one anothers saluation. … Of husbands and wiues mutuall care ouer one anothers body.

items.text: Seek first the salvation of your spouse; do not let care for earthly things make you neglect it.
items.quote: procuring the Saluation of one another

items.text: Let your conduct adorn the gospel, that your spouse may not be kept from faith but be won to it.
items.quote: vnchristian cariage of a beleeuer that is maried to one that beleeueth not: hereby the vnbeleeuer is kept off from embracing the Gospell

items.text: Observe one another's life and conversation, and keep each other back from running into sin.
items.quote: keepe not backe, nor restraine one another from running into any sinne

items.text: Do not merely seek to please one another; in love draw each other away from evil, not into it.
items.quote: seeking mutually to please one another in all things, without respect of good or euill

items.text: Do not let fear of offending keep you from instructing and admonishing your spouse when they are in sin and danger.
items.quote: An vndue feare of offending one another by Christian instruction, admonition, reproofe

items.text: Do not mock or scoff at the holy zeal and forwardness you see in your spouse; rather encourage it.
items.quote: mocke, and scoffe at that holy zeale, and forwardnesse which they obserue in their bedfellowes

items.text: Nourish and cherish one another's body as your own flesh.
items.quote: No man hateth his owne flesh, but nourisheth and cherisheth it: now man and wife are one flesh

items.text: Love and cherish your spouse in every condition: in poverty and wealth, sickness and health, and bear one another's burdens in distress.
items.quote: for better for worse, for richer for poorer, in sicknesse and in health to loue and to cherish

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 30 · Of husbands and wiues backwandnesse to helpe one another in time of need. … Of husbands and wiues preuenting each others discredit.

items.text: Provide what is needful for one another, and be a continual comfort and help to ease each other's burdens.
items.quote: a continuall comfort and helpe each to other, and to ease the burdens of one another

items.text: Regard the good name of your spouse as dear as your own, and seek each other's honor and credit.
items.quote: As deare ought the good name of the wife be vnto the husband, and of the husband to the wife, as their owne.

items.text: Do not disclose or spread abroad each other's infirmities or anything that may discredit; rather conceal them as much as you may with a good conscience.
items.quote: may in no case delight to discouer vnto others, and spread abroad the infirmities, and imperfections of one another

items.text: Do not open your ears to hear every tale against your spouse, but show yourself displeased with those who bring evil reports.
items.quote: must not haue their eares wide opened to heare euery tale and report that shall be brought to one against the other, but rather shew themselues displeased

items.text: Do not be over-hasty to judge or condemn your spouse on reports; rather suspend judgment.
items.quote: may not be ouer-headie or hastie to iudge and condemne

items.text: Do not rashly believe evil reports about each other; suppress all light suspicions as much as you can.
items.quote: must not rashly beleeue any euill report of one another, but rather suppresse all light suspitions

items.text: Interpret doubtful things in the better part, and mitigate evident faults as far as truth and justice allow.
items.quote: To interpret doubtfull things in the better part. 2. To mitigate, so farre as truth and iustice will suffer, the faults which are euident.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 11 · Of wiue-like courtesie and obeysance. … Of wife-like modestie in apparell.

items.text: Show him outward obeisance on solemn occasions: when he goes or returns, when making a great request, or at table, to testify your reverence.
items.quote: to declare her reuerence by some obeysance

items.text: In attire, have regard to your husband's place and estate rather than your own birth or humor: be neither too costly for his ability nor unfitting his calling.
items.quote: apparell be neither for costlinesse aboue her husbands abilitie, nor for curiousnesse vn beseeming his calling

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 28 · Of propertie in goods, whether it giue libertie to dispose them as a wife will. … Of the reasons against a wiues propertie in the common goods of the family.

items.text: Do not dispose of any goods—even what is your own by inheritance or gift—without your husband's consent.
items.quote: She can neither let, sell, alien, giue, nor otherwise of right make any thing away... without his consent

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 1 · Of the heads of those common-mutuall duties. … Of Desertion.

items.text: Account one another one flesh and preserve the inviolable union of marriage; do not depart or put away.
items.quote: Let not the wife depart from her husband: Let not the husband put away his wife.

items.text: Keep the marriage bed undefiled; be faithful to your spouse in body and desire.
items.quote: Matrimoniall Chastity.

items.text: Love your spouse with a genuine and tender affection.
items.quote: A louing affection of one to another.

items.text: Dwell together, for cohabitation is the means by which provident care is effected.
items.quote: the Meanes whereby it may be the better effected (which is Cohabitation)

items.text: Provide for your spouse's soul, body, good name, and goods.
items.quote: a prouident care of one for another

items.text: Together with your spouse, perform your duties to the members of the household and to guests.
items.quote: Members of the familie. 2. Guests which come to the familie.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 43 · Of a wiues actiue Obedience. … Of a wiues willingnesse to dwell where her husband will.

items.text: Obey his lawful commands readily, and redress what he justly blames.
items.quote: readily to doe what he lawfully commands. ... carefully to redresse what he iustly blameth.

items.text: Be willing to dwell where he will have you dwell, and go with him when he moves from place to place.
items.quote: a wife ought to be willing to dwell where her husband will haue her dwell.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 26 · Of humane lawes which restraine wiues from disposing goods, without or against their husbands consent. … Of the inconueniences which may follow vpon a wiues disposing goods without or against her husbands consent.

items.text: Dispose of no goods, lands, or inheritance without your husband's consent, and obey the laws that make such dispositions void.
items.quote: euerie gift, grant, or disposition of goods... made by a woman couert... without her husbands consent, are void.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 9 · Of wiue-like sobriety. … Of wiue-like mildnesse.

items.text: Show your husband outward reverence in your gesture and speech, manifesting your inward respect for him.
items.quote: A wiues outward reuerence towards her husband is a manifestation of her inward due respect of him.

items.text: Maintain a sober, comely, grave, and gracious carriage before your husband, showing respect for his God-given authority.
items.quote: such a comely, graue, and gratious carriage, as giueth euidence to the husband that his wife respecteth his place & the authority which God hath giuen him.

items.text: Order your countenance, gesture, and whole carriage before your husband with mildness, showing contentment and willingness to be ruled by him.
items.quote: Mildnesse in a wife hath respect also to the ordering of her countenance, gesture, and whole cariage before her husband.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 5 · Of a wiues acknowledgement of her owne husbands superioritie. … Of wiues denying honour to their owne husbands.

items.text: Acknowledge your own husband, to whom God by his providence has joined you in marriage, to be worthy of a husband’s honor and to be your superior.
items.quote: wiues acknowledge their owne husbands, euen those to whom by Gods prouidence they are ioyned in mariage, to be worthy of an husbands honour, and to be their superiour

items.text: Be in subjection to your own husband, even if he is an infidel or of evil character, and let your conduct be with respect and fear.
items.quote: Be in subiection to them: let your conuersation be in feare.

items.text: Do not imagine you could better submit to any other husband than your own; apply the general acknowledgement of a husband’s superiority to your own husband.
items.quote: they thinke they could better subiect themselues to any husband, then their owne

items.text: Do not marry a man of far lower rank, or a youth, merely to rule over him, for by marrying you make yourself subject to him by God’s law and man’s.
items.quote: purposely mary men of farre lower ranke then themselues, for this very end, that they may rule ouer their owne husbands

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 13 · Of a wiues reuerend speech to her husband. … Of the titles which wiues giue their husbands.

items.text: Speak reverently of her husband both in his presence and in his absence.
items.quote: A wiues reuerence is manifested by her speech, both in her husbands presence, and also in his absence.

items.text: Be sparing in speech when with her husband: do not talk much, interrupt him, or take over the conversation, but listen.
items.quote: For this end in his presence her words must be few

items.text: Give her husband titles that signify superiority and reverence, such as Lord, husband, or Master with his surname; avoid titles of equality, familiarity, or abuse.
items.quote: the titles which a wife in speaking to her husband, or naming him, giueth vnto him, they must be such as signifie superioritie, and so sauour of reuerence.

items.text: Speak to him with meekness and quietness, not with stoutness or stubbornness.
items.quote: Meeknesse to the manner of framing her speech to him.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 38 · Of husbands and wiues mutuall prouidence about the goods of the family.

items.text: Be as provident as you can with a good conscience in getting, keeping, and disposing goods for the mutual good of your spouse.
items.quote: be as prouident as they can be with a good conscience in getting, keeping, and disposing competent goods and riches for the mutuall good one of another.

items.text: Provide for her material needs, as one who must care for his own.
items.quote: care of prouiding for their owne enioyned to them

items.text: Ensure she will have a fitting portion of the goods if she outlives you.
items.quote: the wife, if she suruiue the husband, ought to haue such a portion of those goods, as are meet for her place and charge.

items.text: Help him in providing and preserving the goods of the family, and do not waste what he brings home.
items.quote: by her industry and prouidence shee did so preserue and increase his goods

items.text: Keep at home and govern the house, as the Apostle directs.
items.quote: keepe at home, and gouerne the house

items.text: Do not waste what she provides through gambling, drinking, or reveling.
items.quote: the husband by carding, dicing, drinking, reuelling, or other like meanes should waste all away

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 23 · Of a wiues restraint in disposing goods without consent of her husband: and of the ground of that restraint. … Of the law of a wiues vow.

items.text: Do not give away or spend the common goods of the family without your husband's consent, except in extraordinary necessity.
items.quote: a wife hath not power so to doe

items.text: Do not make a vow without your husband's consent; if you have vowed, let him disannul it.
items.quote: a wife might not make a vow without her husbands consent... though she hath vowed, yet her husband hath power to disanull her vow.

items.text: Be subject to your husband in everything.
items.quote: Let wiues be subiect to their husbands in euerie thing.

items.text: While you remain in the family, do not dispose of the family goods without your elder brother's consent.
items.quote: the younger brother might not simply without or directly against the elder brothers consent dispose the goods of the family.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 20 · Of the things whereabout a wife must haue her husbands consent. … Of a wiues liberty in extraordinary matters.

items.text: Do nothing that belongs to his authority simply without or directly against his consent.
items.quote: A wife must doe nothing which appertaineth to her husband authoritie simply without, or directly against his consent.

items.text: Guide and govern the house, providing sufficiently for the family and distributing to the poor as she sees occasion.
items.quote: It is the wiues place and dutie to guide or gouerne the house.

items.text: Relieve those in great need, even without her husband's consent, if he is hard-hearted.
items.quote: if they be in great need, yet without his consent she may releeue him.

items.text: If her husband wastes the estate, lay up what goods she can for the good of her husband, herself, children, and whole household.
items.quote: a faithfull prouident wife obseruing her husband to riot, may without his consent lay vp what goods she can for her husbands, her own, her childrens, and whole housholds good.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 52 · Of cases wherein a wife ought to forbeare what her husband requireth. … Of the manner of a wiues subiection to her husband.

items.text: Refuse to obey him when he commands what God has forbidden, such as idolatry, impurity, or dishonest gain.
items.quote: If an husband require his wife to doe that which God hath forbidden she ought not to doe it.

items.text: Before refusing, first with meekness and by all good means try to dissuade him from urging what she cannot do with a good conscience.
items.quote: first labour with all meekenesse and by all good meanes that she can to disswade her husband from vrging and pressing that vpon her

items.text: Subject yourself to him as you would to Christ, for he is Christ's representative in his office.
items.quote: The wife must subiect her selfe to her husband in that manner, that she would or should subiect her selfe to Christ.

items.text: Submit to him even if he is an enemy of Christ, for in his office he bears Christ's image.
items.quote: Yea: because in his office he is in Christs stead, though in his heart an enemie.

items.text: Let your subjection be seasoned with humility, sincerity, cheerfulness, and constancy.
items.quote: there are foure vertues which are especially needfull hereunto... Humilitie, Sinceritie, Cheerefulnesse, Constancie.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 55 · Of wiues humilitie in euery duty. … Of wiues complementall subiection.

items.text: Be subject to your husband with humility, thinking better of him than yourself.
items.quote: as the Church is humbly subiect to Christ, so let wiues be to their husbands.

items.text: Be subject to your husband with sincerity, from the heart, not merely in outward show.
items.quote: as the Church is sincerely subiect to Christ, so let wiues be to their husbands.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 48 · Of a wiues readinesse to redresse what her husband iustly reproueth in her. … Of a wiues contentment with her husbands present estate. Of submission hitherto.

items.text: Readily redress whatever he justly reproves in you: if you omitted a duty, perform it; if you committed an evil, make amends and do it no more.
items.quote: a wife readily redresse what is iustly reproued by her husband

items.text: Do not wax worse for his reproof or hate him for reproving you, as scorners do.
items.quote: Contrary is their spirit who for reproofe waxe the worse: being like those scorners that hate those that reproue them.

items.text: Rest content with your husband's present estate, whether high or low, great or mean, wealthy or needy, even if he has decayed from a better estate.
items.quote: a wife must rest satisfied and contented, whether it be high or low, great or meane, wealthy or needy

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 40 · Of husbands and wiues ioint care in gouerning the family.

items.text: Rule your own house honestly, for you are the highest in the family and have authority over all and charge of all.
items.quote: that they rule their owne house honestly

items.text: Govern the house as its mistress, ruling those under you together with your husband, always in subjection to him.
items.quote: the wife is called mistresse of the house, as well as the husband master of the house

items.text: Aid your wife in governing, adding authority to her so that she is not despised or lightly esteemed.
items.quote: The husband by his helpe aiding his wife, addeth much authoritie vnto her, and so causeth that she is not despised, nor lightly esteemed.

items.text: Be subject to your husband in governing, and do not command anything against his command unless it is against the Lord's word.
items.quote: she is subordinate to her husband, and must so rule others as she be subiect to her husband, and not command any thing against his command

items.text: Keep your children in awe when they grow great or stubborn.
items.quote: keeping children when they grow great, or waxe stubborne, in awe

items.text: Nourish and instruct your children when they are young.
items.quote: nourishing and instructing children when they are young

items.text: Rule the men servants in your house.
items.quote: ruling men seruants

items.text: Rule the maid servants in your house.
items.quote: ruling maid seruants

items.text: Perform the acts of prayer, reading the word, catechizing, and other like duties in the family.
items.quote: perform the very actions of prayer, reading the word, catechizing, and other like duties in the family

items.text: Remind your husband of the duty and time of family worship, encourage him, gather the family, and by your example and urging promote instruction.
items.quote: putting her husband in minde both of the dutie it selfe, and of the time of performing it, and incouraging him to doe it, in gathering the family together

items.text: If your husband is absent or negligent, perform prayer, reading, and teaching yourself, or get another to do it.
items.quote: in praying, reading, teaching, and performing like exercises her selfe, so farre as she is able, when her husband is absent, or negligent

items.text: Provide convenient house-room and other necessaries for the family.
items.quote: prouiding conuenient house-roome, and other necessaries for the family

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 42 · Of aberrations contrary to a wiues subiection in doing things without or against their husbands consent.

items.text: Do not take money or goods from your husband's possession without his knowledge and consent.
items.quote: priuily take money out of their husbands closets, counters, or other like places where he laieth it, neuer telling him of it

items.text: Do not demand an allowance of your own choosing, but accept what your husband allots.
items.quote: will haue what allowance they thinke best for themselues and family, and scornfully say, They will not be at their husbands finding

items.text: Bring up your children as your husband directs, not according to your own fancy.
items.quote: cocker, attire, or any way bring vp their children otherwise then their husbands would

items.text: Take in and put out servants as your husband approves, and treat them so as to keep good servants.
items.quote: will haue their owne will about seruants, taking in, and putting out whom they please

items.text: Do not lend out your husband's horses or cattle secretly to please a friend.
items.quote: secretly lend out their husbands horses, or other like cattell, more respecting to pleasure a vaine friend

items.text: When your husband is away, be solitary and abstain from merry meetings, showing his absence is a damp to your mirth.
items.quote: then most frolicke and iolly, when their husbands are furthest off

items.text: Be a keeper at home; do not go out when and where you will without your husband's consent.
items.quote: they thinke they haue power to goe when and whither they will, and to tarrie out as long as they list

items.text: Make no vow or oath, especially a religious one, without your husband's consent.
items.quote: care not how or what they binde themselues vnto without their husbands consent

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 45 · Of a wiues readinesse to come to her husband when he requires it. … Of a wiues readinesse to doe what her husband requireth.

items.text: Come to your husband when he calls for you or sends for you, and yield even if you think it a slight to do so.
items.quote: to come to her husband when her husband requireth it, either by calling her, or sending for her.

items.text: Perform the business he requires of you, and do not refuse it as if you were too good to serve him.
items.quote: to performe what businesse he requireth of her.

items.text: If you think his command unseemly, first try by all fair means to be spared; but if he insists and the thing is not unlawful, yield.
items.quote: if by all she could not haue preuailed, then (the thing being not simplie vnlawfull and a sinne) she should haue yeelded.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 41 · Of the vices contrary to a ioint care of gouerning the family. … Of husbands and wiues mutuall helpe in hospitality.

items.text: Do not leave all government of the family to her, but help her, especially in religious duties, since she was made to be your helper.
items.quote: shall your wiues who were made to be an helpe to you, haue no helpe from you

items.text: Be not careless of the government, but add your aid as joint governor with your husband.
items.quote: Doe not such peruert that maine end for which God made them, euen to be an helpe?

items.text: Do not keep back children and servants from religious exercises, nor use them as instruments of iniquity, but support his religious governance.
items.quote: but keepe backe children and seruants, and so are a great griefe vnto their religious husbands

items.text: Do not scoff at her good counsel, but allow her to find fault and help redress what is amiss.
items.quote: when they scoffe and scorne at that good counsell which their wiues giue them

items.text: In hospitality, take order for provision of things outside the house, as your part of the joint duty.
items.quote: To take order for the prouision of things without doores is more fit for the husband

items.text: In hospitality, order the smaller things within the house, as your part of the joint duty.
