items.quote: to order the smaller things within doores is more fit for the wife

items.text: Receive her friends and kindred as if they were your own, since you are one flesh.
items.quote: ought each of them to esteeme of the others friends as of their owne

items.text: Receive his friends and kindred as if they were your own, since you are one flesh.
items.quote: ought each of them to esteeme of the others friends as of their owne

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 30 · Of answers to the reasons for a wiues property. … Of examples and other reasons alleadged for libertie of wiues to dispose goods.

items.text: Yield to your husband in the disposing of goods; do not claim an equal right and power.
items.quote: she may not thinke to haue an equall right and power, she must giue place and yeeld.

items.text: Give your wife a portion to dispose as she sees good.
items.quote: Her husband ought to giue her a portion to dispose as she shall see good

items.text: Ensure your wife has more free and plentiful use of all goods than servants or children.
items.quote: There is due to her a more free and plentifull use of all the goods, then vnto them.

items.text: Do not think that your care and labor in increasing your father's estate gives you equal power to dispose of it.
items.quote: such a childe, or such a seruant hath as great a right and power to dispose such goods as his father or his master

items.text: Render the marriage debt to one another, for each has equal power over the other's body.
items.quote: the wife hath as great a power ouer the husbands body as the husband ouer the wiues

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 71 · Of an husbands office. … Of the resemblance betwixt Christ and an husband.

items.text: Be subject to your husband as the body is subject to the head, for he is your head as Christ is head of the church.
items.quote: Subiection is due to an husband as well as to Christ.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 18 · Of the cases wherein a wife hath power to order things of the house without her husbands consent. … Of diuers kindes of consent.

items.text: Do nothing against your husband's mind; obtain his consent for the things you do.
items.quote: a wife haue her husbands consent for the things which she doth.

items.text: Do what your husband requires.
items.quote: in doing what her husband requireth.

items.text: Be content with your husband's estate and ability, resting satisfied in it.
items.quote: Contentment in resting satisfied and content with his estate and abilitie.

items.text: Even if your husband is an unbeliever or wicked, be subject to him in fear.
items.quote: S. Peter exhorteth faithfull wiues that were maried to Infidell husbands to be subiect to them, and that in feare.

items.text: When your husband is impotent or absent without leaving order, take charge of household affairs yourself, following God's rules of justice, equity, truth, and mercy.
items.quote: the wife hath power to dispose matters without her husbands consent: prouided that she obserue those rules of Gods word concerning iustice, equitie, truth and mercie

items.text: When you have acted on an implicit consent, inform your husband of what you have done when you can.
items.quote: she ought (when conueniently she can) to make known to her husband what she hath done

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 51 · Of cases wherein a wife ought not to forbeare what her husband forbiddeth.

items.text: Yield subjection to your husband as to the Lord, obeying him in everything except where God's command overrides.
items.quote: wiues be subiect to their owne husbands, as the Church is subiect vnto Christ

items.text: When you are not sure that God commands something your husband forbids, do not do it; wait for his consent.
items.quote: If she doubt, then she must stay, and forbeare till she gaine his consent.

items.text: Before doing what God commands against your husband's prohibition, earnestly seek to win his consent.
items.quote: she vse all good meanes she can to gaine her husbands consent, before she doe, euen that which is commanded, against his consent.

items.text: Teach your children the principles of religion, even if your husband forbids you.
items.quote: teach her children the principles of religion

items.text: Restore what you have unjustly or fraudulently taken, even if your husband forbids it.
items.quote: restore that which she hath vniustly and fraudulently gotten

items.text: As her head, be to your wife in Christ's stead: love, guide, and provide for her as Christ does the church.
items.quote: the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ is the head of the Church.

heading: Treatise 2 · The second Treatise. PART. II. Of common-mutuall duties betwixt Man and Wife. · Section 43 · Of vices contrary to mutuall helpe in hospitality. … Of husbands and wiues vnmercifulnesse to the poore.

items.text: Provide for your own household; otherwise you are worse than an infidel.
items.quote: he that prouideth not for them is worse then an infidell

items.text: Take the pains to entertain guests when your husband invites them; do not refuse all such pains.
items.quote: for a wife to refuse all paines in that kinde, and to be discontented when her husband inuites any friends... argueth not a louing affection, nor a wiuelike subiection vnto her husband

items.text: Do not overburden your wife by bringing guests too often, especially guests of no good name.
items.quote: an husband may be in this kinde ouerburdensome to her, by being too ioueall... bringing guests too often into the house, especially if they be guests of no good name

items.text: Entertain your spouse's kindred and friends as willingly as your own; do not be backward or grudge.
items.quote: are backward, and grudge at the entertainment of each others friends and kindred

items.text: At meals, remind one another to send a portion to those who have nothing provided.
items.quote: send part vnto them for whom none is prouided.

items.text: Be bountiful to the poor according to your ability, not grudgingly.
items.quote: the husband himselfe must according to his abilitie be bountifull to the poore

items.text: Stretch out your hand to the poor and needy, and give of what you lawfully may.
items.quote: she is said to stretch out her hand to the poore, and to the needy

items.text: Suffer your wife to be bountiful to the poor, provoke her to it, and allow her means to give.
items.quote: suffer his wife, yea prouoke her so to be, and withall allow her wherewithall to be bountifull

items.text: Stir up your husband to liberality toward the poor, and do not be grieved at his bounty or move him to shut his hand.
items.quote: the wife also must stirre vp her husband to liberalitie... and grieued at their husbands bountie, and still mouing him to shut his hand

items.text: Give good direction to one another in distributing alms: the husband telling who is fit to be relieved, the wife telling what is best to give.
items.quote: the husband by telling the wife who are fit to be releeued... the wife by telling the husband what things are fittest to be giuen away

items.text: Praise and encourage your wife when she gives help to the poor, so that she may continue.
items.quote: he is said to praise her, thereby incouraging her to hold on in doing those good things which she did

items.text: Do not hoard goods or let them perish while the poor are in need; give while they are good.
items.quote: couetously hoord vp all they can get... suffer victuals and other things to perish in the house... rather then that any thing whilst it is good should be giuen out

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 36 · Of Zipporahs case in circumcising her sonne. … Of the restraint of wiues about allowance for themselues or families without their husbands consent.

items.text: Do not dispose of goods or appoint allowance for yourself or your family without his consent.
items.quote: A wife hath not power to appoint what she list her selfe without or against her husbands consent, either for her owne allowance, or for her family

items.text: Rest satisfied with the allowance he appoints, for he is the head and must have the overruling stroke.
items.quote: she must rather rest satisfied with that which he appointeth: for he being the head, must haue the ouer-ruling stroake therein

items.text: If his allowance is too small, try by persuasion to move him to honor, but if he cannot be moved, be content and patient.
items.quote: moue him to that which tendeth to his honour and reputation: but if she can no way preuaile, her subiection requireth contentment and patience

items.text: Be a help to him by counsel, persuasion, and other like means rather than acting on your own.
items.quote: by counsell, perswasion, and other like meanes she may be a great helpe

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 39 · Of a wiues subiection to her husband about children. … Of a wiues subiection in entertaining strangers iournying abroad, and making vowes.

items.text: Do not give names to your children without or directly against your husband's consent.
items.quote: A wife may not simply without, or directly against her husbands consent, order and dispose of the children in giuing them names

items.text: Do not dress or adorn your children above your husband's place and calling; be governed by him in this.
items.quote: she did it not without her husbands consent

items.text: Do not appoint your children's callings without your husband's consent.
items.quote: though before her childe was borne she had by solemne vow dedicated him to the Lord, yet when the childe was borne she asked her husbands consent about it.

items.text: Do not determine your children's place of upbringing or marriage without your husband's consent.
items.quote: she would not send him till Isaak had giuen his consent for his abode there, and taking a wife from thence.

items.text: Do not order or dispose your children's portions without your husband's consent.
items.quote: the wife of her selfe hath not power to order them

items.text: Do not take in or thrust out servants against your husband's mind.
items.quote: They may not take in, or thrust out seruants against their husbands minde.

items.text: Do not employ servants in things you know your husband would dislike unless you gain his consent.
items.quote: they should not vse and imploy their seruants in such things as they know their husbands would dislike, except they can gaine their husbands consent.

items.text: Do not use the family's beasts or cattle without your husband's consent.
items.quote: the Shunemite, who hauing occasion to vse a beast went to her husband, and said, send I pray thee with me one of the asses.

items.text: Do not bring strangers into the house or entertain them without or against your husband's consent.
items.quote: they may not bring strangers into the house and entertaine them without or against their husbands consent.

items.text: Do not journey abroad without your husband's consent.
items.quote: though that good wife had a very weighty and iust occasion to goe vnto the Prophet, yet she would not before she knew her husbands minde.

items.text: Do not make vows without your husband's consent, so that they may be established.
items.quote: the law giueth an husband power to disanull her vow when he knoweth it, it implieth that she ought to haue his consent in making it

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 1 · Of the Generall Heads of this Treatise. … Of that loue which husbands owe their wiues.

items.text: Love her as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her; love her above all others on earth.
items.quote: Husbands loue your owne wiues, euen as Christ also loued the Church

items.text: Be her guide and good example.
items.quote: he is to be a guide, and good example to his wife

items.text: Dwell with her according to knowledge, treating her with understanding and honor as the weaker vessel.
items.quote: he is to dwell with her according to knowledge

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 15 · Of wiues meeknesse in their speeches. … Of a wiues obedience in generall.

items.text: Speak to thy husband meekly and gently in all discourse, with a mild countenance, not hastily, angrily, disdainfully, or scoffingly.
items.quote: Meeknesse in a wiues manner of framing her speech to her husband, doth also commend her reuerend respect of him.

items.text: Entreat what thou desirest of him fairly; persuade him to duty mildly; restrain him from evil with meekness.
items.quote: If she be desirous to obtaine any thing of him, fairely she must intreat it... If she would moue him to performe a bounden dutie, mildly she must perswade him.

items.text: If thou must tell him of a fault, do it with humility and reverence, observing a fit season and gentle manner.
items.quote: If she haue occasion to tell him of a fault, therein she ought to manifest humilitie and reuerence, by obseruing a fit season, and doing it after a gentle manner

items.text: When reproved by him, be silent and patient; do not answer again with reproach or ten words for one.
items.quote: This meeknesse requireth also silence and patience, euen when she is reproued.

items.text: Speak of thy husband with reverence in his absence, as Sarah did; do not speak reproachfully behind his back.
items.quote: The reuerence which a wife beareth to her husband, must further be manifested by her speeches of him in his absence.

items.text: Moderate thy passion and keep in thy tongue with bit and bridle, even if provoked, that thy husband taste not of thy bitterness.
items.quote: Let wiues therefore learne first to moderate their passion, and then to keepe in their tongues with bit and bridle

items.text: Obey thy husband as one's head and master; submit to his rule, for God has placed him in authority over thee.
items.quote: The first law that euer was giuen to woman since her fall, laid vpon her this dutie of Obedience to her husband

items.text: Do not seek to rule or overrule thy husband, nor insist on thy own will; let him exercise authority over thee.
items.quote: They must rule and ouer-rule all, they must command not only children and seruants, but husbands also

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 59 · Of wiues cheerefulnesse in euery dutie. … Of the extent of a wiues obedience.

items.text: Be cheerful in performing every duty to her husband, not sullen or murmuring, so as to make subjection pleasing to God and man.
items.quote: Therefore as the Church is cheerefully subiect vnto Christ, so let wiues be to their husbands.

items.text: Be constant in subjection to her husband, continuing in faithful obedience all the days of their life together, not intermittent or apostatizing.
items.quote: Therefore as the Church is constantly subiect vnto Christ, so let wiues be to their husbands.

items.text: Obey her husband in all things within his authority, even against her own will, unless his command contradicts God's will.
items.quote: Shee may doe nothing against Gods will; but many things must she doe against her owne will if her husband require her.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 16 · Of husbands ready yeelding to their wiues humble suits. … Of husbands harshnesse to their wiues.

items.text: Readily grant her lawful, humble requests; do so freely and cheerfully, more than for any other, unless granting it would be unlawful.
items.quote: he ought to shew so much courtesie as readily to grant her desire

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 43 · Of an husbands giuing fauours to his wife.

items.text: Give your wife favors and gifts freely, not as a debt, but as proof of love.
items.quote: Kindnesse and mildnesse in action consisteth in giuing fauours (as we speake) vnto his wife.

items.text: Be more generous and liberal to your wife than to all others, so she may see she is loved above all.
items.quote: In giuing fauours to a wife, an husband ought to be more bountifull and liberall, then to others, that so she may see thereby he loues her aboue all

items.text: When you give her a favor, deliver it with your own hands unless you are absent.
items.quote: In giuing fauours it is best to bestow them with his owne hands, vnlesse he be absent from her.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 3 · Of an husbands hatred and want of loue. … Of an husbands wise maintaining his authoritie.

items.text: Do not hate her: the nearer and dearer she is, the more violent hatred would be, so keep all hatred from your heart.
items.quote: let husbands take heed how they suffer it to soake into them.

items.text: Love her, and let not even the want of love be found in you, for love is the first mover of all duty.
items.quote: Where this want of loue is, there can be no duty wel performed

items.text: Maintain your authority as head; do not relinquish it or abuse it, but use it for her good and protection.
items.quote: If he abuse his authoritie, he turneth the edge and point of his sword amisse

items.text: Be an example in love, gravity, piety, and honesty, that she may reverence you and give you dutiful respect.
items.quote: Be an ensample in conuersation, in loue, in spirit, in faith, and in purenesse

items.text: Reverence your husband and give him dutiful respect, as to the image and glory of God.
items.quote: worke a reuerend and dutifull respect in their wiues

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 50 · Of wiues discontent at their husbands estate.

items.text: Do not regret your marriage or tell your husband that you would not have married him if you had known his estate; look to God and be content with his providence.
items.quote: If notwithstanding all the meanes which possibly they could vse, they be deceiued, they are to looke vnto God

items.text: Do not lay the blame of your husband's decayed estate upon him, nor vex him with discontented looks, passionate words, or impatient behavior; look to God's providence.
items.quote: Though the estate should be ouerthrowne by the vnthriftinesse of an husband, yet ought a wife to looke vnto Gods prouidence therein

items.text: Stoop to your husband's present condition; do not through pride keep up costly apparel, dainty food, rich furniture, or other expenses beyond his means.
items.quote: will not abate any thing of their braue apparell, dainty cheere, rich furniture, and other like things, which are causes of great expence to their husbands

items.text: Be diligent to help raise and increase your husband's estate; do not lie idly in bed or sit still, but take pains.
items.quote: will not take any whit the more paines to raise vp and increase their husbands estate

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 7 · Of that fellowship which is betwixt man and wife, notwithstanding a wiues inferiority. … Of husbands good esteeme of their owne wiues.

items.text: Rule over her with mutual and loving consent and agreement, as the soul rules the body.
items.quote: As the soule therefore ruleth ouer the body, by a mutuall and louing consent and agreement, so must a man ouer his wife.

items.text: Do not treat her as a servant; she is your partner, not a servant.
items.quote: whence it commeth to passe that wiues are oft vsed little better then seruants.

items.text: Set her at your side above all children, servants, or anyone else in the family.
items.quote: he should set her at his side next to him aboue all children, seruants, or any other in the family

items.text: Esteem your own wife as the fittest and best for you, as one given by God.
items.quote: An husband ought to esteeme that particular person to whom by Gods prouidence he is ioyned in mariage, to be the fittest, and best for him.

items.text: Love your own wife as your own body.
items.quote: husbands loue your OWNE wiues... your OWNE bodies

items.text: Regard her as having power over your body, and yield your body to her as she yields to you.
items.quote: the wife (as well as the husband) is therein both a seruant, and a mistresse, a seruant to yeeld her body, a mistresse to haue the power of his.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 68 · Of care in choosing such husbands as wiues may without griefe be subiect vnto. … Of an husbands place.

items.text: Be subject to your husband as unto the Lord, even as the Church is subject to Christ, for as long as he lives.
items.quote: as the Church is subiect to Christ, so let wiues be to their husbands

items.text: Carry yourself to your wife as God requires, bearing the image of Christ in your headship, and be a savior to her body.
items.quote: if an husband carry himselfe to his wife as God requireth, she will finde her yoke to be easie

items.text: Before consenting to marry, be very careful in your choice of a husband: respect above all his good qualities and conditions, bearing the image of Christ, so that subjection may be with joy and comfort.
items.quote: be very carefull in their choise of husbands: and in their choise to respect aboue all, their good qualities and conditions, therein bearing the image of Christ

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 33 · Of the subiection of wiues in distributing goods to charitable vses. … Of obedience to an husband in such things as he sinfully forbiddeth.

items.text: Obey his restraint from giving alms from his goods, even if he sins in forbidding it.
items.quote: though the husband sinne in restraining his wife, yet shee in that restraint may obey, and that in the Lord

items.text: Try by all good means, yourself and through friends, to move him to grant you liberty to give alms.
items.quote: she ought to vse all the good meanes she can by her selfe and her friends to moue her husband to grant her some libertie

items.text: If he will not grant you liberty, make known to him the cases of those in need and persuade him to relieve them.
items.quote: then she ought to make knowne vnto her husband such persons cases as she thinkes meet to be releeued, and vse all the motiues she can to perswade him to afford them some releefe

items.text: According to your ability, commit something to her discretion and disposition so she may give alms.
items.quote: an husband ought according to his abilitie to commit something to her discretion and disposition

items.text: If you live in his house and have no portion of your own, obey his prohibition from giving alms; you are not guilty for not giving.
items.quote: is he now bound to giue almes? shall the curse be executed on him if he giue not? ... not a curse or sinne

items.text: Obey his prohibition from visiting the sick or prisoners if he forbids it, even if you desire to do such a work of mercy.
items.quote: suppose a sonne or seruant be desirous to visit one sicke or in prison, but his Parent or Master (though leaue be asked) will not suffer him

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 10 · Of husbands preposterous opinion of their owne wiues. … Of the Stoicall disposition of husbands to their wiues.

items.text: Do not judge her corruptly or misinterpret her good qualities, but think well of her as she deserves.
items.quote: a corrupt and peruerse opinion which many haue of their owne wiues, thinking them of all other the worst and vnfittest

items.text: Delight in her entirely and wholly, only in her.
items.quote: to delight in his wife intirely, that is, so to delight in her as wholly and only delighting in her

items.text: Let your love to her comfort you and drive out other grief.
items.quote: Such delight did Isaak take in his wife as it droue out a contrary strong passion... he loued her, and was comforted after his mothers death.

items.text: Rejoice with the wife of your youth and be always ravished with her love.
items.quote: Reioyce with the wife of thy youth: Let her be as the louing Hinde, and pleasant Roe, and be thou rauisht alwaies with her loue.

items.text: Overlook her blemishes and imperfections, counting them as nothing or delighting in her nonetheless.
items.quote: so far to exceed, as to make a man ouersee some such blemishes in his wife... or else to count them no blemishes

items.text: Esteem her highly, affect her ardently, and respect her tenderly beyond what others might think fit.
items.quote: so highly to esteeme, so ardently to affect, so tenderly to respect her, as others may thinke him euen to doat on her.

items.text: Manifest your inward affection by outward carriage, especially because of your authority.
items.quote: because of the husbands place of authority, he must especially take all occasions to manifest this his inward affection.

items.text: Do not be cold or Stoical, but account her dearer than any other woman.
items.quote: Stoick-like delight no more in their owne wiues then in any other women, nor account them any dearer then others.

items.text: Let your affection be grounded on her soul and inward qualities, not merely on her body, and keep it within Christian gravity and sobriety.
items.quote: the affection whereof I speake is not a carnall, sensuall, beastly affection, but such an one as may stand with Christian grauitie and sobriety: hauing relation to the soule of a mans wife as well as to her body

items.text: Let your affection be as great to your husband as his is to you.
items.quote: The wiues affection ought to be as great to her husband

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 76 · Of a mans loue to himselfe, a motiue to prouoke him to loue his wife.

items.text: Love her as his own body, for they two are one flesh.
items.quote: God hauing commanded men to loue their wiues as their owne bodies

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 75 · Of Christs example, a motiue to prouoke husbands to loue their wiues.

items.text: Love your wife as Christ loved the church, not for what you gain but for her good, overcoming her faults with goodness.
items.quote: If Christ who can receiue nothing from the Church notwithstanding loue her, ought not men much more to loue their wiues?

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 39 · Of vndiscreet reproouing a wife. … Of an husbands strangenesse to his wife.

items.text: Regard place, persons, time, and temper in reproving her.
items.quote: regard nor place, nor persons, nor time, nor temper of themselues or their wiues, nor any other circumstance in reprouing

items.text: Use meekness and moderation in reproof, not bitter and disgraceful words.
items.quote: with such bitter and disgracefull termes, as either they prouoke their wiues to answer againe

items.text: Do not reprove when in anger or passion, but control your own spirit.
items.quote: they neuer rebuke but when they are in passion, and so scarse know what they doe

items.text: Show her an amiable and pleasant countenance, not a lofty, grim, frowning, or fiery face.
items.quote: his countenance in his wiues presence, and towards his wife, must be composed to an amiable pleasantnesse.

items.text: Be familiar and amiable in gesture toward her, and do not treat her as a stranger, especially in company.
items.quote: An husbands gesture ought to be so familiar, and amiable towards his wife, as others may discerne him to be her husband

items.text: Avoid excessive fondness and wantonness in public; keep husband-like gravity, sobriety, modesty, and decency.
items.quote: they shew more lightnesse, fondnesse, and dotage, then true kindnesse and loue, which forgetteth not an husband-like grauity, sobriety, modesty and decency.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 44 · Of husbands beating their wiues.

items.text: Do not strike or beat your wife, for she is your own flesh and joint head of the household.
items.quote: With submission to better iudgements, I thinke he may not

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 74 · Of husbands louing their wiues as themselues.

items.text: Love your wife as your own body, with a true and entire affection, without any dissimulation or flattery.
items.quote: They which pretend great loue to their wiues in shew only, offend against nature it selfe.

items.text: Deal with your wife with all tenderness and mildness, nourishing and cherishing her as a bird cherishes her young.
items.quote: husbands with all tendernesse, and mildnesse to deale with their wiues

items.text: Do good to your wife more willingly and cheerfully than to your parents, children, and friends, granting her requests and seeking her benefit.
items.quote: more willingly and cheerefully to doe any thing for their wiues then for parents, children, friends or any other

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 9 · Of childrens asking their parents blessing, whether it be lawfull or no.

items.text: Ask your parents' blessing, seeking God's blessing through their prayers.
items.quote: children ought to seeke this blessing of their parents

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 45 · Of an husbands bearing with his wines infirmities. … Of husbands testinesse.

items.text: Bear with her infirmities as the weaker vessel, showing her honor and tenderness.
items.quote: she is a weake vessell: therefore she is much to be borne withall.

items.text: When she has natural imperfections—inward or outward—show pity and compassion, not offense or contempt.
items.quote: These infirmities should breed pitie, compassion, commiseration, yea and greater tendernesse and respect, but no offence.

items.text: When she actually transgresses, redress it with meek admonition, seasonable advice, and gentle entreaty.
items.quote: By vsing the best and mildest meanes he can to redresse them, as meeke admonition, seasonable aduice, gentle intreatie, and compassionate affection.

items.text: Remove occasions that make her offend, so far as you conveniently can.
items.quote: By remouing the stone whereat she stumbleth, by taking away the occasion (so far as conueniently he can) which maketh her offend.

items.text: Overlook offences that are small or tolerable, passing them by as if you did not perceive them.
items.quote: By turning his eyes away (if the matter be not great, but such as may be tolerated) and taking no notice of the offence, but rather passing by it.

items.text: If you notice an offense, forgive and forget it.
items.quote: By forgiuing and forgetting it (if notice be taken thereof.)

items.text: Do not be testy or peevish, quickly provoked at the least offense, but gently forbear and wisely pass over her faults.
items.quote: not to be prouoked when there is cause of prouocation ministred, is a true Christian vertue

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 49 · Of an husbands prouiding things needfull for his wiues boay. … Of neglecting wiues in their weaknesse.

items.text: Provide competent food, raiment, and all things needful to preserve her health.
items.quote: In health by prouiding such things as are needfull to preserue health, as competent food, raiment, and the like necessaries.

items.text: In sickness provide what is needful to recover her health or to comfort, cherish, and refresh her.
items.quote: In sicknesse such things are to be prouided as are needfull either to recouer her health, or to comfort, cherish and refresh her in her sicknesse.

items.text: To the utmost of your power, procure what may satisfy her longings when she is with child.
items.quote: In procuring for their wiues to the vttermost of their power and abilitie, such things as may saue their longing

items.text: Provide all things needful for her travail and lying in childbed.
items.quote: In prouiding such things as are needfull for their trauell and lying in childbed.

items.text: Do not through covetousness refuse her the means she needs in childbirth, such as a midwife, nurse, convenient lodging, and suitable diet.
items.quote: Some through couetousnesse refuse before hand to afford meanes to their wife to prouide such things as are needfull for her selfe and child

items.text: Do not in her time of pain and weakness upbraid her with lightness or say the child is not yours.
items.quote: through iealous suspicion forbeare not euen in the time of their wiues paine and weaknesse, to vpbraid them with lightnesse, and to say that the childe is none of theirs.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 5 · Of husbands losing their authoritie. … Of husbands high account of wiues.

items.text: Do not take occasions from his faults to despise your husband; it is a just judgment on him if he makes himself contemptible, but it is not your part to despise him.
items.quote: though a wife ought not to take these occasions to despise her husband

items.text: Account your wife a yoke-fellow and companion, giving her honor as a fellow heir of the grace of life.
items.quote: The husband must account his wife a yoke-fellow and companion.

items.text: Tenderly respect your wife in your opinion of her, your affection to her, and your carriage towards her.
items.quote: That an husband tenderly respect his wife.

items.text: Do not rule by sternness, roughness, or cruelty; force breeds slavish fear, hatred, and inward contempt, not true obedience.
items.quote: The sterne, rough, and cruel carriage of husbands, who by violence and tyranny goe about to maintaine their authority.

items.text: Do not yield to your wife's bent in unlawful things, even to avoid giving her discontent; that is a double fault and loses your authority.
items.quote: Against their owne judgement yeeld to the bent of their wiues minde in such things as are vnlawfull.

items.text: Provide for her providently, caring wisely for her needs.
items.quote: That prouidently he care for her.

items.text: Be very watchful against evil instigations, even from your wife, for Satan seeks to subvert your house by her.
items.quote: Let husbands therefore be very watchfull against their wiues euill instigations.

items.text: Do not make yourself contemptible by profaneness, riotousness, drunkenness, or lewdness; behave worthily so that your authority is not lost.
items.quote: by their profanenesse, riotousnesse, drunkennesse, lewdnesse, lightnesse, vnthriftinesse, and other like base carriage, make themselues contemptible, and so lose their authoritie.

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 47 · Of a wiues meeke taking a reproofe.

items.text: Rebuke her when there is needful cause, as one having authority from God.
items.quote: The husband hauing authoritie ouer his wife, by vertue thereof he hath power, yea it is his dutie as there is needfull cause to rebuke her

items.text: Yield obedience to your husband's reproof; this is the chiefest trial of sound obedience.
items.quote: it is her dutie to yeeld obedience thereunto

items.text: Take your husband's reproof meekly, suppressing passion so you can judge the matter rightly.
items.quote: By meeknesse in taking a reproofe.

items.text: Endeavor to redress what your husband justly reproves in you.
items.quote: By endeuour to redresse what is iustly reproued.

items.text: Even if your husband's reproof is bitter or spoken in anger, do not forget your duty; still bear it meekly.
items.quote: He therein forgets his place, yet thereupon she must not forget her duty.

items.text: If his reproof is unjust and he will not hear your apology, endure the grief patiently for conscience toward God.
items.quote: if he refuse to heare her, or will not beleeue her, then (as S. Peter speaketh in another case) she must endure griefe for conscience toward God.

items.text: Do not answer back or return his reproof with scornful speeches, imprecations, or threats.
items.quote: they shall be sure to haue the reproofe rebounded backe againe vpon their faces

items.text: When reproved, do not justify yourself or lay the blame on him; acknowledge your fault and forsake it.
items.quote: they will seeke to iustifie themselues, and lay all the blame on their husbands

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 73 · Of the benefit which a wife hath by an husband. … Of the example of the Church set before wines.

items.text: Be subject to your husband as the Church is to Christ.
items.quote: Wiues are as much bound to be subiect to their husbands, as the Church to Christ.

items.text: Show your husband gratitude by cheerful and ready subjection, not rebellion or disdain.
items.quote: No better testimony of a gratefull heart can be given by a wife to her husband, then cheerefull and ready subiection.

items.text: Protect her from hurt and danger, and provide all things needful for her.
items.quote: he is on the one side her protector, to defend her from hurt, and preserue her from danger; and on the other side, a pronider of all needfull and necessarie

items.text: Govern and aid her as a king, pray with her and for her as a priest, and teach and instruct her as a prophet.
items.quote: he is a King to gouerne and aid her, a Priest to pray with her and for her, a Prophet to teach and instruct her.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 35 · Of well ordering reproofe in the matter thereof. … Whether an husband may reprooue his wife for such things as he is guilty of.

items.text: Reprove her with mildness, as a fruit of love.
items.quote: he must haue an especiall care to sweeten it, especially with mildnesse

items.text: Do not proceed to blows or strokes when reproving her.
items.quote: he may not proceed to blowes, and strokes.

items.text: Reprove her only for a fault you know to be true, not on a light report.
items.quote: Iustice requireth that it be a truth, and a knowne truth

items.text: Reprove her only for weighty faults that endanger her soul, the estate, or the family.
items.quote: namely for some fault that is dangerous to her soule, hurtfull to their estate, contagious by reason of ill example

items.text: Do not believe every light report against her.
items.quote: Credulitie is when credence is giuen to euery light report

items.text: Do not entertain undue suspicion of her.
items.quote: light and causelesse suspicion, which is the mother of iealousie

items.text: Do not reprove her for every small or light matter you dislike.
items.quote: make euery small and light matter which any way he disliketh, matter of reproofe

items.text: Take care that you are not guilty of the fault you reprove in her.
items.quote: he ought to haue an especiall care that he be not guiltie of that crime for which he blameth his wife

items.text: Reprove her for her fault even if you are guilty of the same, lest you also be guilty of neglecting her.
items.quote: if he reproued his wife, he might thereby reclaime both her and himselfe

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 71 · Of combats in pretence of wiues honour. … Of husbands variablenesse.

items.text: Do not make challenges of fight or enter single combats and duels on pretext of maintaining her honour; that course brings her dishonour and you danger.
items.quote: no honour can redound to the wife thereby, but much dishonour and danger to the husband

items.text: Love her with a constant, everlasting love, not by fits; let no provocations or transgressions make you cease to do her good.
items.quote: Hauing loued his owne, he loued them vnto the end ... no prouocations, no transgressions could euer make him forget to loue

items.text: Ground your love on God's ordinance and the matrimonial bond; resolve to be unchanged by any provocation, passing by or bearing with her infirmities.
items.quote: ground his loue on Gods ordinance... passe by all infirmities

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 46 · Of an husbands prouident care for his wife. … Of neglecting their wiues edification.

items.text: Provide her with all things needful, both for soul and body.
items.quote: In prouiding things needfull for his wife.

items.text: Protect her from all things hurtful.
items.quote: In protecting her from things hurtfull.

items.text: Provide private means of spiritual edification for her, such as reading the word, prayer, and catechizing, performing them yourself or arranging for another.
items.quote: holy and religious exercises in the house, as reading the word, praier, catechising

items.text: Provide public means of spiritual edification for her, ordering your habitation and other needs so that she may enjoy the preaching of the word.
items.quote: so to order his habitation, and provide other needfull things, as his wife may be made partaker thereof

items.text: Provide private religious exercises for the good of the whole household, reading the word, prayer, and catechizing.
items.quote: as a master of a family must provide these for the good of his whole house

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 13 · Of an husbands kinde acceptance of such things as his wife doth. … Of husbands too great loftinesse.

items.text: Order your behavior wisely toward your wife for her good and your own honor.
items.quote: dwell with her according to knowledge... order his cariage wisely to his owne honour and his wiues good

items.text: Give your wife no just offense, and wisely handle any offense she gives.
items.quote: giue no iust offence to his wife... wisely he order that offence which is giuen by her

items.text: Kindly accept every good duty she performs, and commend and reward what she does well.
items.quote: kinde and respectiue acceptation of euery good duty which his wife performeth... wisely commend and reward what she doth well

items.text: Show your husband reverent behavior, gesture, and speech.
items.quote: the seuerall duties of a wife: which were drawne to two heads Reuerence.

items.text: Obey your husband.
items.quote: the seuerall duties of a wife: which were drawne to two heads Reuerence. Obedience.

items.text: When she shows reverence, answer with courteous behavior, gesture, and speech, and do not lord it over her.
items.quote: he ought to meet her... by some like courteous behauiour, gesture, and speech... not Lord-like ouerlooke

items.text: Do not provoke your children.
items.quote: Fathers ought not to prouoke their children

items.text: Do not provoke your wife.
items.quote: Fathers ought not to prouoke their children, much lesse husbands their wiues.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 55 · Of husbands too great straitnesse ouer their wiues. … Of husbands neglect of their wiues future estate.

items.text: Let her have such means as may enable her to reward the obedient and to relieve the needy, that she be not ashamed.
items.quote: their wiues are not only depriued of meanes to gaine respect of their children and seruants at home

items.text: Make such provision before death that if she survive thee she may maintain herself according to the place to which thou hast advanced her.
items.quote: so prouide for her, as she may haue wherewithall to maintaine her selfe, and to liue according to that place whereunto by him she is aduanced

items.text: Declare thy mind and will plainly before thou diest, that thy wife be not circumvented of what thou intendest her.
items.quote: declared their minde and will before they die, lest their wiues should be circumuented and defrauded of that which they intended them

items.text: Commend thy wife to some faithful friend to be an helper unto her, as Christ commended his mother to John.
items.quote: request some faithfull friend in his steed to be an helper vnto her; (as Christ commended his mother vnto his disciple Iohn)

items.text: Be diligent, thrifty, and provident, cutting off needless expenses, lest thou leave thy wife in debt or poverty.
items.quote: for their wiues sake be some-what the more diligent, thrifty, and prouident, and cut off many vnnecessary expences

items.text: Do not by fawning or forcing draw thy wife to part with her jointure or inheritance, nor leave her worse than before marriage.
items.quote: draw their wiues to yeeld up that interest they haue in money, goods, house or land by ioynter, inheritance, or any other way, and yet make them no sufficient recompence

items.text: Be subject to the laws for conscience sake, and leave thy wife at least her thirds as a testimony of love and care.
items.quote: Besides an husband ought (though the law forced him not) to leaue at least the thirds to his wife

items.text: Make thy will in timely manner, and do not put it off hoping thy wife may die before thee; lest God disappoint thy hopes.
items.quote: put off the making of their wills of purpose that they might not put in their wiues thirds

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 65 · Of the freenesse of husbands loue. … Of husbands vnkindnesse.

items.text: Love your wife freely, not for her beauty, wealth, or prospects, but solely because she is your wife.
items.quote: husbands should loue their wiues, though there were nothing in wiues to moue them so to doe, but only that they are their wiues

items.text: Do what you can to make your wife worthy of love, dwelling with her according to knowledge.
items.quote: doe what lieth in their power, to make their wiues worthy of loue: thus will it be in truth said, that they dwell with their wiues according to knowledge

items.text: Love your wife with pure, chaste love, keeping the marriage bed undefiled; do not let your affection become wanton lust.
items.quote: husbands must learne so to be affected towards their wiues as may stand with holinesse, and chastitie

items.text: Prefer her good above your own interests, and be ready even to lay down your life for her soul's good if necessity requires.
items.quote: we ought to lay downe our liues for the brethren: therefore by iust consequence for our wiues

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 1 · Of the generall Heads of Childrens duties. … Of Childrens loue to their Parents.

items.text: Love your parents with a warm, constant affection, answering their love to you.
items.quote: loue deserueth loue: and most vnworthy are they to be loued, who cannot loue againe.

items.text: Fear your parents with a filial fear, as under their authority.
items.quote: The authoritie of parents requireth feare in children.

items.text: Reverence your parents, giving them due honor and respect.
items.quote: The Authoritie of parents requireth of children — Reuerence.

items.text: Obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
items.quote: Children obey your Parents in the Lord: for this is right.

items.text: Repay your parents' care and provision by providing for their needs.
items.quote: Their Necessitie requireth Recompence.

items.text: Bury your deceased parents' bodies with decency.
items.quote: Their Body with decency must be buried.

items.text: Maintain your deceased parents' good name and credit with honor.
items.quote: Their Credit with honour must be maintained.

items.text: Do not hate, despise, mock, or curse your parents.
items.quote: hatred and despight of parents: a vice more then monstrous, and vnnaturall. From thence commeth mocking and cursing of parents.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 27 · Of childrens actiue obedience. … Of childrens disobedience to their parents commandements.

items.text: Obey your parents' lawful commandments: come when they call, go where they send, attend upon them, and faithfully discharge any business they commit to you.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Domesticall Duties, Treatise 5, Section 27
items.quote: What lawfull commandements soeuer parents giue to their children, they must be ready to the vttermost of their power to obey.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 5 · Of a childes reuerend framing his speech to his parent. … Of the vices in children contrary to the forenamed reuerence in speech.

items.text: Give your parents honorable titles: call your father 'Father' and your mother 'Mother,' and do not be ashamed to do so in public.
items.quote: No title can be more honourable then that which is most proper and vsuall, Father to the one parent, and Mother to the other.

items.text: Speak few words before your parents, only on just occasion; if they are unwilling to hear more, hold your peace.
items.quote: vsing few words before their parents: and those few not without iust occasion

items.text: Speak meekly and humbly to your parents; do not answer as their equal or give word for word.
items.quote: By meeke and humble speeches.

items.text: Choose a fit season to speak to your parents: not when they are busy, in company, or angry.
items.quote: By obseruing a fit opportunity: as when parents are not seriously busied, or in company, or in passion.

items.text: Answer your parents readily and willingly when they call or speak to you; tell them everything they ought to know.
items.quote: By a present, ready, willing, pleasing answer, when by their parents they shall be spoken vnto.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 60 · Of neglecting to maintaine their wiues.

items.text: Help and succour her as your own body, not as you would any other.
items.quote: helpe and succour their wiues

items.text: Do not suffer seducers to come to her and deceive her, but guard her from them.
items.quote: suffering them to come and deceiue their wiues

items.text: Seek after her when she wanders, as Christ seeks the lost sheep until he finds it.
items.quote: seeketh after the lost sheepe vntill he finde it

items.text: Do not carelessly pass over ill reports against her, for her disgrace is your own dishonor.
items.quote: the discredit of a wife will turne to the mans dishonour

items.text: When she is misused, do not turn away or smile at it, but take her part and right her wrongs.
items.quote: the head is as much affected with a wrong done to the bodie, as to it selfe

items.text: Do not suffer children or servants to insult her, but uphold her authority as joint governor of the house.
items.quote: suffer both children and seruants to insult ouer them

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 10 · Of the vices contrary to childrens reuerend gesture towards their parents. … Of childrens obedience.

items.text: Rise up and go to meet your parents when they come, rather than keeping your seat.
items.quote: they can suffer their parents to come to them, and they abide in their place and not stirre to meet them.

items.text: Do not disdain to stand bare-headed in your parents' presence, even when others are present.
items.quote: thinke much to stand bare-headed any while in their parents presence.

items.text: Do not be over-familiar with your parents, toying and giggling on every light occasion, for it disgraces them.
items.quote: Wantonnesse and boldnesse, when children are ouer-familiar with their parents: toying and gigling vpon euery light occasion.

items.text: Do not be so ambitious for place that you would go above your parents; rather debase yourself below your inferiors than exalt yourself above your parent.
items.quote: when children are so ambitiously desirous of place... they will be aboue their parents.

items.text: Ask your parents' blessing; do not think it fit only for young children, but seek it as a benefit.
items.quote: they little consider the benefit of a parents blessing.

items.text: Obey your parents, for obedience is the surest evidence of the honor you give them, and without it reverence is mere mockery.
items.quote: Reuerence without obedience is a meere mockage, nothing at all acceptable.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 29 · Of an husbands pressing his authoritie in weighty matters. … Of neglecting reproofe.

items.text: Use your authority in weighty matters so that it may be better regarded and show your love to her.
items.quote: To vse a mans authoritie about weightie matters, matters of moment, maketh it to haue such weight in it, as it will much better be regarded

items.text: Add just and weighty reasons to your commands, so that she may discern their lawfulness and necessity.
items.quote: it is behouefull that an husband adde to his commandement iust & weightie reasons

items.text: Command rarely, not too frequently, lest your authority be blunted and fail when most needed.
items.quote: his commandements must be Rare, not too frequent.

items.text: Command by entreaty rather than peremptorily, following Paul's example of entreating for love's sake.
items.quote: By way of intreating, not too peremptorie.

items.text: Reprove your wife for her sins when occasion offers, as a means to draw her from sin and death.
items.quote: he should reproue her: for this is an especiall meanes to draw her from those sinnes

items.text: Yield to your husband's just commands in weighty matters, recognizing they are for your good.
items.quote: a wife will either be brought to yeeld unto that which is commanded, or to condemne her selfe for not yeelding

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 61 · Of an husbands first beginning to loue his wife. … Of husbands dissimulation.

items.text: Begin first to love her, and let your love provoke her to love, as Christ first loved his church.
items.quote: Thus must an husband first begin to loue his wife.

items.text: Love her in truth and in deed, not only in word or with outward show.
items.quote: So must husbands loue their wiues in truth and in deed.

items.text: Be a guide to her; go before her in good works, and by your example instruct and incite her to do her duty.
items.quote: he should be to his wife, a guide... by his example to instruct, and incite her to doe her dutie.

items.text: Provide for her things requisite, and trust her with what is fitting, as part of loving her in deed.
items.quote: trust them with nothing, nor prouide for them things requisite

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 16 · Of parents consent to the mariage of their children.

items.text: Get your parents' consent before you marry; do not marry without or against their will.
items.quote: children ought to haue their parents consent vnto their mariage

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 38 · Of well ordering reproofe in the manner thereof,

items.text: Reprove her rarely, only upon urgent and necessary occasion; do not continually find fault with her.
items.quote: Reproofes therefore must be — Rare.

items.text: Reprove her in a spirit of meekness.
items.quote: a reproofe must be giuen in meeknesse

items.text: Reprove her in secret, when alone with her, not before others.
items.quote: When an husband is alone with his wife, then is the fittest season for reproofe:

items.text: If she disregards a secret rebuke, reprove her before one or two trustworthy friends, preferably her relatives, but never before anyone of the household under her governance.
items.quote: Take one or two more, namely wise, graue, faithfull friends, if it may be, of her kindred... but by no meanes before any of the house vnder her gouernment.

items.text: Even when her fault is public, manifest dislike of the sin without diminishing her honor before the household.
items.quote: Wisely he must so manifest his dislike of her fault, as he no way impaire her honour

items.text: Use soft and gentle words in reproof, as a gentle admonition rather than a sharp rebuke, without reviling or insulting.
items.quote: his reproofe must be so ordered, as it may seeme to be rather a gentle admonition, then a sharpe rebuke.

items.text: If her sin is heinous, you may use some sharpness, but never bitterness or evil language.
items.quote: in an extraordinary case some sharpnesse may be vsed... but yet this sharpnesse must not be made bitter by any euill language.

items.text: Never rebuke your wife when you are in passion; first bring yourself under control.
items.quote: lay it downe for a rule, neuer to rebuke their wiues when they are in passion.

items.text: Do not reprove her while she is in passion; wait until both are calm.
items.quote: forbeare this duty of reprouing his wife euen when she is in passion.

items.text: Maintain her reputation before children and servants, as she is joint governor with you over them.
items.quote: because she is with him a ioynt gouernour of them, he ought by all meanes to maintaine her reputation before them.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 7 · Of childrens reuerend speeches of their parents. … Of a childs reuerend cariage to his parent.

items.text: Speak of them with reverence both before their faces and behind their backs.
items.quote: their speech not only to them before their faces, but also of them behinde their backes, must be so framed

items.text: Speak nothing of them that you would be loath should come to their ears.
items.quote: let children speake nothing of their parents that they would be loath should come to their parents eare.

items.text: Speak of those things which tend to their commendation, that so you may honour them.
items.quote: let them speake of those things which most tend to their commendation, that so they may honour their parents

items.text: Bury their other matters in silence; interpret doubtful things in the better sense; extenuate evident faults; and sharply reprove those who slander them.
items.quote: Let other things be buried in silence... interpret in the better sense things doubtfull, and, so farre as they may, extenuate things euident, and sharply reproue them that slander their parents.

items.text: Do not disclose their infirmities, spread untruths about them, or mock or curse them.
items.quote: Contrary to that kinde of blessing is discouering of parents infirmities, and broaching vntruths of them, and mocking and cursing them expresly condemned.

items.text: If your parent is coming to you, hasten to meet him.
items.quote: If a parent be comming to a childe, and the childe obserue it, let him haste to meet his parent.

items.text: Perform child-like obeisance to them, such as uncovering your head, bending your knee, bowing your body, or standing up, as befits your age and sex.
items.quote: Let such child-like obeisance be performed as becommeth the age and sex, either in going to, remaining before, or going from a parent: as vncouering the head, bending the knee, bowing the body, standing vp.

items.text: Order your countenance and gesture soberly and modestly in your parent's presence.
items.quote: Let the countenance, and gesture of the body be so soberly and modestly ordered in the presence of the parent.

items.text: Give your parent the upper place and hand; if you are above him, come below him.
items.quote: Let the vpper place, and hand be giuen to parents: and if occasionally a childe be aboue his parent, let him come below him.

items.text: Even if you are more wealthy or honourable than your parent, when alone with him revere him rather than take the upper hand.
items.quote: when they are alone, the childe must rather reuerence the father.

items.text: Ask your parents' blessing according to the custom of the time and place where you live.
items.quote: According to the custome of the time and place wherein they liue, let children aske their parents blessing.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 20 · Of obiections for childrens marrying without parents consent, answered. … Of childrens forbearing to dispose any of their parents goods without consent.

items.text: Do not marry without your parents' consent; you are not your own, but their inheritance, and you cannot give yourself in marriage any more than you can give away their goods.
items.quote: a childe therefore may no more marry for himselfe without consent of parents, then alienate his parents goods for himselfe.

items.text: While you live in your parents' house, do not dispose of any of their goods without their consent; you are as a servant, not yet the lord of the property.
items.quote: children though liuing in their parents house, ought not without their parents consent to dispose their goods

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 14 · Of the vnlawfulnesse of childrens entring into religious orders without consent of parents. … Of the vnlawfulnesse of childrens trauelling, and binding themselues prentises without consent of parents.

items.text: Obey them: do not enter any religious order without their consent, nor against their mind and good liking.
items.quote: children may ... enter into religious orders, not only without consent, but also against the minde and good like of their parents.

items.text: If they are in such necessity that they cannot live without your help, do not forsake them; give them succour as the law of God requires.
items.quote: if parents be in such necessitie, as they cannot liue without their childrens helpe, their children may not by entring into any religious order forsake their parents.

items.text: When they need your help, do not think prayer alone suffices; endeavor to aid them as you are able.
items.quote: To pray for that which a man indeuoureth not to doe, when he may doe it, is a plaine mocking of God.

items.text: Do not travel abroad or go seeking your fortune without their consent, lest you bring grief upon them.
items.quote: such children as trauell, and seeke their fortunes (as they speake) without consent of parents, like the Prodigall childe.

items.text: Do not bind yourself as an apprentice or enter into any covenant without their knowledge and consent.
items.quote: a custome in this land more vsuall then lawfull, for children to binde themselues prentises without consent of parents.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 3 · Of a childes feare of his parent. … Of a childes Reuerence in refraining speech before his parent, and in hearkening to his parent.

items.text: Hold your parent in honorable esteem, and let that esteem produce an awed respect for him.
items.quote: a childes awfull respect of his parent

items.text: In all things endeavor to please your parent, and be loath to offend him.
items.quote: a desire and indeauour in all things to please the parent, and on the other side a loathnesse to offend him.

items.text: Do not hold a base or vile esteem of your parent, even if he is poor, unlearned, or subject to infirmities.
items.quote: that base and vile esteeme of parents, which is in the heart of many children: especially if parents be poore, of low degree, vnlearned, ignorant, or subiect to any infirmities.

items.text: Recognize that your parent stands in God's place and is the means, under God, of your very being.
items.quote: how they are in Gods stead, and a meanes vnder God of their childrens being

items.text: In your parent's presence, keep silence: do not speak until he gives leave, and break off your speech when he enters.
items.quote: forbearing to speake (especially when parents are speaking, or till parents giue leaue to their children to speake,) and in breaking off speech, when parents come

items.text: Listen patiently to your parent's speech, enduring it even if it is long and tedious.
items.quote: Though parents in their speech seeme to be long and tedious, yet must children indure it.

items.text: Do not be saucy or overbold in speech, prating on without regard to your parent's presence.
items.quote: sawcinesse and ouermuch boldnesse in children, when, without due respect of their parents presence, they will be prating

items.text: Do not fret, murmur, or walk away while your parent is speaking, even if his speech is long.
items.quote: fretting and murmuring against parents (if at least their speech be any whit long) and flinging or slinking away before they haue done.

items.text: Do not interrupt or hinder your parent's admonition or instruction by your talking or impatience.
items.quote: if children by their loquacitie, or impatiencie hinder or interrupt their parents speech when they are giuing any admonition or instruction

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 45 · Of childrens care to burie their parents being dead. … Of the decency wherewith children ought to see their parents buried.

items.text: See to it that your parents' bodies are buried with decency and honor befitting their station, according to the custom of the church.
items.quote: to bring the bodies of their parents deceased, with such decencie and honour, as may be answerable to the place and reputation wherein they liued.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 33 · Of Childrens submission to their parents correction. … Of childrens conforming their iudgements to their parents.

items.text: Bear patiently the correction your parent gives you.
items.quote: By bearing patiently the correction which his parent shall giue him.

items.text: Amend readily the fault for which you are justly corrected.
items.quote: By amending readily that for which he is iustly corrected.

items.text: Give your parent rest and delight by amending the fault for which you have been corrected.
items.quote: giue this rest and delight to his parent by amending the fault for which he is corrected

items.text: Consider that your parent corrects you out of love and for your good.
items.quote: The cause is the loue he beareth to his childe. The end which he aimeth at, is his childes good.

items.text: Do not disdain your parent's correction nor be obstinate, growing worse despite it.
items.quote: Disdaine, when children scorne to be corrected... Obstinacie, when they will be no whit bettered thereby, but still runne on in their leaud courses.

items.text: Obey your parents in all things, as far as you do not transgress God's commandments.
items.quote: Children obey your parents in all things. So farre forth as children transgresse not any of Gods commandements in obeying their parents, they ought to obey.

items.text: Bring your judgment and will to your parent's, thinking what he appoints is meet and convenient for you.
items.quote: labour to bring their iudgement and will to the bent of their parents: to thinke that meet and conuenient for them to doe which their parents will haue them doe.

items.text: Do not think you can better discern what is fit for you than your parents.
items.quote: who thinke they can better discerne what is fit and meete for themselues, then their parents.

items.text: In calling, marriage, apparel, and allowance, accept your parent's judgment as meetest for you.
items.quote: children are to thinke that kinde of calling, that particular match, that apparrell, and that allowance to be meetest for them, which their parents thinke meete.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 52 · Of an husbands prouiding for his wife according to his estate and abilitie. … Of husbands allowing their wiues to bestow on others, as they see good occasion.

items.text: Maintain her in as good an estate and condition as yourself; marriage has advanced her to your dignity and made her partner of all your goods.
items.quote: an husband ought to maintaine his wife in as good an estate and fashion as himselfe

items.text: Allow her, if she has discretion, to order her own necessities as she thinks best.
items.quote: he must suffer her to order such things as are needfull for her selfe according to her best liking

items.text: Do not stint her allowance as you would a child's or servant's; give her more plentiful provision than them.
items.quote: These may haue their portions stinted vnto them, which is vnmeet to be done to a wife.

items.text: Do not make her drudge at home and go meanly while you are brave and feast abroad, so that she is ashamed to be seen with you.
items.quote: Many husbands make their wiues drudge at home, fare hardly, and goe meanly; who are themselues braue in apparrell

items.text: Give her something of her own to bestow on children, servants, and the poor, and exhort her to use it for charity.
items.quote: let his wife haue some stocke, and portion of her owne, free to her selfe to dispose as she seeth good

items.text: Praise her when she uses well what you have given her, as the husband of the virtuous woman did.
items.quote: Her husband praiseth her.

items.text: Do not give away what your husband has reserved to himself without his consent.
items.quote: If she giue of that which her husband hath reserued to himselfe, as her giuing is vnlawfull

items.text: Stretch out your hand to the poor and reach out to the needy, as you have means.
items.quote: she stretcheth out her hand to the poore, and reacheth forth her hands to the needie

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 64 · Of Gods promise mouing children to obey their parents.

items.text: Obey and honor your parents, for this is the first commandment with promise.
items.quote: an expresse charge to honour their parents

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 19 · Of husbands too much strictnesse towards their wiues. … Of an husbands mildnesse.

items.text: Do not stand upon the uttermost step of your authority; be content with the duty she performs, not exacting more and more.
items.quote: stand vpon the vttermost step of their authoritie, and yeeld no more to a wife then to any other inferiour

items.text: Do not burden your wife with unwelcome guests or frequent, unseasonable tasks; consider her weakness in sickness, childbearing, or nursing.
items.quote: grieuous by bringing such guests into the house as they know cannot be welcome to them: burdensome by tu frequent, and vnseasonable inuiting of guests

items.text: Do not hold your wife under as a child or servant; do not restrain her from doing anything without your express consent.
items.quote: hold their wiues vnder as if they were children or seruants, restraining them from doing any thing without their knowledge and particular expresse consent

items.text: Do not be over-busy in prying into every household affair; give your wife opportunity to exercise her wisdom and care as your helper.
items.quote: ouer busie in prying into euery businesse of the house, and will haue their hand in all

items.text: Do not be overly suspicious of your wife or over-strict in taking account; trust her fidelity rather than servants.
items.quote: ouer suspicious of their wiues, and thereupon ouer strickt in taking account of them

items.text: Commend and reward your wife for what she has done well, without flattery or stirring envy or lust in others.
items.quote: wisely commend and reward what she hath well done

items.text: Perform your duty to your wife mildly and gently; handle her tenderly as glass, remembering her weakness, and be an example of gentleness.
items.quote: mildly he must performe that duty which he oweth to her

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 26 · Of an husbands manner of commanding his wife any thing. … Of an husbands forbearing to presse things vnbeseeming a wiues place.

items.text: Season all your commands to her with mildness, not harshness.
items.quote: must all be seasoned with mildnesse

items.text: Do not command her to do what is unlawful or forbid her what is lawful, lest you set your authority against God's.
items.quote: to bring his owne authority into opposition with Gods: in which case he bringeth his wife into this strait, either to reiect Gods commandement or his.

items.text: Respect her conscience; do not force her to act against what she believes Scripture requires, even if you disagree.
items.quote: The conscience is subiect to God alone: if it be forced it will be a fearefull horror, and a very hell in that party whose conscience is forced.

items.text: If her scruple is mistaken, first patiently instruct her and show her error from Scripture, not by coercion.
items.quote: He must first labour to resolue her conscience by a plaine discouery of her error; which is a true and a great token of loue.

items.text: If after instruction she still cannot yield out of weakness in a matter of small consequence, forbear pressing her conscience.
items.quote: an husband ought so farre to manifest his mildnesse as to forbeare to presse her conscience

items.text: If her refusal is obstinacy in a weighty matter, maintain your authority and by lawful means bring her to yield.
items.quote: In case of obstinacy it is very expedient that an husband stand vpon his power to maintaine his authority

items.text: Do not require her to do anything unbefitting a wife or shameful; guard her honor.
items.quote: Things vnbeseeming the place of a wife are dishonourable vnto her

items.text: Do not burden her with trivial commands; reserve your commands for matters of weight and moment.
items.quote: Such as are of weight and moment

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 12 · Of childrens forbearing to doe things without consent of parents. … Of consent of parents for childrens entring into a calling.

items.text: Do nothing without your parents' consent while you are under their government.
items.quote: A forbearance from doing things without consent of parents.

items.text: Do whatever your parents require of you.
items.quote: A performance of such things as parents will haue done.

items.text: Seek your parents' consent before choosing and entering a calling.
items.quote: children ought to haue the consent of their parents in making choise of their calling

items.text: Seek your parents' consent before making marriage.
items.quote: Making mariage

items.text: Seek your parents' consent before disposing of goods.
items.quote: Disposing of goods

items.text: Seek your parents' consent in ordering your apparel.
items.quote: Ordering apparell

items.text: Seek your parents' consent before making vows to God.
items.quote: Making vowes

items.text: Train up your children well, for God has laid this charge upon you.
items.quote: God hath laid it as a charge upon parents, that they should see their children well trained up

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 58 · Of an husbands protecting his wife from danger. … Of an husbands maintaining his wife against children of a former venter, and seruants.

items.text: Protect her from all danger; be to her a saviour, as Christ is to the church.
items.quote: protect her from things hurtfull

items.text: Prevent dangers she may fall into, and recover her when she has fallen into them.
items.quote: To preuent... such dangers as his wise is like to fall into. To recouer her out of such as she is fallen into.

items.text: Keep away from her all who would seduce her in the faith; do not let them harbour in your house.
items.quote: keepe them away that they come not at her, or to put them away from her so soone as he can: he may not suffer them to harbour in his house.

items.text: If she is drawn or taken from home, seek her and bring her back.
items.quote: he must seeke her, and fetch her againe... or cause her... to be brought home againe.

items.text: Maintain her good name; if she is unjustly slandered, defend her reputation as your own, even after her death.
items.quote: If she be vniustly slandered, he is to maintaine her credit and reputation as much as his owne.

items.text: Defend her against harm from strangers, and also from children and servants within the house.
items.quote: he must be a tower of defence to protect her... not only against strangers... but also against children and seruants.

items.text: Uphold her honor against stubborn children, especially stepchildren; use your fatherly authority to keep them in awe.
items.quote: the countenance of a father for the most part keepeth most in awe... maintaine her honour against them.

items.text: Restrain your children from rising up against their mother; let them not be insolent toward her.
items.quote: Children growne to yeeres... will be ready to rise vp against their mother... the countenance of a father... keepeth most in awe.

items.text: Suffer not a servant to be insolent toward your wife; if he will not submit, put him away.
items.quote: his seruant might haue a priuiledge... yet when she waxed insolent against her mistresse... he cast her out of his house.

items.text: If she is wronged by the children, right her; but if she wrongs them, do not support her wrong; instead labor to pacify her and, if necessary, place the children elsewhere to preserve peace.
items.quote: if she be the wrong-doer, he may by no meanes boulster her vp against his children... put them forth to be brought vp in some other place... Peace and vnitie betwixt man and wife must of all other be kept inuiolable.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 12 · Of mothers giuing sucke to their owne children.

items.text: Nurse your own children yourself, as far as you are able.
items.quote: they are bound to giue sucke to their owne children

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 30 · Of childrens obedience to their parents instruction. … Of childrens readinesse to amend what is iustly reproued by their parents.

items.text: Obey your parents' wholesome instructions for the well ordering of your life.
items.quote: Such wholsome instructions as parents giue their children for the well ordering of their cariage, children ought conscionably to obey

items.text: Patiently bear your parents' reproofs, whether they be mild or bitter, just or unjust.
items.quote: This patience in a childe must be manifested to his parent, whether his reproofe be milde or bitter, iust or vniust

items.text: Amend what your parents justly reprove in you, for otherwise your patience is mere dissimulation and mockery.
items.quote: If a childe be iustly for his fault reproued by his parents, both conscience toward God, and obedience to his parent, requireth that he readily redresse that which is amisse

items.text: If you answer a parent's reproof, do it mildly, reverently, and seasonably, never peremptorily crossing or thwarting them.
items.quote: so he doe it mildly, reuerendly, and seasonably: not too peremptorily crossing or thwarting his parent

items.text: Aim to bring joy and comfort to your parents by observing their instruction, as a wise son makes a glad father.
items.quote: a wise sonne maketh a glad father. Now this is a thing which children ought to aime at, to reioyce their parents heart

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 18 · Of husbands forbearing to exact all that they may.
