items.text: Accept her obedience in such a way that it comes from her own voluntary disposition, not from force.
items.quote: he ought so to frame his cariage towards her, as that obedience which she performeth, may rather come from her owne voluntary disposition, from a free conscience to God-wards

items.text: Do not exact from your wife whatever she would owe if exacted; observe what is lawful, needful, convenient, expedient, and what she is willing to do.
items.quote: Husbands ought not to exact of their wiues, whatsoeuer wiues ought to yeeld vnto if it be exacted.

items.text: Do not move her from place to place without her good liking unless an urgent calling forces you.
items.quote: remoue her from place to place, and carrie her from that place where she is well setled without her good liking

items.text: Do not be burdensome to her with guests; tender her in the care and pains of entertaining them.
items.quote: yet ought not he to be grieuous and burdensome therein vnto her: the greatest care and pains for entertaining guests lyeth on the wife

items.text: Yield your consent to her requests readily, even offering it voluntarily if she is bashful.
items.quote: he ought to be ready and free in yeelding his consent... if she be bashfull and backward in asking consent, he ought voluntarily of himselfe to offer it

items.text: Give her a general consent to order household affairs; refer to her discretion the decking of the house, provision of food, ruling maidservants, and bringing up young children.
items.quote: A generall consent is especially requisite for ordering of houshold affaires... husbands ought to referre matters to their ordering, and not restraine them in euery particular matter

items.text: Put trust in your wife in household affairs, giving her greater liberty than children, friends, or servants.
items.quote: he ought together with his generall consent put trust in his wife... To his wife... greater liberty, and licence must be giuen

items.text: Exercise general oversight over all household affairs; allow nothing unlawful or unseemly, for the principal charge lies on you.
items.quote: That he haue a generall ouersight in all, and so interpose his authority as he suffer nothing that is vnlawfull or vnseemly to be done by his wife

items.text: Obey your husband, yielding what you owe, but let it be from a willing heart.
items.quote: As a wiues reuerence so also her obedience must be answered with her husbands courtesie

items.text: Go with your husband and dwell where he thinks meet.
items.quote: the wife ought to goe with her husband, and dwell where he thinkes meet

items.text: Cheerfully entertain the guests your husband brings into the house.
items.quote: she ought cheerefully to entertaine what guests he bringeth into the house

items.text: Guide the house and order its affairs; this charge is laid upon you.
items.quote: it is a charge laid vpon wiues to guide the house

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 12 · Of mothers giuing sucke to their owne children.

items.text: Nurse your own child yourself; do not put it out to a wet nurse except in necessity.
items.quote: They are directly giuen for the childs food that commeth out of the wombe

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 24 · Of the sinne of children in purloining and wasting their parents goods. … Of childrens forbearing to binde themselues to doe any thing against their parents consent.

items.text: Do not murmur against their restraint of your spending; accept their allowance and your subjection.
items.quote: being through the watchfull eie and prouident care of their parents restrained from ouerlauish spending, or from laying out any thing with their owne hands, they murmure against that restraint.

items.text: Do not privately take or purloin any of their goods, money, or wares; it is theft.
items.quote: Some priuily take away and purloine what goods, money, wares or any thing else they can come by of their parents.

items.text: Do not wastefully spend your portion or run into debt so that they must pay or suffer by law.
items.quote: Others riotously spend their portion, like the prodigall childe, and runne into debt, and so make their parents either to pay it, or to leaue them to the law.

items.text: Do not cunningly seek to gain possession of all they have while they live or before they willingly resign it.
items.quote: being come to yeeres, and their parents growne old, seeke to defeat their parents of all they haue, and to bring their parents vnder them.

items.text: Dress only as they approve: not against their mind, above their ability, or unbefitting their place and calling.
items.quote: apparell themselues both against the minde, and also aboue the ability, and vnbeseeming the place and calling of their parents.

items.text: Do not bind yourself by vow, oath, or other means to do anything without your parents' consent.
items.quote: The law giueth the parent power to disanull his childes vow. It is therefore a childes dutie to abstaine from vowing without his parents consent.

heading: Treatise 4 · The fourth Treatise. Husbands Particular Duties. · Section 23 · Of husbands bitternesse. … Of an husbands manner of instructing his wife.

items.text: Love her and be not bitter toward her.
items.quote: Loue your wiues and be not bitter vnto them.

items.text: Call her by mild and kind titles such as wife, spouse, or love; avoid names that set her too high or too low.
items.quote: The titles wherewith he calleth her... must all be mixed with mildnesse.

items.text: When you instruct her, do it with meekness and adapt your teaching to her understanding.
items.quote: Instruct with meekenesse... Note the vnderstanding and capacity of thy wife, and accordingly fit thine instructions.

items.text: Instruct her in private between you two, so that her ignorance is not exposed before others.
items.quote: Instruct her in priuate betwixt thy selfe and her, that so her ignorance may not be blazed forth.

items.text: When instructing her, instruct children and servants in her presence so that she may learn from it.
items.quote: In the family so instruct children and seruants when she is present, as she may learne knowledge thereby.

items.text: Mix your precepts with sweet and weighty persuasions as proofs of great love.
items.quote: Together with thy precepts mixe sweet and pithy perswasions, which are testimonies of great loue.

items.text: Do not be harsh or rough in instructing; do not force deep mysteries on her or expose her ignorance to others.
items.quote: harsh and rough manner of instructing... thrust into their wiues heads... proclaime their ignorance before children, seruants, and strangers.

items.text: Give commandments and reproofs with mildness.
items.quote: The commandements which he layeth vpon her... the reproofes wherewith he checketh her, must all be mixed with mildnesse.

items.text: Speak of her behind her back with mildness.
items.quote: Whether an husbands speech be... of her behinde her backe, it must be sweetned with mildnesse.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 47 · Of childrens paying their parents debts after their death. … Of childrens imitating their parents good example.

items.text: Pay the debts of your deceased parents, as far as you are able, especially if you inherit their estate, to preserve their credit.
items.quote: If the estate of parents, their goods or lands come to their children, their dutie is to pay their debts, so farre as they can

items.text: Take care of reports made of them after their death; suppress ill rumors and do not speak ill of them.
items.quote: what children doe for their parents credit in absence behinde their backes, they must much more doe when they are dead

items.text: Imitate their good example and walk in their steps, so that their blessed memory may be kept fresh.
items.quote: it is an especiall meanes to maintaine and continue this their credit, for children to walke in their steps

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 20 · Of Parents care to giue a fit name to their childe at his Baptisme. … Of Parents care in bringing their children to be baptized in due season.

items.text: Give your child a fit name at baptism, one that is holy, sober, and suitable, that the name may testify of his baptism and stir him to virtue.
items.quote: Parents be carefull in giuing a fit name

items.text: Bring your child to be baptized in the first season, not deferring beyond eight days, to honor God and secure the child's spiritual good.
items.quote: not meet for Christians to defer the baptizing of their children beyond eight dayes

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 38 · Of childrens sinne in yeelding to their parents against God. … Of infirmities whereunto parents are subiect.

items.text: Obey them only in the Lord; never sin to please them, for their authority is subordinate to God's.
items.quote: In comparison of Christ Father and mother must be hated.

items.text: Repay them for their kindness, care, and cost according to your ability, especially in their time of need.
items.quote: children indeauour as much as in them lieth, to repay what they can for their parents kindnesse, care, and cost towards them

items.text: Bear with their natural infirmities and cover them as far as you can.
items.quote: the dutie of children is both to beare with them, and also to couer them so farre as they can

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 18 · Of the reasons to moue parents to see their children baptized. … Of Parents procuring their children to be rightly baptized.

items.text: Have your children baptized by a minister of the word with water, in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, applying the water to their bodies at least the face, and do it seasonably.
items.quote: It is parents duty to get them that euidence.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 17 · Of the equity of the point, and reasons why children should haue their parents consent vnto their marriage. … Of the sinne of Children in marrying without their parents consent.

items.text: Do not marry without your parents' notice and consent, for by marriage you leave them and transfer your submission to a spouse.
items.quote: By mariage children are put from their parents... children should haue notice of that kind of leauing them, and consent thereto.

items.text: If your parents urge a match you cannot love and there is no just exception, labor with all your might to bend your affection to their will.
items.quote: they ought with the vttermost of their power to endeauour to bring their affection to the bent of their parents will

items.text: Pray earnestly to God to alter your affection and settle it on the one your parents have chosen, unless you see just cause to the contrary.
items.quote: make instant prayer vnto God... that he would be pleased to alter the course of their affection, and to settle it on the party whom their parent hath chosen

items.text: If your parent is negligent in finding you a spouse, do not cast off subjection; instead tell them of a fit match and ask their consent and help.
items.quote: A parents negligence is not a sufficient pretext to make a child cast off that subiection which he oweth to his parent

items.text: Do not lightly esteem your parents' authority by taking a spouse of your own choice, whether secretly or rebelliously against their command.
items.quote: Contrary is the minde and practise of such children as ouer lightly esteeming their parents power, take matches of their owne choice: and that sometimes priuily... rebelliously

items.text: Have a hand in your child's marriage, using your experience and love to guide them to a fit help, for their own good.
items.quote: parents... hauing by much experience better vnderstanding of a meete helpe... the parent should haue a stroake

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 54 · Of the equall respect that children are to beare to both parents. … Of pretences alledged to obey father rather then mother.

items.text: Honor and obey your father; give him equal respect with your mother, and do not neglect or despise him even if your mother is more tender or familiar.
items.quote: Honour thy Father and thy Mother.

items.text: Honor and obey your mother equally with your father; do not despise her for her weakness, tenderness, or lesser power, but see God's image in her and show her reverence even when your father's will prevails in indifferent matters.
items.quote: Yee shall feare euery man his mother, and his father.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 36 · Of childrens yeelding to practise at their parents command, such things as in their iudgements they cannot thinke very meet. … Of the restraint of childrens obedience.

items.text: Yield to your parents' peremptory commands in things indifferent, even if you cannot see them as fit, saying like Peter, 'Nevertheless at thy word I will do this.'
items.quote: in practise they ought to yeeld vnto it, saying to their parents as Peter to the Lord, Neuerthelesse at thy word I will doe this

items.text: With reverence and humility give your reason why something seems unfit, and ask your parent not to press it; but if your parent insists on an indifferent thing, yield.
items.quote: But yet if in things indifferent, parents be otherwise minded then their children, and will haue their children yeeld to them, they must yeeld.

items.text: Do not obey any command that makes you sin; refuse even a parent's command if God forbids it.
items.quote: If therefore parents command their children to doe any thing which the Lord hath forbidden them, they ought not to doe it.

items.text: If your parent forbids you from doing a duty God commands, do it anyway; obey God rather than man.
items.quote: if parents forbid their children the doing of any necessary duty commanded of God, the childe ought to doe it notwithstanding the parents inhibition.

items.text: Listen respectfully to your child's reasons regarding a command, and if it is not necessary, yield to your child rather than press it.
items.quote: parents ought in such a case to yeeld to their children (as Iaakob did.)

items.text: Yield to your husband rather than your father when their commands conflict, for God's law gives your husband the priority.
items.quote: by Gods law a wife is to yeeld to her husband rather then to her father.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 23 · Of parents prouiding things needfull for the life and health of their children. … Of parents too much niggardlinesse, and carelesnesse toward their children.

items.text: Provide all needful things for their life and health: food, clothing, wholesome recreation, and means for recovery when sick; do not withhold due provision out of covetousness.
items.quote: Parents to their power must prouide for their children: else the Apostle counteth them worse then Infidels.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 4 · Of Parents praying for their children. … Of parents endeauouring to be righteous that they may leaue Gods blessing to their children.

items.text: Pray for your children without ceasing, before they are conceived, while they are in the womb, when they are born, throughout their lives, and when you are departing.
items.quote: Pray without ceasing

items.text: Ask your parents' blessing, desiring them to pray for God's blessing on you.
items.quote: childrens asking their parents blessing: which intimateth a desire that parents would pray for Gods blessing on them.

items.text: Endeavor to walk uprightly before God and please him, that your children may inherit God's blessing.
items.quote: Leaue therefore a good memory to thy children rather then much wealth.

items.text: Do not make imprecations against your children, for God may hear them in wrath to your own woe.
items.quote: feare not to make fearefull imprecations against their children? God oft in wrath and vengeance heareth such imprecations to the woe of parent and childe

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 58 · Of childrens subiection to Guardians, Tutors, &c. … Of the equitie whereby children should be moued to obey their parents.

items.text: Submit to your guardians, tutors, and governors, for they bear a parent's charge over you.
items.quote: If by the law children are vnder them, they ought in equitie to be subiect to them.

items.text: Honor your guardians, tutors, and governors as their charge and care deserve.
items.quote: their honour must be answerable to their charge and care.

items.text: Obey your parents, for in obeying them you obey God, since they stand in God's stead.
items.quote: children in obeying their parents, obey God; in refusing to obey them, refuse to obey God.

items.text: Repay your parents' love, pain, care, and cost by giving them the obedience and honor that is their due.
items.quote: the loue which parents beare to children, the paine, paines, care, and cost they haue beene at

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 34 · Of parents teaching their children piety.

items.text: Train them up in true piety: teach them the ordinances of the Lord, and take occasion from their questions to instruct them.
items.quote: Wherefore Parents must traine vp their children in true piety.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 37 · Of instructing children so soone as they are capable.

items.text: Begin to nurture your children as soon as they are capable of any instruction.
items.quote: Parents ought to begin to nurture their children so soone as they are capable of any instruction.

items.text: Hearken to your father's voice; do not become inflexible in evil.
items.quote: Elies sonnes being suffered to goe on in wickednesse till they came to ripenesse of yeeres, would not afterwards harken to the voice of their Father.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 1 · Of the heads of Parents duties. … Of the contraries to loue.

items.text: Love them with a fervent, natural affection, that you may do every duty toward them cheerfully.
items.quote: Loue... fast fixed in the heart of parents towards their children.

items.text: Nourish them with food, clothing, and other necessary provisions.
items.quote: nourish children, namely with food, apparrell, and other like necessaries.

items.text: Bring them up under good discipline and nurture.
items.quote: nurture them, namely with good discipline.

items.text: Instruct them in the ways of God and his Word.
items.quote: instruct them, namely in the waies of God.

items.text: Do not provoke them to wrath by overmuch rigor.
items.quote: Prouoke not your children to wrath.

items.text: Do not be remiss in discipline; avoid over-much remissness.
items.quote: ouer-much-remisnesse.

items.text: Do not let covetousness, lust, vain-glory, superstition, or idolatry quench your natural affection for them.
items.quote: many cleane put it out through couetousnesse, lust, vaine-glory, superstition, idolatry.

items.text: Do not dote on them excessively; keep the golden mean in love.
items.quote: too much doting vpon children.

items.text: Do not sacrifice your children to idols or devils, nor harm them through superstition or idolatry.
items.quote: sacrificing their children, and offering them vp to deuils.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 61 · Of Gods accepting childrens obedience. … Of the title FIRST giuen to the fift commandement.

items.text: Honor your father and mother, for this is the first commandment with promise, a perpetual and universal law binding all children at all times.
items.quote: Honour thy father and thy mother... this is a commandement, yea the first commandement, and that with promise

items.text: Obey your parents; this duty is not left to your discretion but is a matter of conscience before God.
items.quote: no arbitrary matter left to childrens discretion whether they will obey their parents or no: but a matter whereunto in conscience they are bound

items.text: Repay your parents for their care; this recompense is good and acceptable before God.
items.quote: exhorted children to recompence their parents, he saith, That is good and acceptable before God.

items.text: Continue to honor your parents as long as they live, whatever your age, marriage, or high office.
items.quote: so long as a childe hath a parent, of what age or estate so euer he be, he oweth an honour vnto his parent.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 35 · Of directing parents how to teach their children true pietie.

items.text: Teach them only principles of piety grounded on God's Word.
items.quote: Whatsoeuer principle of pietie, parents doe teach their children, they must be sure that it be grounded on Gods word.

items.text: When they begin to read, have them read the holy Scripture.
items.quote: When children begin to read, let them read the holy Scripture.

items.text: Catechize them daily, little and often, so they learn with delight.
items.quote: Let children be catechised constantly from day to day... precept vpon precept... here a little, and there a little.

items.text: At table and on walks, turn ordinary things to spiritual instruction.
items.quote: at table, by resembling the spirituall food... when they are walking abroad... make spirituall vses.

items.text: Open to them the meaning of the church's ordained rites.
items.quote: Let parents open to their children the mysteries of those outward rites... as of Preaching, Baptising children...

items.text: Tell them of God's great works and the memorials of his deliverances.
items.quote: a declaration of such great and admirable workes as God... especially such workes as haue beene done in their time...

items.text: Put them only to religious masters in religious households.
items.quote: Let religious schoole masters be chosen for children.

items.text: Be a living example of piety before them.
items.quote: Let parents be to their children a good patterne and example in pietie.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 14 · Of the fathers dutie in incouraging his wife to nurse her childe. … Of parents ioynt care about their childrens Baptisme.

items.text: Encourage and help his wife in nursing their child, providing all needful things.
items.quote: incourage his wife, and helpe her with all needfull things for the performance of this dutie

items.text: Nurse her own child unless necessity requires otherwise; do not put the child out to nurse for ease, pride, gain, or pleasure.
items.quote: when no necessity requireth put forth their children to be nursed by others

items.text: Do not forbid his wife to nurse their child, nor grieve her by complaints of trouble, disquiet, or expense.
items.quote: forbid their wiues to nurse their children, or are a griefe to them by their complaints of trouble, disquiet and expence

items.text: See that their children be rightly baptized in due season.
items.quote: Procure that their children be rightly baptized in due season

items.text: Take the chief care for the child's baptism, since he is the principal governor and has the greatest charge.
items.quote: the father is the chiefe and principall Gouernour, and hath the greatest charge: accordingly he ought to haue the greatest care

items.text: If her husband is negligent about the child's baptism, remind him of his duty and stir him up to perform it.
items.quote: if the husband be too backward and negligent, the wife ought so farre as she is able to put him in minde of his dutie therein, and to stirre him vp

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 45 · Of parents cockering their children.

items.text: Correct and reprove them faithfully; do not refuse to give a displeasing word, for neglect offends God and ruins the child.
items.quote: neglect of reproofe is a meanes to make children rude, presumptuous, rebellious

items.text: Do not displease or grieve your parents; honor them with affectionate obedience.
items.quote: they cared not to displease their father, yea to grieue his heart, and vex his soule

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 41 · Of childrens bearing with their parents infirmities. … Of childrens bearing with their parents casuall necessities.

items.text: Bear with your parents' weaknesses, and do not let their infirmities lessen your reverence or duty toward them.
items.quote: Children beare with their parents infirmities when they doe not the lesse reuerendly esteeme their place, or person, nor performe the lesse dutie to them because of their infirmities.

items.text: Pass over your parents' faults and conceal them from others, as love covers a multitude of sins.
items.quote: Children couer their parents infirmities both by passing by them and taking no notice of them, and also by concealing them from others as much as they can.

items.text: When your parents suffer poverty, sickness, or other hardships, do not let these diminish your respect or service to them.
items.quote: In all these, children must beare with their parents, as in the forenamed infirmities; neither lesse reuerendly esteeme of them, nor performe the lesse dutie because of them.

items.text: Treat a needy mother-in-law as you would your own mother, continuing to serve and care for her.
items.quote: Though Naomi were poore, yet Ruth her daughter in law continued to doe a childs dutie and seruice vnto her.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 44 · Of childrens releeuing their parents according to their neede.

items.text: Visit your parents when they are sick.
items.quote: In sicknesse they must visit them, as Ioseph visited his father.

items.text: Comfort your parents in their time of mourning.
items.quote: In time of mourning, they must comfort them, as the children of Iaakob.

items.text: Provide necessary things for your parents when they are in want.
items.quote: In want, they must prouide things needfull for them.

items.text: Protect and preserve your parents in times of danger.
items.quote: In time of danger they must doe what they can for their protection and preseruation.

items.text: If your parents would be left without support after your death, arrange for their care before you die.
items.quote: take what order they can for the well-being of their parents after their owne departure

items.text: Do not let your parents be in need when you have the means to help them.
items.quote: who hauing the goods of this world, suffer their parents to want.

items.text: Do not let your parents live poorly while you live in comfort and luxury.
items.quote: suffer them to liue poorely, and basely, when themselues Diues-like fare delicately, and goe gorgeously attired euery day

items.text: Do not bring your parents to poverty by lavish spending or by urging them to be your sureties.
items.quote: bring their parents to such extremities, as to pouertie by their lauish spending; to prison by importuning them to be their sureties

items.text: Do not cause your parents excessive grief by your evil behavior.
items.quote: to excessiue griefe by their mischieuous practises

items.text: Never strike your parents.
items.quote: what shall we say of such gracelesse children, as dare strike their parents?

items.text: Never murder your parents.
items.quote: father-quellers, and mother-quellers

items.text: Do not consecrate your goods to religious uses while your parents are in need.
items.quote: children by consecrating their substance to the Temple, might be freed from this dutie of recompence to parents

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 31 · Of parents training vp their children to some good calling. … Of parents care in choosing a fit calling for their children.

items.text: Train them up to some good calling.
items.quote: a training vp of children vnto a good calling

items.text: Teach them reading, writing, and principles of learning as groundwork for any calling.
items.quote: Children are to be trained vp in those things which are the ground worke of all callings, as reading, writing, and principles of learning.

items.text: Choose for them a lawful calling, approved by God's word.
items.quote: The calling whereunto children are trained vp must be lawfull, approued by Gods word

items.text: Choose a calling fit for the child's ability and inclination.
items.quote: The calling must be fit for the childe that is trained vp to it

items.text: Among fit callings, prefer the best and most excellent.
items.quote: that which is best and the most excellent is to be preferred

items.text: If they find them fit, train them up to the ministry.
items.quote: traine vp such children as they finde fit, to the great and weighty calling of the ministery

items.text: Ease your parents and, if their need requires, relieve and maintain them.
items.quote: to ease their parents, and (if the need of parents require it) to releeue and maintaine them

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 46 · Of correcting children.

items.text: Correct your child; withhold not correction from him; use the rod as need requires.
items.quote: Chasten thy sonne: correct thy sonne: with-hold not correction from the childe: thou shalt smite him with the rod.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 28 · Of parents teaching their children good manners. … Of parents suffering their children to be rudely brought vp.

items.text: Teach your children good manners and how to order the course of their lives.
items.quote: The nurturing of children before mentioned consisteth 1. In teaching them good manners.

items.text: Train your children up to a good calling.
items.quote: The nurturing of children before mentioned consisteth... 2. In training them vp to a good calling.

items.text: Reverence your parents and other superiors, carrying yourself with respect toward them.
items.quote: precepts of reuerencing our superiours, and carying our selues with respect one to another

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 22 · Of Parents faults in neglecting their childrens Baptisme.

items.text: Have your child baptized; do not deny or hinder the sacrament, for the sin lies on you if you fail to procure it.
items.quote: the sinne lieth on such parents as procure not baptisme for their children: especially at that age when their children cannot gainsay it.

items.text: Baptize your child with water in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, not with other forms or signs.
items.quote: In the name of the Father, and of the Sonne, and of the Holy Ghost.

items.text: Have your child baptized by a lawful minister, God's ambassador, not by heretics, idolaters, lay persons, or women.
items.quote: a lawfull Minister in Gods roome and name, as Gods ambassador, putteth the seale of God to his couenant.

items.text: Bring your child to the church to be baptized before the assembly of saints, not privately with only a few witnesses.
items.quote: it is not the walls of the Church, but the assembly of Saints, that addeth to the honour of the Sacrament.

items.text: Do not put off your child's baptism longer than is meet; prefer the sacrament over worldly circumstances.
items.quote: put off the baptising of their children longer then is meet

items.text: Give your child a fitting Christian name, not heathenish, idolatrous, or ridiculous.
items.quote: care not what heathenish, idolatrous, ridiculous names they giue to their children.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 52 · Of the extremes contrary to a parents lawfull care in prouiding fit callings for his children. … Of parents care in prouiding fit mariages for their children.

items.text: After you have had them well educated, do not leave them to shift for themselves; provide them a fit calling.
items.quote: a carelesse neglect of children after they are well educated, a leauing them to shift for themselues.

items.text: Do not place them in callings unfit for them merely for gain or honor.
items.quote: they care not how fit their children be for the place, so it be a place of gaine and honour.

items.text: Use no unlawful means such as simony or bribery to bring them into callings.
items.quote: by vnlawfull meanes purchase their desires: as, by Simony to procure an ecclesiasticall function (whence oft followeth also periury) or by bribery to procure an office.

items.text: Take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands; provide fit marriages for your children.
items.quote: Take wiues to your sonnes, and giue your daughters to husbands

items.text: Do not marry without your parents' consent.
items.quote: Children may not marry without consent of parents

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 54 · Direction to parents in prouiding mariages. … Of parents prouiding a stocke for callings and mariages of their children.

items.text: Provide a match that is meet: not too near of kin, of contrary religion, too unequal age, or too disparate in estate.
items.quote: the match prouided must not be too neere of kin, of a contrary religion, of too vnequall an age, of too great disparity in estate

items.text: Do not force your child into marriage against their mind; use fair means, and if they will not yield, refer the matter to God.
items.quote: he may not force his childe thereto... asked her consent... a middle course is so to be held, as the parties may willingly with a mutuall consent ioyne themselues together

items.text: Seek out a fit match for your child when need requires; do not let them pass the flower of their age carelessly.
items.quote: parents carelesly let their children passe the floure of their age: and neuer consider whether need require that they should mary or no

items.text: Do not marry your child before they are of years of discretion or able to perform essential duties of marriage, merely for rich matches.
items.quote: through a couetous desire to get great and rich matches for their children, marie them before they be of yeares of discretion to like or dislike, to know what is meet or vnmeet; or able to performe euen the essentiall duties of mariages

items.text: Do not for outward advantage match your child to those who are by nature unfit for marriage: idiots, idolaters, profane persons, or force them into such.
items.quote: for outward aduantages match their children to such as by nature are vnfit for mariage, to ideots, to idolaters, to profane persons, or they care not to whom

items.text: Lay up beforehand a competent portion for your children, so they may be set up in a calling and obtain a fit match.
items.quote: before hand to lay vp some stocke, or competent portion for their children

items.text: Let everything you lay up for your child's portion be justly gotten; lay nothing that is unjustly gotten.
items.quote: iustly they come by that which they lay vp: and lay nothing towards a childs portion which is any way vniustly gotten; for the treasures of wickednesse profit nothing

items.text: Do not covet too much to make your child rich, so that you yourselves live meanly and deprive yourselves of necessaries.
items.quote: couet not too much to make their children rich, and for that purpose liue meanly and basely themselues, yea and depriue themselues of many necessaries

items.text: Let all needful duties of charity to the poor and justice to the Church and commonwealth be performed; do not let laying up for children hinder any of these.
items.quote: all needfull duties of charity to the poore, and of iustice to the Church and common-wealth be performed, and pretext of laying vp for children hinder none of these

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 50 · Of Parents care in prouiding fit callings for their children. … Direction for parents in prouiding callings for their children.

items.text: Provide a fitting calling and place for each child to exercise the gifts he has received by nature or education.
items.quote: Parents ought to prouide fit callings for their children, and fit places for them to exercise the gifts which by nature or education they haue gotten.

items.text: Let the calling match the child's training and ability, so that he may be a crafts-master in it.
items.quote: That such callings be prouided as their children haue beene trained vp vnto, and are in some measure fitted and enabled to performe the duties thereof.

items.text: Use only lawful and honest means in obtaining the calling, so that you may with faith ask God's blessing upon it.
items.quote: such meanes be vsed for prouiding a calling as parents in vsing them may with faith call vpon God for his blessing.

items.text: Provide fit marriages for your children.
items.quote: Prouiding fit mariages for them.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 7 · Of the preposterous course which couetous and vniust parents take for the good of their children. … Of a mothers care ouer her childe while it is in her wombe.

items.text: Have a provident care for your children's good in all times and in all things, both temporal and spiritual.
items.quote: A prouident care for their childrens good. This extendeth it selfe to all times, and to all things.

items.text: Do not by covetous or unjust courses seek to provide for your children.
items.quote: Let not therefore care for children draw thee to any coueteous or vniust courses.

items.text: As soon as you perceive a child conceived in your womb, have especial care of yourself so that the child may be safely brought forth.
items.quote: so soone as she perceiueth a childe to be conceiued in her wombe, ought to haue an especiall care thereof

items.text: Avoid violence of passion, violent motion of body, or distemper of body that may cause abortion or miscarriage.
items.quote: through violence of passion... or through distemper of the bodie... cause any abortion or miscariage

items.text: Do not purposely take things to destroy the child in your womb.
items.quote: they who purposely take things to make away their children in their wombe, are in farre higher degree guiltie of bloud

items.text: Be very tender over your wife when she is with child, and helpful to her in all things needful; do not be careless or deny her things needful.
items.quote: Husbands also in this case must be very tender ouer their wiues, and helpfull to them in all things needfull

items.text: See that your wife observes all needful care for the good of the child in her womb.
items.quote: to shew it belonged to him to see her obserue it

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 25 · Of parents too much lauishnesse and indulgency vpon their children. … Of parents neglect in nurturing children.

items.text: Feed them with ordinary moderate diet, not with dainty foods, lest they become squeamish and unhealthy.
items.quote: If at first children be fed with ordinary moderate diet, they will afterwards both be in better health and liking

items.text: Do not dress them in garish apparel; clothe them modestly, lest you foster vanity.
items.quote: Vanity in apparell doth also much corrupt young children: ... now for parents to pranke them vp, what is it but to blow vp the fire of that vanity

items.text: Do not tend them too tenderly; allow them to grow and endure some hardship.
items.quote: Tending children too cockishly maketh them too long children, and too tender: and oft altereth a good constitution of body.

items.text: Limit their time in sport; train them up to some good calling, for too much play makes them unfit.
items.quote: Too much sport maketh them wilde, rude, vnfit to be trained vp to any good calling, and spendeth their spirits

items.text: Provide good nurture and education, using their reason and capacity, for without it they become like beasts.
items.quote: so ought parents to make vse of those parts and gifts, lest for want of vsing them, in time they be lost

items.text: Do not give them too much liberty; curb them, for too much liberty brings ruin.
items.quote: Contrary to good nurture is too much liberty: which oft bringeth much woe, and vtter ruine upon children

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 36 · Of Parents faults contrary to their dutie of teaching their children piety.

items.text: Care for your children's spiritual life and eternal salvation, not only their food, clothing, and worldly calling.
items.quote: care taken for their spirituall life in this world, or eternall life in the world to come.

items.text: Teach them piety and godliness, not profaneness, pride, riot, lying, or deceit.
items.quote: Many are so farre from teaching piety, as they teach their children profanenesse, pride, riot, lying, deceit, and such like principles of the deuill.

items.text: Ensure they are taught the true religion, and do not entrust them to popish kindred for worldly benefit.
items.quote: commend their children to the education of such kindred [popish], in hope of some temporall benefit.

items.text: Catechize them daily in the Lord's Prayer, the Creed, and the Ten Commandments, in a language they understand.
items.quote: So farre are many from catechising their children and that daily, as they teach them not so much as the Lords praier, the Beleefe, and the ten Commandements.

items.text: Use God's holy rites, his glorious works, and his extraordinary mercies or judgments to instruct them.
items.quote: Few vse the forenamed outward helpes, as the holy rites appointed of God, the great and glorious workes of God, his extraordinary workes of mercy or iudgement, to instruct their children thereby.

items.text: Choose for them schoolmasters who are godly and learned, not profane, popish, or unlearned, even if they are kin or friends.
items.quote: care not to what schoolemaster they put their children, be he profane, or popish, or vnlearned, especially if he be a kinsman.

items.text: Give them a godly example, and do not let your own bad behavior pull down what instruction builds.
items.quote: Their euill example is not only an hinderance to the good instruction of others, but also maketh all their owne counsells to be in vaine.

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 56 · Of the difference of childrens subiection to naturall parents, and to such as only are in the place of parents. … Of childrens subiection to fathers and mothers in law.

items.text: Be subject to your step-father or step-mother as one set over you by God in the place of a parent.
items.quote: Subiection is noted in Christs example

items.text: Revere your step-parent; give them the honor due to those in a parent's place.
items.quote: Reuerence in Moses

items.text: As Ruth recompensed Naomi, render due recompense to your step-parent for their care and kindness.
items.quote: Recompence in Ruths

items.text: Honor your step-parent as you would honor your own natural parent, for in doing so you honor your natural parent.
items.quote: to honour a father, or mother in law, is to honour a naturall parent

items.text: Do not despise your step-parent in heart, grumble at them in speech, or be undutiful in behavior; bear reverend and childlike respect.
items.quote: beare a reuerend, dutifull, and child-like respect

items.text: Overcome natural dislike of a step-parent by conscience and the fear of God, doing what nature cannot.
items.quote: Conscience and religion ought to alter corrupt nature

items.text: Be subject to a step-parent even if he is harsh or unjust, and overcome evil with good.
items.quote: be subiect not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward

items.text: Honor and obey your guardian, tutor, or governor as one in the place of a parent.
items.quote: owe in conscience child-like dutie vnto them

items.text: Reverence and recompense your parent-in-law, as Moses honored Jethro and Ruth cared for Naomi.
items.quote: The respect which Moses beare to his father in law, and Ruth to her mother in law

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 42 · Of adding admonition to instruction. … Of parents reprouing their children.

items.text: Whet instruction upon them often; do not think it enough to tell them what they ought to do, but add admonition and beat it into their hearts.
items.quote: Parents must oft whet instruction vpon their children: they may not thinke it enough to tell their children what they ought to doe, but to instruction they must adde admonition

items.text: Correct them as occasion requires, beginning with reproof, and if need be proceeding to blows.
items.quote: The many good fruits which the holy Ghost noteth to proceed from due reproofe doe shew that it is a dutie whereof parents ought to make conscience

heading: Treatise 5 · The fifth Treatise. Duties of Children. · Section 50 · Of the superstitious dutie enioyned by Papists to children after their parents decease. … Of the aberrations of children in the manner of their obedience.

items.text: Bury your parents' corpse when they die.
items.quote: burying the corps

items.text: Preserve your parents' good name and credit after their death.
items.quote: preseruing the credit of parents

items.text: Do not procure dirges, masses, pardons, releases, or continual prayers to free your parents from purgatory; after death the soul is fixed.
items.quote: procure Diriges, Masses, Pardons, Releases... make continuall prayers to free them out of Purgatory
items.conflict: Contrary to Scripture: no purgatory, prayers for the dead are vain.

items.text: Do not take private revenge for wrongs done to your parents; leave vengeance to God, but execute lawful justice if required.
items.quote: children after their parents death reuenge such wrongs as haue beene done to them in their life time

items.text: Perform your duties to your parents in conscience, for the Lord's sake, not from fear of punishment or hope of reward.
items.quote: Children must so performe their duty to their parents as they would or should performe it to the Lord

items.text: Perform your duties in sincerity, doing them heartily as to the Lord, not in outward show only.
items.quote: Whatsoeuer ye doe, doe it heartily as to the Lord

items.text: Perform your duties cheerfully, with a willing and ready mind, for the Lord loves cheerfulness.
items.quote: performed cheerefully, with a willing and ready minde: for the Lord loueth cheerefulnesse

items.text: Perform your duties reverently, as to them who bear the image of God.
items.quote: reuerendly as to them which beare the Image of God

items.text: Perform your duties so as not to sin against God in performing them; do not please your parents by disobeying God.
items.quote: so be performed, as in performing them no sinne be committed against God

items.text: Persevere in doing your duty to your parents; do not wax weary in their long need, sickness, or poverty.
items.quote: Constancy must be added to all other vertues

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 68 · Of the prerogatiue of the first-borne sonne.

items.text: Leave to your firstborn son his due inheritance: a double portion or the whole freehold estate, as God and law appoint.
items.quote: God hath so appointed it: he made this to be one of the prerogatiues of the first-borne, to haue a double portion.

items.text: Provide for your other children as well: train them to callings, lay up portions, or settle other estates on them besides the main inheritance.
items.quote: parents ought to be so much the more prouident for their other children, in training them vp to callings, or laying vp portions, or setling other estates vpon them beside the maine inheritance

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 60 · Of parents care to commend their children to some faithfull friends. … Of neglecting to make a Will.

items.text: Set faithful friends in your own place to guide your children for their good.
items.quote: whom parents are to set in their owne place for the good of their children

items.text: Make a will to put your house in order and settle peace among your children.
items.quote: Put thy house in order.

items.text: Leave your estate to your children.
items.quote: leaue their estates to their children

items.text: Give your children direction, exhortation, and blessing when you are departing.
items.quote: no blessing that they will leaue behinde them

items.text: Do not cast off care for your children's future under pretext of God's providence.
items.quote: make the very name thereof a pretext to cast off that care

items.text: Make your will while your understanding is good and with wise counsel, not delayed.
items.quote: The fit time is while his vnderstanding is good, and his memorie perfect

items.text: Do not put off making your will out of a foolish fear that it will hasten death; delay only unsettles your mind.
items.quote: if a mans Will be once made, then he must needs die out of hand

items.text: Be content with the portion your father allots you and keep peace with your siblings over inheritance.
items.quote: make them content with that allowance which he hath set out vnto them

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 5 · Of the extremes contrary to seruants feare of their masters.

items.text: Fear him with a reverent and dutiful fear, not only out of dread of punishment, but so as to seek to please him.
items.quote: so they may auoid that, they care not whither their master be pleased or no.

items.text: Do not despise him for poverty, weakness, age, or low estate, but honor his place and authority as bearing God's image.
items.quote: If I be a master, where is my feare, ô ye that despise my name?

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 66 · Of parents impartiall respect to all their children. … Of parents preferring a dutifull childe before a disobedient childe.

items.text: Have an impartial respect to all your children, and perform duty indifferently and equally to all.
items.quote: Parents ought to haue an impartiall respect to all their children, and performe dutie indifferently and equally to all.

items.text: Punish the rebellious child as a duty, an evidence of love, and a means of doing him good.
items.quote: the punishing of the rebellious childe is a parents dutie; an euidence of loue, and a meanes of doing him good.

items.text: Like grace and goodness in a child, and for its sake love him the more; be alienated from impiety and obstinate rebellion.
items.quote: It is no partialitie to like grace and goodnesse in a childe, and for grace and goodnesse sake to loue his childe so much the more.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 47 · A direction to parents in correcting their children.

items.text: Be sure there is a fault committed before correcting, so there is just cause for it, not after your own pleasure.
items.quote: that they be sure there is a fault committed: that so there be iust cause of correcting

items.text: Make the fault known to the child corrected and apparently convince him thereof, so correction may be for instruction.
items.quote: That the fault be made knowne to the childe corrected: and he apparantly conuinced thereof.

items.text: Especially correct faults you can show to be against God's word, such as swearing, lying, pilfering, as most dangerous and to be purged out.
items.quote: the faults be such especially, as the parents can shew to their children... to be against Gods word; as swearing, lying, pilfring

items.text: Have an eye to God's manner of correcting his children, and in particular of his correcting yourself, as a perfect rule.
items.quote: An eye must be had to Gods manner of correcting his children, and in particular of Gods correcting the parent himselfe.

items.text: Pray for yourself and for your child, lifting up your heart for direction and blessing in correction.
items.quote: Prayer must be made by parents for themselues and for their children... but to lift vp the heart for direction and blessing.

items.text: Give correction in love, with tenderness and compassion, as God corrects his children in love.
items.quote: Correction must be giuen in loue... God correcteth his children in loue: so must parents.

items.text: Give correction in a mild mood, when your affections are well ordered, not in choler, rage, fury; defer correction when passion is moved.
items.quote: Correction must be giuen in a milde moode, when the affections are well ordered, and not distempered with choler, rage, furie.

items.text: Keep due order: correction by word must go before correction by the rod, showing you take no delight in smiting.
items.quote: Due order must be kept. Correction by word must goe before correction by the rod.

items.text: Respect the age and disposition of the child: use lighter correction for the young, tender, or flexible, and more severe for the grown and stubborn.
items.quote: if he be young and tender, the lighter correction must be vsed

items.text: Respect the fault: correct with greater severity sins directly against God, open, notorious, scandalous, known, often committed, or habitual.
items.quote: Due respect must be had to the fault: Sinnes directly against God, open, notorious, scandalous sinnes... are with greater seueritie to be corrected.

items.text: Behold your own faults in correcting your child's, so more compassion will be wrought in you.
items.quote: A parent must behold his owne faults in correcting his childes: so more compassion will be wrought in him.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 23 · Of seruants willingnesse to performe their dutie.

items.text: Serve your master with good will and cheerfulness, as serving the Lord Christ.
items.quote: with good will... willingnesse and cheerefulnesse

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 13 · Of the obiections for putting children forth to nurse.

items.text: Nurse your own child at the breast, if you are able and it is not dangerous; learn the skill needed and do not pretend inability without just cause.
items.quote: conscience ought to moue them to nurse those children, which necessity forceth them to bring forth

items.text: Endure the disturbance of night nursing and help your wife as you are able, pitying her.
items.quote: they must be content to endure some disturbance as well as their wiues

items.text: If your husband forbids you to nurse, use all means to persuade him; do not yourself provide a nurse or send the child away; if he persists, be a patient sufferer.
items.quote: vse all the meanes they can by themselues or others to perswade their husbands to let them performe it

items.text: Do not put your child out to a nurse merely to save money; no gain may dispense with a bounden duty.
items.quote: no gaine may giue a dispensation against a bounden duty

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 33 · Of parents faults contrary to their dutie of training their children vp to a calling.

items.text: Train up your child in a calling, and do not allow him to live in idleness at home.
items.quote: suffer their children to liue like little masters at home, and passe ouer all their youth in idlenesse

items.text: Teach your child in childhood the general and common grounds of all callings.
items.quote: neglect to teach their children in their child-hood the generall and common grounds of all callings

items.text: Bring up your child in lawful and godly callings, not in unwarrantable or idolatrous ones.
items.quote: bring vp their children in vnwarrantable and vnlawfull callings

items.text: Have respect to the fitness of your child for the calling you choose for him.
items.quote: haue no respect at all to the fitnesse of the calling

items.text: Educate your child to the honor of God, not merely for gain.
items.quote: only seeke after the most gainfull trade, and neuer thinke to educate their children most to the honour of God

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 48 · Of parents too much indulgency. … Of parents too much seueritie in correcting their children.

items.text: Correct your children for their faults; do not let indulgence keep you from it.
items.quote: Many so cocker their children, as they will suffer them to run into any misdemeanour, rather then correct them.

items.text: Do not be offended with your husband when he corrects the children; do not hinder him from this duty.
items.quote: Mothers for the most part offend herein, who are so farre from performing this dutie themselues, as they are much offended with their husbands if they doe it.

items.text: Do not correct too severely, in wrath, or for no fault; avoid provoking your children.
items.quote: Nothing more prouoketh then immoderate seuerity.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 10 · Of prouiding things needfull for the childe, so soone as it is borne: and of crueltie contrary thereunto. … Of giuing sucke to children.

items.text: Provide before the birth all things needful for the child's weakness, as Mary wrapped Jesus in swaddling clothes.
items.quote: sufficient prouision of all things needfull for a childe in that weaknesse be before hand prouided.

items.text: Nourish the baby with the milk of your breast, for it is the best food, and do not try to rear the child without suck except in urgent necessity.
items.quote: the milke of the breast is fit for young babes, and with it they are to be nourished.

items.text: Do not abandon your newborn child in public places for others to show mercy; care for it as your own, for even the ostrich is hardened who leaves her eggs.
items.quote: leaue their new-borne children vnder stalls, at mens doores, in Church porches, yea many times in open field.

items.text: Help the mother in the care of the newborn as much as you can, for the main burden lies on her.
items.quote: the care especially lieth vpon the mother: yet so as the father must afford what helpe he can.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 3 · Of the Anabaptists arguments against the authoritie of masters, and subiection of seruants. … Of a seruants feare of his master.

items.text: Honor your master as worthy of all honor.
items.quote: account his master worthy of all honour

items.text: Be subject to your master in all fear.
items.quote: S. Peter commandeth seruants to be subiect in al feare.

items.text: Fear your master with awe of his place and dread of his power.
items.quote: Feare: which is an awfull dread of a master. An awe in regard of his masters place: a dread in regard of his masters power.

items.text: Please your master well in all things.
items.quote: please well in all things

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 15 · Of seruants hearkning to their masters instructions in piety. … Of Seruants faults contrary to obedience in matters of religion.

items.text: Obey your master's instructions in the way of righteousness, hearkening to his teaching of piety.
items.quote: ought to be obedient to their instructions

items.text: Do not refuse to serve a religious master, but willingly place yourself under such a household head.
items.quote: of all masters they will not serue such as are religious

items.text: When called to religious exercises, do not murmur or say you were not hired for this, but join in the household's worship.
items.quote: being called in to any religious exercise, they will be ready to say, I was not hired for this

items.text: Do not be negligent in your work because your master is religious; serve a believing master well, not despising him.
items.quote: They that haue beleeuing masters let them not despise them, but rather doe them seruice

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 64 · Of parents leauing their estate to their children when they die. … Of the inconueniences which improuident parents bring their children vnto after their death.

items.text: Leave your whole estate to your children at your death, after paying debts and discharging works of charity.
items.quote: leaue their whole estate to their children.

items.text: Leave to your children especially the estate you received from your ancestors, for it is their inheritance.
items.quote: That estate especially which parents haue receiued from their progenitors are they most bound to leaue vnto their children.

items.text: Do not sell your ancestral land so as to cut it off from your posterity.
items.quote: a man might not sell his land to cut it off from his posterity.

items.text: Order your manner of living according to your means, living under rather than above them, so that you may reserve an inheritance for your children.
items.quote: cut their coat according to their cloth. Of the two it is much better for parents to liue vnder, then aboue their meanes.

items.text: Do not waste your whole estate in your own lifetime, but preserve it for your children as links in a continued family.
items.quote: Some parents lauish and bezell out all their estate in their owne life time... wronging their children, and depriuing them of their right.

items.text: Do not leave your estate so burdened with debts and bonds that your children become servants to creditors.
items.quote: leaue their estate to their children, but so incumbred with debts, bonds, recognizances, and statutes, as their children were better be without it.

items.text: Do not make present gain by cutting down timber or taking the heart of your land, to the prejudice of your children after you.
items.quote: they wil not forbeare to make any present gaine that they can... as they who cut downe all the timber and wood that they can, and take out all the heart of their land.

items.text: Keep up timely repairs so that your children do not inherit damages that small cost in your lifetime could have prevented.
items.quote: by meere negligence suffer things to goe to decay for want of timely reparations... might haue beene preuented with laying out a few shillings.

items.text: Settle and clear the titles of your estate in your lifetime so that your children are not put to lawsuits over the inheritance.
items.quote: care not in their life time to cleere the titles of those things which they leaue to their children... it oft costs children more in suit of law.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 57 · Of the extremes contrary to a parents prouiding portions for his children. … Of Parents last blessing to their children.

items.text: Provide for your children out of your estate, laying up portions for them, and do not refuse to help them in their calling and marriage when they have need.
items.quote: bestow a groat to helpe them in calling and mariage

items.text: Do not lay your debts as a burden on your eldest son or heir by making him bound for you.
items.quote: vrging their eldest sonne especially who is their heire, to be bound for them

items.text: When you are near death, give wise and wholesome precepts to your children to direct them in their Christian course.
items.quote: commend some wise and wholsome precepts vnto their children, the better to direct them in their Christian course

items.text: Commend your children to God's grace and blessing in faithful prayer, especially as you leave them.
items.quote: commend their owne soules into Gods hand, so commend their children vnto Gods grace and blessing

items.text: Choose wise friends to be as parents to your children after you depart.
items.quote: A wise choise of some friends to be as parents to them

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 17 · Of seruants obedience to reproofe and correction. … Section

items.text: Bear reproof and correction patiently, even if unjust; do not answer again, resist, or seek revenge.
items.quote: Patiently to beare all manner of reproofe and correction.

items.text: Readily amend whatever you are justly reproved or corrected for.
items.quote: Readily to amend that for which they are iustly reproued or corrected.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 36 · Of seruants endeuour to make their iudgement agree with their masters. … Of seruants yeelding to doe such things at their masters command, as they cannot thinke to be most meet.

items.text: Obey your master in all things and please him well in all things.
items.quote: Obey in all things, Please well in all things.

items.text: Labor to bring your judgment to agree with your master's, and think that meet and good which he does.
items.quote: labour to bring their iudgement to the bent of their masters iudgement, and to thinke that meet and good which he doth.

items.text: If you think a command is unfit, humbly give your master reasons; but if he stands on his authority, his word must prevail and you must obey.
items.quote: if their master will not hearken to their reasons, but stand vpon his authoritie, his word must preuaile.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 69 · Of parents partiality towards some children. … Of the causes for which the first-borne may be disinherited.

items.text: Show equal affection to all your children; do not prefer one above the rest.
items.quote: Many parents haue their darling children, to whom so much affection is shewed, as in comparison none is shewed to others.

items.text: Give every child means to maintain life, as you gave life to all.
items.quote: as life is giuen to all children, so meanes of maintaining life should be giuen to all.

items.text: Do not disinherit your first-born without just cause; the inheritance belongs to him by right.
items.quote: they vniustly disinherit their first borne. For the inheritance of right belonging to them, and they not deseruing to be disinherited.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 21 · Of seruing with sincerity. … Of seruing for conscience sake.

items.text: Serve your master with singleness of heart, honestly and uprightly.
items.quote: in singleness of heart, so as all must be performed with an honest and vpright heart

items.text: Whatever you do in your master's service, do it heartily, not half-heartedly.
items.quote: whatsoeuer yee doe, doe it heartily

items.text: Do not serve your master hypocritically with a double heart.
items.quote: when seruants haue a heart, and a heart, making shew-of one heart outwardly, and haue another, euen a cleane contrary heart within them.

items.text: Do not be an eye-servant, diligent only when your master is watching.
items.quote: when seruants are diligent so long as their masters eye is on them

items.text: Serve your master as you would serve Christ, for conscience toward God.
items.quote: as vnto Christ, as the seruants of Christ, doing the will of God, as to the Lord

items.text: Do not serve your master merely for wages or human approval; aim at God's reward.
items.quote: who doe all the seruice which they doe on by-respects

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 1 · A Resolution of the Apostles direction to Seruants. … Of the lawfulnesse of a masters place and power.

items.text: Recognize that your master's authority and your subjection are ordained by God, and yield him reverence and obedience accordingly.
items.quote: God ingenerall ordained degrees of superioritie and inferioritie, of authority and subiection: and in particular gaue to masters the authoritie which they haue, and put seruants in that subiection wherein they are.

items.text: Obey your master with fear and trembling, in singleness of heart, as unto Christ.
items.quote: Seruants be obedient to them that are your Masters according to the flesh, with feare and trembling in singlenesse of your heart, as vnto Christ.

items.text: Serve your master not with eye-service as men-pleasers, but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.
items.quote: Not with eie-seruice, as men-pleasers, but as the seruants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.

items.text: With good will do service, as to the Lord, and not to men, exercising cheerfulness, readiness, diligence, and faithfulness.
items.quote: With good will doing seruice, as to the Lord, and not to men.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 10 · Of seruants obedience. … Of seruants forbearing to doe things without their masters consent.

items.text: Obey your master as your rule and guide in all things that are not against God's will.
items.quote: The will of their master must be their rule and guide (in things which are not against Gods will.)

items.text: Do not go where you wish, but go only when and where your master sends you.
items.quote: Seruants may not goe whither they will.

items.text: Do your master's business, not your own, while you are in his service.
items.quote: They ought not to doe their owne businesse and affaires.

items.text: Do the work your master assigns, not what you prefer.
items.quote: They ought not to doe what businesse they list themselues.

items.text: Do not marry while your covenant of service lasts unless your master consents.
items.quote: If his master haue giuen him a wife: whereby is implied; that if a seruant mary, it must be with his masters consent.

items.text: Do not dispose of your master's goods without his consent, not even for charitable purposes.
items.quote: They ought not to dispose their masters goods at their owne pleasure, no not for charitable vses.

items.text: Do not go away from your master before your agreed term is completed.
items.quote: They may not before their couenanted time be expired goe away from their master.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 24 · Of seruants quicknesse and diligence in their seruice.

items.text: Be quick in your service: take up no more time about one thing than must needs, and be ready to do one thing after another.
items.quote: He that is quicke in his seruice taketh vp no more time about one thing then must needs; but is ready to doe one thing after another.

items.text: Be diligent in your service: hold on, and employ all the labor and pains you can for the well effecting of that which you are to do.
items.quote: imploy all the labour and paines that he can for the well effecting of that which he is to doe

items.text: Do the work your master appoints as the work of God, and do it with all diligence, for cursed is he that does the work of the Lord negligently.
items.quote: The worke which seruants are by their master appointed to doe, is to them the worke of God... Cursed is he that doth the worke of the Lord negligently.

items.text: Do not be idle, lazy, slothful, or sluggish in your master's service; such idleness is plain theft, for your best service is due to him.
items.quote: idlenesse and sloth, the truth is, that it is a plaine theft. For the best seruice that seruants can doe, is due to their master

items.text: Be as diligent in your master's work as if it were your own, for it is not enough to avoid idleness in doing nothing, but you must take heed you are not slothful in doing something.
items.quote: they ought to be as diligent in their masters worke, as if it were their owne

items.text: Do not spend your master's time in prating about state and Church-business, for that time belongs to your particular calling.
items.quote: Much of that time which they should spend about their masters businesse (which is their particular calling) they spend in prating about state, and Church-businesse

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 19 · Of seruants amending that for which they are iustly reproued or corrected. … Of seruing with trembling.

items.text: When justly rebuked or corrected for your faults, repent and amend rather than continue in them.
items.quote: More then patience is required of them that are deseruedly rebuked or corrected for their faults: namely repentance, and amendment.

items.text: Do not go on in your evil ways after rebuke and correction, provoking your master further.
items.quote: Contrary is their disposition, who notwithstanding all rebuke and correction goe on still in their euill and lewd courses

items.text: Serve your master with fear and trembling, showing a servant-like fear in your heart.
items.quote: Let therefore seruants here learne by their manner of performing all their duties, to declare that there is a true seruant-like feare seated in their hearts.

items.text: Be careful and circumspect to avoid your master's displeasure and give him no just occasion of offence.
items.quote: they must so carrie themselues as they prouoke not their master to wrath, but be very carefull and circumspect to auoid his displeasure

items.text: Do not despise your master's authority or say in your heart, 'Who is he that we should serve him?'
items.quote: a proud despising of a masters authority (saying, if not with their mouthes, yet in their heart, as Gaal of Abimelech, who is he that we should serue him?

items.text: Do not be carelessly unafraid of punishment before you feel it, like desperate thieves.
items.quote: a wretched carelessenesse, not fearing any punishment before they feele it

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 7 · Of the vices contrary to a seruants reuerence in speech.

items.text: Speak modestly and quietly before your master, showing respect for his presence.
items.quote: full of prate, and loud in speech before their master, or in the roome next to him

items.text: Do not answer back or insist after your master has shown dislike or commanded you to be silent.
items.quote: Importunity in speaking, and replying againe and againe, though their masters doe not only shew their dislike thereof, but also expresly charge them to speake no more.

items.text: Listen patiently while your master speaks; do not interrupt or turn away before he finishes.
items.quote: either they will interrupt him, or fling away

items.text: Speak when duty requires: answer when bidden, warn your master of harm, clear yourself of false suspicion, and ask for direction when uncertain.
items.quote: though they vnderstand, they will not speake

items.text: Give your master the title of respect due to his place, even if he is poor or lowly.
items.quote: scorne to giue the title Master to him that is set ouer them, because he is a poore and meane man

items.text: Speak humbly as becomes your present place, not proudly because of your birth or parentage.
items.quote: their words are high and lofty against their master, pretending that they are as good as he

items.text: Do not murmur or grumble at every discontent, for harsh words stir up anger.
items.quote: Muttering and murmuring vpon euery occasion of discontent

items.text: Do not interrupt your master when he is seriously occupied or in passion; choose a fitting time to speak.
items.quote: Vnseasonable interruption of their master: speaking to him when he is seriously occupied in some weighty businesse

items.text: Answer promptly when your master calls; do not make him call again and again.
items.quote: suffering him to call, and call againe and againe

items.text: Never lie to your master; answer him truthfully, for he stands in God's place.
items.quote: Flapping their master in the mouth with a lie

items.text: Speak no evil of your master behind his back; cover his weaknesses rather than reveal them.
items.quote: Euill language of their master behinde his backe

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 6 · Of seruants reuerence in speech.

items.text: Refrain from speaking in your master's presence unless you have just cause.
items.quote: By sparing to speake, without iust cause in their masters presence or audience

items.text: Do not reply when you observe your master is unwilling that you speak any more.
items.quote: By forbearing to reply when they obserue their masters vnwilling that they should speake any more

items.text: Attend carefully to what your master says, as Samuel did to God: Speak, for thy servant heareth.
items.quote: by attending to that which their masters shall deliuer to them: for seruants ought to shew such a respect to their masters speaking to them, as Samuel did to God

items.text: Speak to your master only when you have just occasion: when he asks you, or when it is needful for his good.
items.quote: That they haue iust occasion to speake: and that is either when their masters require them to speake ... or when they see it behouefull for their masters that they should speake

items.text: If you know anything profitable for your master, declare it to him even though he has not asked.
items.quote: When they know any thing that may be profitable for their masters, they ought to declare it, though they be not asked

items.text: If your master through ignorance or passion refuses what is good for him, persuade him to do it.
items.quote: When masters through ignorance, passion, or such like cause, refuse to doe that which their seruants know to be good for them, they ought to perswade their masters to doe it

items.text: When you are not fully instructed in what you ought to do, ask your master what is to be done.
items.quote: When seruants are not fully instructed in those things which they ought to doe for their master, they ought to aske of him what is to be done

items.text: When you speak to your master, let your words be reverent: give him reverent titles, and be few, meek, mild, and humble.
items.quote: That seruants giue reuerend titles to their masters ... That their words be few, no more then must needs ... That all their words spoken to their master be meeke, milde and humble

items.text: Choose a fit season to speak to your master, when he is at leisure and his mind is quiet.
items.quote: That they obserue a fit season to speake to their master: as when he is at leasure to heare them ... or when his minde is quiet, not troubled with passion

items.text: Give a ready and present answer when your master asks you.
items.quote: That they giue a ready and present answer to their master

items.text: Never lie to your master; speak the whole truth to him.
items.quote: That all their speeches and answers to their master be true, not daring to tell a lie vnto them

items.text: Speak well of your master behind his back, never evil.
items.quote: speaking good of him, and no euill

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 38 · Of mothers peculiar care in nurturing young children. … Of parents folly in letting goe all their power ouer their children.

items.text: Teach and nurture your children especially while they are young, for you are most with them and your teaching will stick with them.
