items.quote: mothers should teach their children especially while they are young

items.text: Teach your child even while he is tender; do not leave the nurturing only to the mother.
items.quote: his father taught him eue• while he was tender

items.text: See that the mother performs her duty of nurturing the children, for you are governor over child, mother, and all.
items.quote: see that mothers doe theirs also, because he is a gouernour ouer child, mother, and all.

items.text: Do not forsake your mother's teaching.
items.quote: Oft doth Salomon warne children not to forsake their mothers teaching.

items.text: Continue to nurture and admonish your children as long as you remain their parents, even after they are grown.
items.quote: hold on therein, as long as they retaine any gouernment ouer them: yea so long as they remaine to be parents vnto them.

items.text: Keep the reins in your own hands and retain power to curb them; slacken as they grow, but never let go entirely.
items.quote: euer keepe the reines in their owne hands, and retaine a power to curbe their children as they see occasion.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 42 · Of the third motiue, Gods will. … Of the fourth reason, the reward of good seruice.

items.text: Obey your master as unto the Lord, because this is the will of God.
items.quote: God in his word hath plainly made it knowne that it is his pleasure that they who are vnder the authority of masters should obey them

items.text: Obey not only as a matter of civil order but for conscience sake, as to the Lord.
items.quote: so as it is not only a matter of ciuill policy, but also of conscience, to be done for conscience sake

items.text: Remain in subjection even if your master would exempt you, because no creature can dispense with God's will.
items.quote: Masters may let them goe free: but retaining them as seruants, they cannot exempt them from a seruants subiection

items.text: Yield duty conscientiously even if your master is careless in exacting it, because it is God's will.
items.quote: though masters be carelesse in exacting dutie, yet let seruants be conscionable in yeelding duty, because it is Gods will

items.text: Do good service in all your work, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of inheritance.
items.quote: Knowing that whatsoeuer good thing any man doth, the same shall he receiue of the Lord, whether he be bond or free

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 38 · Of seruants forbearing to obey their master against God.

items.text: Obey him in all things lawful, but refuse any command that is against God's word.
items.quote: if masters command their seruants neuer so peremptorily to doe any vnlawfull thing, that is, any thing forbidden by Gods word, they may not yeeld to it.

items.text: If he forbids what God commands, obey God rather than him.
items.quote: if masters forbid their seruants to doe that which God hath commanded them to doe, they must, notwithstanding their masters prohibition, doe it.

items.text: Do not flatter him or consent to his sin out of fear or fawning.
items.quote: So prone are seruants to sooth their masters, as there is no sinne so horrible which at their masters command they will not be ready to doe.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 25 · Of seruants faithfulnesse. … Of seruants carelesnesse ouer their masters goods.

items.text: Show all good faithfulness in the service you owe your master.
items.quote: To shew all good faithfulnesse.

items.text: Keep carefully whatever your master commits to your trust, so that nothing is lost, spoiled, or impaired.
items.quote: Keepe that which is committed to thy trust.

items.text: Endeavor to increase your master's estate and not merely preserve it.
items.quote: They ought further to doe what lieth in them to aduance their masters estate.

items.text: If you see damage or hurt done by others to your master's goods, redress it if you can, or make it known to your master.
items.quote: If seruants espie any dammage or hurt done by others to their masters goods, they must redresse it, if they can, or at least make it knowne to their masters.

items.text: Do not through carelessness or negligence let loss or damage come to your master's goods, whether in field, house, or cattle.
items.quote: Contrary to seruants fidelitie in safe keeping their masters goods committed to their charge is Carelesnesse and negligence in suffering losse and dammage come to their masters.

items.text: Be faithful in every area of your master's life that is committed to you: his goods, business, secrets, fellow servants, children, bedfellow, and person.
items.quote: The Goods, the Businesses and affaires, the Counsels and secrets, the other seruants, the Children, the Bedfellow, the Person of their master or mistresse.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 28 · Of seruants fraud. … Of seruants faithfulnesse in the businesses which they are to dispatch for their masters.

items.text: Do not steal, purloin, or defraud your master in any way, whether by false accounts, concealing prices, or taking bribes.
items.quote: not only open and manifest stealth... but also putting more into the account of expences then hath beene expended

items.text: Do not secretly take what is due to you if your master withholds your wages; leave it to God or the law.
items.quote: A masters sinne is no warrant to make seruants answer sinne with sinne.

items.text: Pay your servant the wages due to him; do not detain them.
items.quote: masters detaine their seruants wages

items.text: Fear God in your service so that your master's business may prosper.
items.quote: that their masters businesse may prosper vnder their hands

items.text: Pray to God for success in your master's business.
items.quote: He called vpon God to prosper his endeuours

items.text: Give thanks for every success God gives in your master's business.
items.quote: He gaue thankes when he saw the Lord begin to prosper that he tooke in hand

items.text: Take all opportunities diligently in your master's business, as if it were your own.
items.quote: He omitted nothing that in the vttermost of his wisdome he conceiued to be behouefull for that matter

items.text: Do not be careless whether your master's business prospers; use holy means and avoid wickedness that hinders God's blessing.
items.quote: they vse those things which doe mainly hinder and keepe away Gods blessing

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 34 · Of seruants faithfulnesse about their masters persons. … Of the meanes to make seruants faithfull.

items.text: Be faithful in giving your master the best help you can in his weakness, sickness, old age, or other distress.
items.quote: seruants therefore must be faithfull in affording them the best helpe that they can.

items.text: Do not leave your master in his time of need, but remain to help him when he is afflicted.
items.quote: Contrary is a seruants vngratefull and inhumane leauing of his master in his time of need

items.text: Do not take occasion from your master's impotence to murder him or betray him to his enemies.
items.quote: take occasion from their masters impotencie to murder him themselues... or to betray him to his enemies

items.text: In all you do for your master, make his case your own, and do for him as you would for yourself.
items.quote: make their masters case their owne, and so doe for him as they would for themselues

items.text: Love your master as yourself, and do to him whatever you would have others do to you.
items.quote: Loue thy neighbour as thy selfe; and whatsoeuer you would that men should doe to you, doe you even so to them.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 26 · Of moderating seruants labour. … Of denying seasonable rest to seruants.

items.text: Do not put them to tasks above their ability that impair their strength, endanger their limbs, or venture their lives.
items.quote: It is contrary hereunto to put seruants to such hard taskes as impaire their strength, endanger their lims, and venture their liues.

items.text: Do not oppress them with too much work, as the Egyptians oppressed the Israelites.
items.quote: or to oppresse them with too much worke, as the Egyptians oppressed the Israelites.

items.text: Provide them things needful and behoveful for the work whereunto they are put.
items.quote: afford their seruants things needfull, and behouefull for that worke whereunto they are put

items.text: Allow them intermission, ease, and rest from labor at seasonable times.
items.quote: Intermission, ease, and rest from labour at seasonable times, is as needfull and requisite, as food and apparell.

items.text: Do not deny them the rest of the night; give them sufficient time for sleep, not making them watch too long or rise too soon.
items.quote: they who make their seruants watch too long at night, and againe, rise too soone in the morning, not affording so much time of rest and sleepe as is needfull

items.text: Do not deny them the rest of the Lord's day, which by divine institution is a day of rest for servants.
items.quote: The other time of rest (being the Sabbath day) is by diuine institution... that thy seruant may rest.

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 8 · Of seruants reuerend behauiour to their masters. … Of the faults of seruants contrary to reuerence in cariage.

items.text: Give your master dutiful and submissive obeisance—bowing or curtseying as befits your sex and place and the custom of the country—when you come to him, go from him, receive a charge, or bring a message.
items.quote: such dutifull and submissiue obeysance and curtesie, as beseemeth their sex and place, and that according to the most vsuall custome of the country

items.text: Stand in your master's presence, showing readiness to perform whatever service he appoints.
items.quote: To stand in his masters presence; which testifieth a readinesse to performe any seruice which his master shall appoint him to doe

items.text: If you are a male servant, uncover your head in your master's presence as a sign of subjection.
items.quote: By vncouering their heads in their masters presence... a signe and token of subiection.

items.text: Compose your countenance and body soberly in your master's presence, showing reverent respect for him.
items.quote: By sobrietie and modestie both in countenance, and in the whole disposition of bodie, especially when seruants are in their masters presence

items.text: Wear apparel that declares you to be a servant under your master, distinguishing you from superiors.
items.quote: The apparell also which seruants weare must be so fashioned and ordered, as it may declare them to be seruants, and vnder their masters

items.text: Do not be rude or fail to show obeisance; learn how to give it, lest you dishonor your parents and upbringing.
items.quote: Some through rudenesse, and want of good bringing vp, come to their masters, and goe from them, as to and from their fellowes: no testimonie of reuerence by any obeysance

items.text: Do not be overly familiar with your master; do not behave as his fellow, but keep reverent distance all day.
items.quote: through too much familiaritie with them, all the day after they will carry themselues fellow-like, scarce vncouering their heads in their masters presence

items.text: Do not wear proud or excessive apparel; do not imitate your master, mistress, or their children, but keep the difference of your station.
items.quote: No distinction ordinarily betwixt a mans children and seruants: nay none betwixt masters and their men, mistresses and their maids.

items.text: Show reverence to your master regardless of his wealth, for God has given him authority as a master, and he bears God's image.
items.quote: God hath giuen as much honour and authoritie to a poore master as to a rich, in that he is a master

items.text: Show reverence in the courts of God and the assembly of God's people, so that the ministry of the word is not evil spoken of.
items.quote: namely, in the courts of God, and assembly of Gods people

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 39 · Of seruants chusing good masters. … Of the second motiue, the place of seruants.

items.text: Choose a master who fears God, and will command nothing contrary to conscience.
items.quote: It is very behouefull that seruants make choice of good masters: at least if it be in their power to chuse.

items.text: Remain with a good master, and do not leave for a worse, if you continue as a servant.
items.quote: It is behouefull that they continue and abide vnder good masters: at least if they continue seruants, and abide vnder any masters.

items.text: Love a faithful master as a father, while respecting his authority.
items.quote: due respect had to his authoritie, must loue him as a father

items.text: Serve your master as you would serve Christ, for he stands in Christ's place.
items.quote: seruants in performing duty to their master performe duty to Christ

items.text: Do not rebel against your master, for by rebelling against him you rebel against Christ.
items.quote: in rebelling against their master they rebell against Christ

items.text: Do not refuse to serve a religious master, nor be restless until you are out of his service.
items.quote: who refuse to serve religious masters, and shun them most of all

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 74 · Of their dutie who are in stead of parents to Orphants. … Of the fraud of Guardians.

items.text: Bring up the orphan as your own child: see them well educated, well placed in a good calling, and give them counsel and oversight.
items.quote: see these Orphants well educated, well placed in some good calling

items.text: See the orphan well married with a suitable match.
items.quote: well maried

items.text: If the orphan is left without means, provide for their necessities; do not let them want or beg.
items.quote: if the Orphants be left destitute of meanes) well prouided for

items.text: Look to your pupil's good education, following the directions given to natural parents.
items.quote: That they looke to their Pupils good education.

items.text: Preserve your pupil's patrimony and inheritance: manage it for their benefit, not your own, and be ready to give a true account.
items.quote: That they preserue their patrimony and inheritance.

items.text: Do not force a marriage upon your ward; only arrange a match fit for them in estate, years, body, and mind, and agreeable to them.
items.quote: such matches put vpon them as they cannot like; yea such as are no way fit for them

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 14 · Of the restraint of masters power: that it reacheth not to their seruants life. … Of masters excesse in correcting seruants.

items.text: Do not take away your servant's life for any fault; your power reaches not so far.
items.quote: His power reacheth not so farre

items.text: Do not dismember your servant; if you smite out an eye or tooth, let him go free as recompense.
items.quote: if vnawares he did smite out an eie or tooth of his seruant, he must make a recompence: which was to let him goe free.

items.text: So correct that you do not cause death; if your servant dies under your hand, you are to be punished.
items.quote: If a seruant died vnder his masters hand when he corrected him, though he intended not wilfully to murder him, that master was to be punished.

items.text: Do not in rage or unmercifully beat your servant so as to endanger life, health, or strength; keep within a set number of stripes.
items.quote: It is beyond a masters power by any correction to impaire life, health, or strength of his seruant

items.text: Do not strike your servant with anything heavy, cragged, hard, or sharp that may wound, bruise, or lame him.
items.quote: strike their seruant with any thing that commeth next to hand, be it heauy, cragged, hard, or sharpe

items.text: Do not put your servant upon desperate attempts for your own quarrel or unjust end, causing his life to be lost.
items.quote: cause them to be made away by putting them vpon some desperate attempt, either to maintaine their owne quarrell, or for some other vniust end

items.text: Do not cause your servant to commit felony, murder, treason, or rebellion, making yourself guilty of his blood.
items.quote: cause their seruants for their sakes to commit felony, murther, treason, rebellion

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 11 · Of a masters wisdome in ordering things indifferent. … Of the power of masters to correct their seruants.

items.text: In commanding things indifferent, have regard to your servant's ability, sex, age, disposition, and conscience, so that what you command is fitting.
items.quote: haue an eie to their seruants ability, sex, age, disposition, conscience, and other like circumstances, that the thing which they command be somewhat agreeable to them

items.text: Do not be too peremptory in pressing your authority and power, especially in doubtful matters against conscience.
items.quote: ought not a master to be too peremptory in pressing his authoritie and power

items.text: When your master commands something not unlawful, do what you can to satisfy him, even if he is peremptory.
items.quote: seruants ought to doe what they can to satisfie their masters command, if he be peremptory in vrging them

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 48 · Of Gods being in heauen, how it is a motiue to prouoke masters well to respect their seruants. … Of Gods impartiall respect of all.

items.text: Give your servant no just cause of complaint.
items.quote: giue no iust cause of complaint to any seruant.

items.text: Show favour to your servant and forbear threatening.
items.quote: shew fauour to thy seruant on earth, and forbeare threatning.

items.text: Deal with your servant as you would have God deal with you.
items.quote: deale with thy seruant, as thou wouldest haue God deale with thee.

items.text: Take notice of your servants' pains, diligence, and faithfulness; do not scorn or neglect them.
items.quote: take notice of our seruants, of their paines, of their diligence, and of their faithfulnesse

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 12 · Of the vnlawfull libertie which seruants take to themselues. … Of seruants hearkning to their masters instructions in matters of their calling.

items.text: Do not go out or absent yourself without your master's knowledge and consent; do not watch for times when he is occupied, away, or in bed.
items.quote: When seruants watch their times to goe whither they list, and their master not know it

items.text: Do your master's business, not your own, and seek not your own profit without his leave; do not use his name to borrow money or get favors.
items.quote: When being bound to their masters seruice, they doe their owne businesse, and seeke their owne profit; and that without their masters leaue

items.text: Do the work assigned you, and do not pick and choose your tasks; do not grumble if you are not placed to your liking.
items.quote: When seruants will chuse their owne worke, and doe that which liketh themselues best, or else doe nothing at all

items.text: Do not marry merely to be freed from your service; keep your covenant of service even if marriage would release you.
items.quote: When seruants, especially maid-seruants, that are bound, doe purposely mary to free themselues

items.text: Do not give away any of your master's goods, even for charity, without his consent; inform him of needs and let him dispose.
items.quote: but priuily without any consent at all, they may not giue away any thing of their masters

items.text: Do not run away from your master; submit even to a froward master, enduring grief for conscience toward God.
items.quote: When vpon discontent they run away from their masters. An Angell from heauen giueth one answer, Submit thy selfe vnder her hands

items.text: Obey your master in all things he commands; even after a day's labor, if he bids you come or go or wait, do it.
items.quote: Though a seruant hath beene all day plowing ... yet when he commeth home, his master commanding him to dresse his supper and wait, he must doe it

items.text: Listen attentively to your master's instruction in your calling, that you may serve him better and later support yourself and others.
items.quote: That by learning a trade or skill in any good calling they may be the better able ... to maintaine themselues

items.text: Instruct your servants in the way of righteousness and in their civil calling, as one having authority over them.
items.quote: his dutie it is to instruct his seruants in the way of righteousnesse, and in that ciuill course of life

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 7 · Of masters commanding power restrained to things lawfull. … Of the sinne of masters in suffering seruants to neglect their dutie.

items.text: Command nothing against God's law; make his law the ground of all you require of your servants.
items.quote: Masters must make Gods law the ground of all those things which they require of their seruants.

items.text: Command your servants to worship God, keep the Sabbath, and be diligent in their calling.
items.quote: These a master by virtue of his authoritie must command his seruants to doe: as to worship God, to sanctifie his Sabbath, to be diligent and conscionable in his calling

items.text: If a servant is papist, separatist, or profane, command and cause him to go to the holy ordinances of God.
items.quote: he ought to command them, and cause them to goe to the holy ordinances of God.

items.text: Do not allow your servants to omit required duties; cause them to do them, or you share their sin.
items.quote: if they cause not their seruants also to doe them, they make themselues accessarie to their seruants sinne.

items.text: Compel your servants to outward religious duties; if you cannot force them, do your utmost endeavor.
items.quote: they may be forced to doe religious and righteous duties: or if a master cannot force these, yet he may and ought to doe his vttermost endeuour

items.text: Obey your master in nothing unlawful.
items.quote: in no vnlawfull thing may he obey.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 46 · Of the subiection vnder which masters are. … Of the equality betwixt masters and seruants in relation to God.

items.text: Rule not over your servant with rigor, but fear God, and do not exact from him anything unlawful or unjust.
items.quote: Thou shalt not rule ouer thy seruant with rigor, but shalt feare thy God.

items.text: Give to your servant what is due, and do not lay more on him than he is able to bear.
items.quote: when you detaine from them any thing that is their due, when you lay more on them then they are able to beare

items.text: Remember that before God you are fellow servants, and treat your servant with kindness and gentleness, not with over-rigorous cruelty.
items.quote: howsoeuer in regard of outward gouernment there be some difference betwixt them and their seruants, yet before God they are as fellow seruants

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 30 · Of seruants faithfulnesse in keeping their masters secrets, and concealing their infirmities. … Of seruants faithfulnesse in helping one another.

items.text: Keep your master's secrets close; reveal them only if they tend to the dishonor of God, the danger of the Commonwealth or Church, or harm to a private person.
items.quote: seruants come to know many of their masters secrets: faithfulnesse therefore requireth to keepe them close.

items.text: Conceal your master's infirmities; do not make them known, for publishing them may impair his credit.
items.quote: a faithfull concealing of masters infirmities

items.text: Be helpful to your fellow servants by good example, good counsel, encouragement, dissuasion from evil, and promoting peace and unity.
items.quote: faithfulnesse requireth that one be helpfull to another in what they may; as by good example, good counsell, incouragement in good courses, disswasion from lewd and wicked practises, peace and vnity

items.text: Do not corrupt your fellow servants by ill example, ill counsel, drawing them into evil, quarrelling, or dissuading them from obedience.
items.quote: by their ill example corrupt their fellowes... or by ill counsell draw one another on to euill

items.text: Do not allure one another to uncleanness; men and maids must not defile one another.
items.quote: to allure one another to vncleannesse, and men and maids to defile one another

items.text: Do not defile your fellow servant, for such sin greatly dishonors your master and his house.
items.quote: it is greatly dishonourable to their master and his house

items.text: Do not marry during your service without your master's consent.
items.quote: it was vnlawfull for seruants during the time of their seruice to marie without their masters consent

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 41 · Of paying seruants their wages. … Of suffering seruants to prouide for themselues.

items.text: Pay them their just wages, according to the covenant.
items.quote: giue them their iust wages

items.text: Allow them wages sufficient for necessary food and clothing.
items.quote: there be a sufficient competency of wages allowed: euen so much at least as may serue to prouide such necessaries as are fit for a seruant

items.text: Give it in due season; do not keep back their hire even one night.
items.quote: That it be giuen in due season. God would not haue the labourers hire be vnpaid one night after it was due.

items.text: Pay them to the full, according to the covenant.
items.quote: That it be paid to the full, according to the couenant

items.text: After sufficient service, allow them to provide for themselves and go free.
items.quote: after sufficient seruice done they suffer their seruants to prouide for themselues

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 23 · Of allowing seruants sufficient food. … Section

items.text: Provide them sufficient, wholesome food in due season, so they may have strength for their work.
items.quote: The food which masters prouide for their seruants must be for qualitie, good and wholesome; for quantitie, sufficient to preserue health and increase strength; for time, giuen in due season.

items.text: Do not stint them below sufficiency; give each one as much as is needful for strength, not merely what they can devour.
items.quote: most meet it is that euery one should haue as much as is needfull for strength

items.text: Do not keep them so long from meat that their health suffers; allow them to interrupt work for necessary meals.
items.quote: not suffering them to interrupt their worke for meat sake

items.text: Provide clothing fit for cold and decent in appearance.
items.quote: all her houshold are clothed with double garments: that is, with such clothing as is fit for cold weather.

items.text: Keep them in order and good compass; see that their apparel is neither base nor garish, but decent for their place.
items.quote: Masters hauing authority ouer their seruants, must keepe them in order and good compasse, and haue respect to decencie in this as in other things.

items.text: Care for them in sickness as in health; nourish and cherish their bodies, not only when they are strong but when they are weak.
items.quote: must be carefull of nourishing, and cherishing them: and that both in health, and sicknesse.

items.text: Do not bring them up too delicately, lest they forget their place and become as sons.
items.quote: bring vp their seruants too delicatly... he shall haue him become his sonne at the length

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 19 · Of masters power to dispose their seruants persons. … Of masters well managing their authoritie.

items.text: When transferring or selling a servant, seek first his good, and put him only to a fitting master who will do him good and not evil.
items.quote: masters must principally respect the good of their seruants: and for that end put them ouer to fit masters, such masters as may doe them good and not euill

items.text: Give your servant the recompense that his place and service justly deserve.
items.quote: All seruants, in that they are seruants, and doe their masters worke, must haue that which of right belongeth to seruants. This is Iustice.

items.text: To a servant who serves with singleness of heart and goodwill, return goodwill and more than ordinary respect, treating him with gentleness and equity.
items.quote: for seruants good will and more then vsuall respect of their masters, let masters returne good will, and more then ordinarie respect to seruants.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 30 · Of masters offence in keeping seruants from the rest of the Lords day. … Of masters care ouer their seruants in sicknesse, and after death.

items.text: Give servants rest from ordinary work on the Lord's day.
items.quote: By keeping seruants at their ordinary worke on that day.

items.text: Do not send servants on errands on the Lord's day.
items.quote: By sending them vp and downe on that day on many errands, as to gather vp debts

items.text: Do not make the Lord's day the greatest day of labor for servants, especially with feasts.
items.quote: By making that the greatest day of paines and labour, namely to such as are in the kitchin, or haue any other businesse about feasts.

items.text: Do not keep servants up late on Saturday nights; allow them sufficient rest for the Lord's day.
items.quote: By keeping them vp too late on Saturday nights: euen till one of the clocke.

items.text: Provide times of moderate recreation for servants to refresh body and mind.
items.quote: it is very meet that seruants should haue some times to refresh themselues

items.text: Provide for a sick servant: spiritual comfort and whatever may give ease and recovery.
items.quote: First spirituall comfort for their soule: then such things as may for the present giue them ease and refreshing, and also... worke a recouery.

items.text: Do not thrust out a sick day-laborer or journeyman without knowing he will be provided for.
items.quote: if he fall sicke in his house, he may not in that case thrust him out of doores, vnlesse he know where he may be wel prouided for.

items.text: If you are poor, make the sick servant's case known to his friends or the church.
items.quote: it is the masters duty, to make the sicke mans case knowne to his friends, or to the Church.

items.text: See that a servant who dies is decently buried in Christian manner.
items.quote: his master must see the last duty in some seemely manner, performed for him, which is Christian buriall.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 44 · Of kindnesse to be shewed to good seruants. … Of vnkinde dealing with good seruants.

items.text: Esteem faithful and good servants as a father esteems his children.
items.quote: Masters must well esteeme of such good seruants: and haue them in high account.

items.text: Take notice of their goodness and kindness, and manifest it by due praise and a good reward.
items.quote: Masters must take notice of the goodnesse, and kindnesse of such seruants: and manifest as much, both by giuing them due praise, and a good reward.

items.text: Do not rashly credit accusations against them, but thoroughly examine the matter; if they slip, pass it over or mildly admonish.
items.quote: If such seruants be accused of any hainous crime, masters must not rashly giue credit thereto, but rather thorowly sift, and examine the matter.

items.text: When their covenanted time expires, do not send them away empty, but help them in marriage or setting up.
items.quote: When such seruants (their couenanted time being expired) depart, their masters must not let them goe away empty: but helpe them in their mariage (as Moses his master did) or in their setting vp.

items.text: Treat your inferiors as you would have your superiors treat you.
items.quote: Thou oughtest so to liue with thy inferiour, as thou wouldest haue thy superiour liue with thee.

heading: Treatise 6 · The sixth Treatise. The Duties of Parents. · Section 71 · Of the dutie of fathers and mothers in law. … Of the faults of parents to their childrens husbands and wiues.

items.text: Treat your child-in-law as your own natural child, seeking their good in every way according to their age and place, except in duties peculiar to natural parents.
items.quote: account their children in law ... as their owne naturall children, and according to the age and place of these children to performe the forenamed duties, and euery way to seeke their good

items.text: Love your stepchildren as your own, for marriage makes you one flesh with their parent.
items.quote: Mariage maketh man and wife one flesh: in which respect they ought to have one minde, and the same affections, as mutually each to other, so ioyntly to the children of each other.

items.text: Do not envy or hinder your stepchildren's prosperity, nor seek to alienate their natural parent's affection from them.
items.quote: enuy at the prosperity of their husbands and wiues children... alienate the naturall parents affection from them

items.text: In disputes between your child and their spouse, judge impartially; do not favor your own child.
items.quote: In all differences they will take part with their owne children, though it be in the worse part, and shew great partiality.

items.text: Give wholesome counsel to your son or daughter and their spouse; do not advise domination, deception, or theft.
items.quote: giue very ill counsell: aduising their sons to keepe their wiues short... priuily to purloine from their husbands.

items.text: If you live with your married child and their spouse, respect their privacy; do not pry or be suspicious, but promote peace.
items.quote: prie into euery thing... shew such suspicion and iealously... cause much discord

items.text: Provide for your stepchild's safety and religious upbringing, as Joseph did for Jesus.
items.quote: Ioseph tooke care to haue his wiues childe circumcised, and presented in the temple... fled from place to place to preserue the childs life

items.text: Guide and support your child-in-law, as Naomi did for Ruth, directing her path and caring for her child.
items.quote: Naomi brought Ruth her sonnes wife into her owne countrey... directed her whither to goe, and what husband to haue, and became a nurse to her childe.

items.text: If widowed, before remarrying, consider the impact on your children and choose a spouse who will be a good stepparent.
items.quote: Let widowers and widowes that haue children seriously thinke of it before hand: and be the more circumspect in taking a second or third husband or wife.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 21 · Of masters endeuouring the saluation of their seruants. … Of masters neglecting to edifie their seruants.

items.text: Seek the spiritual edification of your servants, bearing an impartial respect to all in your house.
items.quote: masters must seeke the spirituall edification of their seruants

items.text: Instruct your servants daily in the principles of religion and all duties of piety.
items.quote: They must daily instruct them in the principles of religion, and all duties of pietie

items.text: Cause your servants to attend the public ministry of the word and worship of God, especially on the Lord's day.
items.quote: Masters must cause their seruants to goe to the publike ministerie of the word, and worship of God

items.text: Take account of your servants' profiting by the public and private means of edification, that you may know whether to give them milk or strong meat.
items.quote: must take an account of their profiting, both by the publike, and also by the priuate meanes of edification

items.text: Add prayer to instruction, and when you see grace in a servant, thank God and pray for its increase.
items.quote: they must to instruction adde prayer

items.text: Afford your servants time for religious exercises, morning and evening, and do not keep them from the public worship of God on the Lord's day.
items.quote: keepe their seruants from the publike worship of God, euen on the Lords day

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 16 · Of masters ordering that correction they giue to their seruants. … Of masters rigour in forcing mariages on seruants: or in separating man and wife.

items.text: In correcting servants, distinguish between age, sex, disposition, and fault; do not be quick to strike those grown in years, but first use rebuke.
items.quote: difference must be put betwixt the age, sex, disposition, and faults of those whom they correct.

items.text: In a joint household, let the master correct men-servants and the mistress maids; but the master may subdue a rebellious maid if the mistress cannot.
items.quote: it is fittest for the master to correct men-seruants, the mistresse maids.

items.text: For servants of an ingenious and willing disposition, pass over many faults that would be corrected in others.
items.quote: If seruants be of an ingenious disposition, willing and forward to doe that which belongeth vnto them, sorry when they haue committed a fault... many things may be passed ouer.

items.text: Measure correction by the greatness of the fault and its circumstances, not by your own passion; the one who knew his master's will shall be beaten with many stripes, but he who knew not with few.
items.quote: Correction must be measured according to the greatnesse of the fault punished, and the circumstances whereby the fault may iustly be aggrauated.

items.text: Do not force a servant to marry against their will; marriage requires the free consent of the parties.
items.quote: No, not without the free consent of the seruants themselues: for mariages must be made with the free consent of the parties that are maried.

items.text: If a servant makes known that necessity requires marriage, respect their chastity and allow them to be married.
items.quote: if seruants shall make it knowne to their master, that necessity requireth they should marie, such respect ought to be had to the chastity euen of seruants... Let them be maried.

items.text: Do not separate married servants from their spouses; the marriage bond gives husband and wife power over one another's bodies that forbids total separation.
items.quote: that power which by the bond of mariage husbands and wiues haue ouer one anothers bodies, suffereth them not to be altogether separated one from another.

items.text: Do not force a servant to marry a woman you have deflowered to cover your shame.
items.quote: when a master hath defloured his maid, to couer his shame he will make one of his seruants marie her.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 36 · Of exercising seruants to a calling. … Of disorder in families through masters negligence.

items.text: Teach your apprentice his trade, that he may have a settled calling and means of maintenance when out of service.
items.quote: They must teach them their trade.

items.text: Tie every servant to a settled work which may be a means of maintenance for him.
items.quote: Other seruants also must be tied to a worke which may be a meanes of maintenance.

items.text: Do not envy your apprentice the mystery of your trade, nor employ him only in errands that profit yourself but not his future.
items.quote: It is contrary hereunto for masters to enuy their prentises the mysterie of their trade: to imploy them from time to time about messages, and errands.

items.text: Do not keep your maids for years in drudgery; teach them housewifery and allow them means and leisure to learn it.
items.quote: keepe their maids many yeares together to drudgery worke, and neuer teach them, nor afford them meanes or leisure to learne points of huswifery.

items.text: Seek your servant's good as well as your own; the end of the master-servant relation is mutual and reciprocal benefit.
items.quote: the maine end of that relation betwixt master and seruant, which is a mutuall and reciprocall good to passe from the one to the other.

items.text: Appoint each servant his own distinct work, that he may know what to do and be accountable for it.
items.quote: That masters appoint to their seruants their proper and peculiar worke, that they may know what to doe, and wherein to exercise themselues.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 3 · Of masters carelesnesse in chusing seruants. … Some of the reasons, directions, & other points there handled, may be here applied. Read it therefore.

items.text: Do not be careless in receiving any into your house: refuse atheists, papists, swearers, and profane persons, lest they infect your household and bring God's curse.
items.quote: ready to receiue any into their house, euen Atheists, Papists, swearers, swaggerers, profane wretches, vncleane persons

items.text: Do not refuse to entertain religious servants on account of contempt for their piety, for by doing so you put away God's blessing from your house.
items.quote: except against such as are religious; thinking it a matter of reproach to entertaine them. By which conceit they oft put away Gods blessing from their house.

items.text: Do not require a great portion of money with an apprentice, clerk, or servant, so as to take only rich men's children; rather exercise charity toward the poor and fit.
items.quote: so stand vpon a great portion of money with a prentise, or a clerke, or other seruant, as they will take none but rich mens children.

items.text: Maintain your authority over your servants, ruling your own house well, so that they are at your command.
items.quote: A master therefore must be able well to rule his owne house: this is a dutie which the Apostle in particular requireth

items.text: Be a pattern of godly behavior in your own conduct, going before your household in fearing the Lord.
items.quote: I and my house will feare the Lord, saith Iosuah: he would not only put them to it, but he also would doe it, he would goe before them.

items.text: Keep your servants in awe and fear, for even children must be kept in subjection, and servants much more.
items.quote: That masters keepe their seruants in awe and feare. Children must be kept in subiection: much more seruants.

items.text: In all your dealings with your servants, command, forbid, and rebuke with all authority.
items.quote: That masters doe the things which they doe in their cariage towards their seruants with authoritie: Command, forbid, rebuke (to vse the Apostles phrase) with all authoritie.

items.text: Guide the house and rule as a mistress, performing the part of a mistress therein.
items.quote: Women also who by vertue of their places are mistresses, are commanded to guide the house, or to rule, and performe the part of a mistresse therein.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 39 · Of masters ouerseeing the wayes of their seruants. … Of prouoking seruants to their dutie both by faire and foule meanes.

items.text: Oversee your servants: have an eye upon them to see how they spend their time and dispatch the business committed to them.
items.quote: masters vse inspection ouer their seruants, and haue an eye vpon their seruants, to see how they spend their time, and dispatch the businesse committed to them.

items.text: Be present with your servants and, as a good example, go before them in labor.
items.quote: If a masters place will beare it, it is behouefull that he be present with his seruants, and as a good president goe before them.

items.text: Use fair means—exhortation, admonition, persuasion, promises of reward—to provoke your servants to be diligent and faithful.
items.quote: masters vse what meanes they can to prouoke and stirre vp their seruants to be diligent and faithfull: as in the first place, exhortation, admonition, perswasion, promises of reward

items.text: If fair means prevail not, rebuke, threaten, and correct them.
items.quote: if faire meanes preuaile not, then they may and ought to rebuke, threaten, and correct their seruants.

items.text: If a servant is impudent in sinning and neither fair nor foul means reclaim him, thrust him out of doors.
items.quote: if seruants be impudent in sinning, and neither faire nor foule meanes will reclaime them, they must then be thrust out of doores.

items.text: Do not thrust a servant out for every small offence; first use instruction, persuasion, admonition, rebuke, and threatening.
items.quote: No instruction, perswasion, admonition, rebuke, threatning is vsed by many when their seruants haue offended, but this thunderbolt cast at them, be gone, get you out of doores.

items.text: Be diligent and faithful in the business your master commits to you, not slack or deceitful.
items.quote: The conceit which the euill seruant had that his master delayed his comming, and so could not see what he did, made him so vnfaithfull as he was.

items.text: As mistress, rise early, give a portion to your maids, and work willingly with your hands.
items.quote: It is recorded of the good mistresse, that shee riseth and giueth a portion to her maids: shee is with them her selfe; shee worketh willingly with her hands.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 2 · Of the heads of Masters duties. … Of masters choosing good seruants.

items.text: Choose servants with an eye to the good of your household and through it the good of church and commonwealth.
items.quote: Thus will masters shew that they seeke, and aime at the good of their family: yea and in their family at the good of Church and common-wealth.

items.text: Carefully inquire after and choose servants who fear God.
items.quote: Mine eies shall be vpon the faithfull of the land, that they may dwell with me: he that walketh in a perfect way he shall serue me.

items.text: Forbear threatening your servants.
items.quote: And yee Masters doe the same things vnto them: forbearing threatning

items.text: Do the same things to them: treat your servants with justice and equity.
items.quote: doe the same things: but more particularly in another place referred to these two branches 1. Iustice. 2. Equity.

items.text: Make trial of a servant's fitness before committing to long service.
items.quote: Make some triall of their fitnesse to that calling, worke and seruice whereunto thou shalt put them.

items.text: Prefer for your service those of mean and poor estate who have no other means of support.
items.quote: Take such especially as are of meane and poore estate, and know not how to maintaine themselues but by seruice.

items.text: If choosing a young servant, consider how he has been educated from infancy, for good education is a means God has blessed.
items.quote: If they be young, see how they haue beene from their infancy educated. Great is the benefit of good education.

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 5 · Of masters making their authoritie to be despised. … Of masters too great rigour.

items.text: Do nothing secretly without your husband’s consent; do not conspire with servants to go out, take goods, or gossip behind his back.
items.quote: conspiring with their seruants to goe abroad, take away goods, gossip, and doe such other like things priuily without their husbands consent

items.text: Carry yourself with such dignity before your servant that he cannot call you a son of Belial; keep yourself from drunkenness, uncleanness, and lewd company.
items.quote: When masters carrie themselues basely and abiectly before their seruants: being light in their behauiour, foolish in their cariage, giuen to drunkennesse, vncleannesse, lewd companie

items.text: Rule your servant with the authority God gave you; command what is needful, and do not entreat him as an equal.
items.quote: intreating and praying their seruants to doe such things as they ought to command

items.text: Do not make your servant your companion in play, drink, or revelry, for such familiarity makes him presume above you.
items.quote: suffer their seruants to be their companions, playing, drinking, reuelling with them

items.text: Keep yourself only for your spouse; do not give a servant power over your body, for that would cause your spouse to be despised.
items.quote: giue their seruants power ouer their owne bodie, doe make both themselues, and their true lawfull bedfellow to be despised

items.text: Do not let your servant rule over you or draw you into unjust or unlawful deeds; keep your place and your integrity.
items.quote: When masters are ouer-ruled by their seruants to doe any vniust or vnlawfull thing

items.text: Do not terrify your servant with continual frowning and fiery looks; give him a good countenance.
items.quote: Many masters by their continuall frowning browes, and fiery eies, doe much terrifie their seruants

items.text: Speak not reviling words to your servant; do not call him fool, for that endangers hell fire.
items.quote: if they be moued neuer so little, cast vpon them all the reproachfull names that they can call to minde

items.text: Strike not your servant in fury on every occasion; remember you are a man like him.
items.quote: when masters are too frequent, and too furious strikers: striking their seruants on euery occasion, not caring how they strike

items.text: So carry yourself that your servant may reverence you rather than dread you.
items.quote: Masters ought so to carrie themselues as their seruants may rather reuerence, then dread them

heading: Treatise 7 · The seuenth Treatise. Duties of Seruants. · Section 32 · Of seruants faithfulnesse about their masters children. … Of seruants faithfulnesse in regard of their masters, or mistresses bed-fellow.

items.text: Tend your master's children tenderly and well while they are young, and keep them clean.
items.quote: to be tender ouer them, and well to tend them: maids especially neatly to handle and looke to them, and cleanly to bring them vp

items.text: Use wholesome speech in their hearing and teach them good things.
items.quote: to vse in their hearing such speech as may minister grace to them, and to teach them good things

items.text: As they grow older, show them reverent respect and esteem them as your betters because they are your master's children.
items.quote: when they grow to some ripenesse of yeares, to beare a reuerend respect to them, and esteeme them their betters because they are their masters children

items.text: Do not be harsh or rude to your master's children when their parents are out of sight.
items.quote: Some in their cariage are very hoggish and churlish to their masters children when their parents are out of sight

items.text: Do not take from your master's children or defraud them of their allowance.
items.quote: Others get from their masters children what they can: and depriue them of their allowance, turning it to their owne gaine

items.text: Do not corrupt your master's children with filthy or unclean speech, teaching them to swear, blaspheme, or use vile language.
items.quote: Others exceedingly corrupt their masters children with their filthy and corrupt communication: teaching them to sweare, blaspheme, and vse all manner of vncleane speeches

items.text: Do not allure your master's children to stage-plays, dice-houses, or other riotous places, nor draw them into overspending.
items.quote: Others allure them to stage-plaies, to dice-houses, and other like places... and draw them to spend in riot such allowance as their parents allow them

items.text: Do not entice or seduce your master's children into sexual uncleanness.
items.quote: Others inueagle their affections: and oft draw them to folly and vncleannesse

items.text: Do not draw your master's children into secret engagement or marriage without their parents' consent.
items.quote: draw them on to be contracted, yea and maried to them often times, and that priuily without consent of their parents

items.text: Refuse to be a party to any deceit between your master and mistress, such as secretly conveying goods for one against the other.
items.quote: If a master should moue his maid priuily to take away iewels, plate, mony, linnen... the seruant ought not to yeeld

items.text: Refuse utterly any solicitation to commit lewdness with your master or mistress, for conscience toward God and faithfulness to them.
items.quote: If a master should allure his maid to commit folly with him, or a mistresse her man... should make them vtterly to refuse it

items.text: Inform one spouse of the other's dangerous sin when it threatens the ruin of the family.
items.quote: seruants faithfulnesse in making knowne to their master the sinne of his wife, and to their mistresse the sinne of her husband, especially if it be such a sinne as may tend to the ruine of the familie

heading: Treatise 8 · The eighth Treatise. Duties of Masters. · Section 33 · Of neglect of seruants in sicknesse: and when they are dead. … Of well imploying seruants.

items.text: Care for your servant when he is sick: keep him in your house and give him what he needs; do not put him out or leave him succorless.
items.quote: when they obserue their seruants begin to be sicke, will put them out of their houses, and leaue them to shift for themselues

items.text: Bear the cost of your sick servant's care; do not make him pay for it or cut his wages.
items.quote: they will afford them things needfull, but all at the poore seruants cost: and if those seruants haue not present money, they will cut it off their wages

items.text: Speak comfortably to your sick servant; do not murmur or complain, lest you grieve him more than his sickness.
items.quote: doe so mutter at their seruants, and fling out such discontented speeches

items.text: Care for your sick servant's soul: give him a word of comfort yourself or send for a minister to do it.
items.quote: haue no respect at all to the spirituall comfort of their soules, they neither giue them a word of comfort themselues, nor send for minister

items.text: If your servant dies, afford him a winding sheet and see that he is buried; do not leave him to be buried for his clothes.
items.quote: if their seruants die, will scarce afford them a winding sheet, but say, let any one that will, burie them for their clothes

items.text: Have a care for your servant's estate, and endeavor that after his service he may live of himself and do good to others.
items.quote: to endeuour and prouide that they may liue of themselues, and doe good to others

items.text: Accustom your servant to painstaking labor and exercise him in a useful calling.
items.quote: masters accustome their seruants to paines... exercise them in some vsefull calling

items.text: Give your servant sufficient wages for his service.
items.quote: giue them sufficient wages

items.text: After sufficient service, allow your servant to provide for himself.
items.quote: after sufficient seruice they suffer them to prouide for themselues

items.text: Keep your servant always employed in some business; do not suffer him to be idle.
items.quote: keepe their seruants exercised and imployed about some businesse

items.text: Do not harbor or feed a servant who refuses to work; if he will not work, he should not eat.
items.quote: if any man would not worke, neither should he eat

heading: Treatise 3 · The third Treatise. Of wiues particular duties. · Section 64 · Of a wiues labouring to bring her iudgement to the bent of her husbands. … Of wiues making their owne will their law.

items.text: Labor to bring her judgment and will to her husband's; when her judgment differs, suspect her own error and do not be peremptory in contradicting his opinion.
items.quote: A wife must labour to bring her iudgement and will to her husbands.

items.text: Yield in practice to what her husband requires in things indifferent, even if she cannot bring her judgment to think it meet, for her subjection is most manifested in such cases.
items.quote: Though in her iudgement she cannot thinke that most meet which her husband requireth, yet she must yeeld to it in practise.

items.text: Learn from her husband in silence with all subjection, not usurping authority over the man.
items.quote: learne in silence with all subiection

items.text: Do not make her own will her law; when her judgment or will differs from her husband's, she must still subject herself, not using the difference as warrant to refuse subjection.
items.quote: when wiues will no further be subiect, then their owne iudgments, wils and affections concurre with their husbands

items.text: Hearken to her when she speaks with modesty, humility, and reverence, and consider her reasons, as the husband of the Shunemite did.
items.quote: he ought to hearken vnto her, as the husband of the Shunemite did
